TITLE: ­­­ERC Starting Grant – Discrete Groups and Geometric Structures (DiGGeS project)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Principal Investigator : Fanny KASSEL

Duration: 1 year with a possible renewal for a second year

Description

Applications are invited for a CNRS postdoctoral position in mathematics at IHES, beginning September 2021, to be funded by the ERC Starting Grant « Discrete Groups and Geometric Structures ».

We are looking for a candidate with a strong research potential, interested in investigating discrete subgroups of Lie groups acting on various geometric spaces. Particular attention will be paid to candidates who already have some experience working on one of the following topics: discrete subgroups of Lie groups, Teichmüller or Higher Teichmüller theory, dynamics on character varieties, geometric structures on manifolds (hyperbolic geometry, convex projective geometry, Lorentzian or more generally pseudo-Riemannian geometry, etc.). ­

Contract details:

The postdoctoral researcher will be part of Laboratoire Alexander Grothendieck — a CNRS research unit at IHES. The IHES provides excellent research conditions, in a quiet environment inside the very active Paris region. The postdoctoral researcher will have access to funding for travel and visitors. In addition to a monthly gross salary of approx. 2,590 euros, he/she will benefit from family housing in a furnished apartment at the IHES residence, as well as access to the IHES cafeteria Monday through Friday.

Applications should be submitted online and include the duly completed application form, a CV, a list of publications, a research statement describing both past research and future research plans (max. 5 pages), as well as 2 or 3 letters of recommendation.

Next call for applications: Fall 2021

Contact

postdoc-application@ihes.fr­­

TITLE: WCSJ 2027 Travel Fellowship: Fully Funded Support for Science Journalists to Attend the World Conference of Science Journalists in London

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the WCSJ 2027 Travel Fellowship, a major international funding opportunity designed to help science journalists, media professionals, journalism students, and eligible researchers or educators attend the World Conference of Science Journalists 2027 in London, United Kingdom.

The World Conference of Science Journalists 2027, widely known as WCSJ 2027, will bring together the global science journalism community in London in September 2027 under the theme:

“Strengthening science journalism through global networks.”

The conference is hosted by the Association of British Science Writers (ABSW) and the World Federation of Science Journalists (WFSJ) and will provide a global platform for journalists and communicators to exchange ideas, discuss emerging challenges, strengthen professional networks, and examine the future of science journalism.

The Travel Fellowship is specifically intended for people who would otherwise struggle to attend because they have limited access to financial support through their employer, organization, institution, or country.

Successful applicants may receive support for:

International or domestic travel to and from London

UK visa application costs

Limited local transport connected to the conference

Up to six nights of accommodation

Full conference registration

Refreshments during the conference

Lunches provided through the official conference programme

The fellowship does not provide a per diem.

Applications must be submitted through the official online application form by:

23 October 2026 at 23:59 BST

The application process is competitive and international. Applicants are assessed on professional merit, commitment to science journalism, motivation, potential contribution to WCSJ 2027, plans for sharing knowledge afterward, quality of previous journalistic work, and financial need.

About the World Conference of Science Journalists 2027

The World Conference of Science Journalists 2027 is one of the most important international gatherings for professionals working at the intersection of journalism, science, health, climate, technology, research, engineering, and public communication.

The event will take place in:

London, United Kingdom

The main conference is announced for:

6–9 September 2027

However, the Travel Fellowship eligibility information asks applicants to be available for the entire fellowship-related conference period from 6–10 September 2027.

Applicants should therefore plan to remain available through 10 September and follow the final schedule provided by WCSJ2027 organizers.

The conference theme is:

Strengthening science journalism through global networks

This theme reflects the increasing importance of international cooperation in a profession facing rapid technological, political, economic, and institutional change.

Science journalists today operate in an environment shaped by:

Misinformation and disinformation

Artificial intelligence

Changing media business models

Declining newsroom resources

Climate change

Public-health emergencies

Scientific uncertainty

Political polarization

New digital platforms

Trust in science

Unequal access to reliable scientific information

WCSJ 2027 is intended to provide a space where journalists and related professionals can collectively discuss these challenges and strengthen networks capable of supporting high-quality, independent science journalism.

About the WCSJ 2027 Travel Fellowship

The Travel Fellowship was created to broaden access to WCSJ 2027.

It recognizes that many excellent journalists, journalism students, and media professionals cannot attend major international conferences because their organizations or institutions do not have sufficient travel budgets.

This can particularly affect professionals working in:

Low-income countries

Lower-middle-income countries

Small independent media organizations

Freelance journalism

Underfunded newsrooms

Universities with limited travel funding

Emerging science journalism communities

The Fellowship therefore aims to increase:

International participation

Diversity

Geographic representation

Professional access

Inclusion of people with limited funding opportunities

It is not restricted only to people whose job title is “science journalist.”

Applicants may qualify if journalism forms a meaningful part of their professional or academic work.

What the WCSJ 2027 Travel Fellowship Covers

Successful applicants receive a financial support package intended to make conference participation possible.

1. Travel to and From London

Approved travel may include transportation such as:

Plane

Train

Coach

Bus

WCSJ2027 Ltd will arrange and pay for approved travel directly.

Applicants should not assume they will simply receive a lump-sum travel payment.

The organizers will generally book approved transport and accommodation on behalf of successful fellows.

2. Visa Application Costs

The fellowship can support the cost of applying for a:

UK Standard Visitor visa

where one is required.

Applicants should check their visa requirements before applying.

They are specifically advised to use official UK government resources to determine whether they need a visa.

Applicants who require a visa should also consider the processing time involved and ensure that they can meet all required documentation and travel conditions.

3. Limited Local Transport

The Travel Fellowship may support local transport associated with attending the conference.

Examples may include transfers between:

Airport and conference-related accommodation

Railway station and accommodation

Bus station and accommodation

Main conference venue

Workshop venues

Official conference evening events where applicable

However, general local transportation in London that is unrelated to official conference activities is not automatically covered.

4. Accommodation

The fellowship includes:

Up to six nights of accommodation

Accommodation is expected to be booked directly by WCSJ2027 Ltd.

Applicants should not assume they can independently book additional hotel nights and request reimbursement.

Extra nights outside the approved fellowship period are not covered.

5. Full Conference Registration

Successful Travel Fellows receive:

Full WCSJ 2027 conference registration

This provides access to the official conference programme and professional activities.

6. Refreshments and Lunches

The fellowship includes:

Refreshments during the official conference programme

Lunches provided through the conference programme

However, meals outside the official conference schedule are not generally covered.

What the Fellowship Does Not Cover

Applicants should carefully understand the costs that remain their own responsibility.

The Travel Fellowship does not cover:

General local transport in London unrelated to official venues or activities

Local transport in the applicant’s home country

Travel undertaken to obtain or renew a passport

Travel undertaken to apply for a visa

Additional hotel nights not booked by WCSJ2027

Charges added personally to a hotel room

Meals outside the official conference programme

Personal expenses

Travel insurance

Health expenses

Per diem payments

This distinction is important when preparing the funding statement.

Applicants should think realistically about whether they can cover expenses that fall outside the fellowship package.

Who Can Apply?

The fellowship is open to several categories of applicants.

1. Science Journalists and Other Media Professionals

Journalists who cover science or science-related subjects are eligible.

Relevant areas include:

Science

Engineering

Climate

Health

Environment

Medicine

Technology

Research

Related scientific fields

Importantly, science journalism does not have to be the applicant’s primary profession or full-time beat.

A journalist who regularly covers health, climate, engineering, science policy, or other scientific subjects as part of a broader reporting role may qualify.

Eligible professionals may include:

Staff journalists

Freelance journalists

Part-time journalists

Full-time journalists

Print journalists

Online journalists

Broadcast journalists

Podcast journalists

Multimedia journalists

Producers

Editors

Other media professionals with a journalism track record

2. Journalism and Related Students

Students may also apply.

Relevant fields include:

Science journalism

Journalism

Media studies

Science communication

Related disciplines

Students must:

Be of legal age in their home country

Be able to travel independently

Students should provide journalistic work where possible.

If they do not have enough published work, supervised long-form coursework may be accepted under certain conditions.

3. Researchers and Educators With Journalism Experience

Researchers and educators working in fields such as:

Journalism

Media studies

Science communication

may also qualify.

However, they must demonstrate a proven track record in journalism.

A researcher or lecturer who works only in academic research, teaching, science communication, or public relations and has no professional journalistic involvement is not eligible.

This distinction is central to the fellowship.

Who Is Not Eligible?

Applicants are not eligible if they work exclusively in areas such as:

Public relations

Science communication

Research

Teaching

without a demonstrated professional involvement in journalism.

In other words, a person can be a science communicator, researcher, teacher, or academic and still qualify, but they must show that journalism is genuinely part of their work.

Applicants should be able to provide published journalistic work or, where applicable for students, acceptable supervised coursework.

No Minimum Professional Experience Requirement

There is:

No minimum number of years of professional experience

Applicants may therefore include both relatively early-career professionals and experienced journalists.

The application asks about years of experience primarily for contextual and statistical purposes rather than imposing a minimum threshold.

Previous Conference Attendance

Applicants who have attended the World Conference of Science Journalists before may still apply.

However, previous attendance may be used as a tie-breaker where candidates receive otherwise similar scores.

Similarly, applicants who previously received travel fellowship support may still apply, although that previous support may also be considered in a tie-breaking situation.

Geographic Eligibility

There are:

No formal geographic quotas

The programme seeks a globally diverse and internationally representative cohort.

Applicants may therefore potentially come from any country if they meet the professional and application requirements.

However, geographic background can influence the administrative review because WCSJ2027 wants to increase access for professionals with limited funding opportunities.

Applicants’ countries of residence will be considered using the World Bank country income classifications in effect on the application deadline.

Applicants normally based in countries classified as:

Low-income

Lower-middle-income

will receive additional consideration.

This does not mean applicants from upper-middle-income or high-income countries are automatically excluded.

Financial need and access to institutional support remain important considerations.

The Importance of Financial Need

Financial need is a central component of the Travel Fellowship.

Applicants will be asked to explain:

What funding is already available to them

Whether their employer can contribute

Whether their institution can contribute

Whether another grant supports them

Why additional WCSJ2027 funding is necessary

Whether they would be unable to attend without fellowship support

Applicants should be transparent.

Having access to some partial funding does not necessarily disqualify an applicant.

Candidates can explain what resources they already have and what gap remains.

Passport Requirements

Before applying, candidates should ensure that they:

Already hold a passport valid until at least the end of September 2027, or

Have already applied for a new or renewed passport and can provide evidence of that application

Applicants should not wait until selection to begin thinking about travel documents.

The fellowship will not pay for travel undertaken specifically to request or obtain a passport.

UK Visa Requirements

Applicants should determine whether they need a UK Standard Visitor visa.

Visa eligibility and requirements vary by nationality.

The programme directs candidates to official UK government sources.

Applicants who require a visa should make sure they can satisfy requirements in time for the September 2027 conference.

The fellowship may cover approved visa application costs but does not cover travel undertaken to attend a visa appointment.

English Language Requirement

The conference language is:

English

Applicants do not need to be native speakers.

They should, however, be able to:

Understand the main points of presentations

Participate in professional discussions

Communicate with other attendees

Benefit from conference sessions

The application itself must also be completed in English.

Applicants’ English is not expected to be perfect.

The organizers specifically emphasize that professional merit and content are more important than native-level English fluency.

Application Materials

Applicants will need to submit several pieces of professional and supporting information.

1. Current Professional Information

Applicants will provide details including:

Current employer

Institution

Professional affiliation

Current position

Professional role

Years of professional experience

This information helps reviewers understand the applicant’s professional context.

2. CV or Résumé

Applicants must submit a:

Maximum two-page CV or résumé

The document should focus on information most relevant to:

Journalism

Science reporting

Media work

Professional development

Science communication where connected to journalism

Awards

Training

Professional associations

Relevant publications or projects

Because the limit is only two pages, applicants should prioritize carefully.

3. Professional Biography

Applicants must provide a professional biography.

This should present a concise overview of the candidate’s:

Work

Areas of expertise

Professional interests

Journalism background

Geographic or thematic focus

The biography must be written in English.

4. Published Work Examples

Applicants will provide examples of professional work from the:

Past two years

Accepted work may include:

Written journalism

Audio journalism

Video journalism

Multimedia work

The quality of these examples is an important selection criterion.

Applicants should therefore choose pieces that best demonstrate:

Accuracy

Independence

Critical thinking

Reporting ability

Quality of storytelling

Scientific understanding

Public relevance

Three Work Examples and Quality Assessment

The selection criteria state that the quality of professional work is assessed primarily through the:

Three work examples provided

Applicants should therefore treat these selections strategically.

Choose work that demonstrates your strongest journalism rather than simply the most recent pieces.

Work in Languages Other Than English

Applicants may submit journalistic work originally published in another language.

They should provide:

The original work

An English translation or transcript

A link to the original publication where possible

AI-assisted translation is allowed.

However, the translation must remain faithful to the original work.

The original should also be provided so multilingual reviewers can assess it where possible.

English proficiency will not be used to downgrade the professional quality of work originally created in another language.

Accepted File Formats

Professional work may be supplied in formats such as:

PDF

MP3

MP4

JPEG

PNG

Applicants should also provide links to original publications whenever possible.

Co-Authored Work

Co-authored or collaboratively produced work may be submitted.

However, applicants should:

Be clearly identified as an author, or

Clearly explain their contribution

This enables reviewers to assess the candidate’s individual professional contribution.

Unpublished Work

Media professionals generally cannot submit unpublished work as professional work examples.

Students are treated somewhat differently.

Students should submit published work whenever possible, including content from:

University newspapers

Student radio

Blogs

Other published student media

If a student cannot provide enough published work, supervised long-form coursework may be submitted, provided it is accompanied by confirmation from the teacher who supervised it.

Supporting Letter

Applicants must provide a supporting letter from an appropriate professional or institutional source.

This may come from:

Employer

Editor

Educational institution

Relevant professional association

The supporting letter must be:

Written in English, or

Accompanied by an English translation

If translated, the translation should be approved by the original author.

The person providing the letter should also read the WCSJ2027 Travel Fellowship Privacy Notice because their personal and professional information may be processed during the application review.

Professional Questions in the Application

Applicants must answer several substantive questions.

These answers are a critical part of the selection process.

Why Do You Want to Attend WCSJ2027?

Applicants should explain specifically why this conference matters to their professional development.

Avoid generic answers such as:

“I want to network and learn new things.”

A stronger response should connect the WCSJ programme and international community to the applicant’s real professional goals.

What Do You Hope to Learn?

Applicants should identify concrete skills, knowledge, or professional insights they hope to gain.

Potential areas may include:

Reporting methods

Investigative techniques

Covering emerging technologies

Climate reporting

Health journalism

Scientific misinformation

Data journalism

Audience engagement

Editorial innovation

The best answer will be specific to the applicant.

How Will Attendance Benefit Your Professional Work?

Applicants should explain how knowledge gained at WCSJ2027 could improve:

Reporting

Editing

Teaching

Professional networks

Newsroom practices

Coverage quality

Professional leadership

The reviewers are looking for evidence that the fellowship will have an impact beyond a single international trip.

What Will You Contribute?

The conference seeks participants who contribute to the community rather than only receive benefits.

Applicants should consider what they bring through:

Regional expertise

Professional experience

Language skills

Specialized reporting

Knowledge of local media environments

Training experience

Community leadership

Underrepresented perspectives

How Will You Share What You Learn?

Applicants need to explain how conference knowledge will be shared afterward.

Possible approaches could include:

Training colleagues

Writing articles

Hosting newsroom sessions

Organizing workshops

Sharing resources through professional associations

Mentoring younger journalists

Publishing conference reflections

Building local networks

The strongest plans will be realistic and directly connected to existing professional communities.

Funding Statement

Applicants must provide a funding statement explaining:

Current available support

Funding gaps

Why additional financial support is required

This is central to assessing need.

Reviewers handling professional merit will not necessarily have access to this financial information.

Selection Process

Applications undergo a:

Two-stage assessment

Stage 1: Professional Review

Professional reviewers assess areas including:

Quality of journalism

Professional experience

Motivation

Commitment to science journalism

Potential contribution to WCSJ2027

Professional-development potential

Stage 2: Administrative and Eligibility Review

Authorized WCSJ2027 Travel Fellowship administrators assess:

Eligibility

Administrative completeness

Financial need

Programme objectives

Overall geographic and professional composition of the cohort

This process helps the organizers balance professional merit with the fellowship’s goal of broadening access.

Selection Criteria

Applications are evaluated against several published criteria.

Commitment to Science Journalism

Applicants should demonstrate engagement with:

Accurate journalism

Fair journalism

Critical journalism

Independent journalism

This can be shown through reporting, editorial work, professional activities, or broader contributions to science journalism.

Professional Development and Community Engagement

The reviewers will consider involvement in activities such as:

Professional associations

Journalist networks

Training

Teaching

Mentoring

Science journalism communities

Participation is not necessarily limited to formal organizations.

Motivation

Applicants should explain convincingly why WCSJ2027 specifically matters to their career.

Reviewers are looking for a well-expressed and engaging motivation rather than generic conference interest.

Potential Benefit and Contribution

The application should demonstrate both:

What the applicant will gain

What the applicant will contribute

This reciprocal approach is central to the fellowship.

Sharing the Benefits

Applicants should have a credible plan to extend the impact of their participation to others.

Reviewers will consider how knowledge might reach:

Colleagues

Professional networks

Students

Audiences

Regional journalism communities

Quality of Professional Work

Professional quality is assessed primarily through the submitted work examples.

Applicants should select their strongest work carefully.

Financial Need

The programme specifically exists for candidates who would otherwise have difficulty attending.

Reviewers will therefore consider financial circumstances as an essential part of final funding decisions.

Diversity and International Representation

WCSJ2027 seeks a cohort that is:

Diverse

International

Professionally varied

Geographically representative

No geographic quotas are used.

However, geographic representation and limited funding opportunities may influence final cohort composition.

Privacy and Fair Assessment

Applicants must read the official WCSJ2027 Travel Fellowship Privacy Notice before submitting.

The notice explains:

How personal data will be used

Applicant privacy rights

Data-processing safeguards

Selection procedures

Reviewers are also subject to an official agreement covering:

Confidentiality

Conflict of interest

Fair assessment

Professional reviewers receive only the information required to assess merit.

They do not receive access to information such as:

Passport details

Contact information

Funding statements

This separation is intended to support impartial assessment.

Online Application Only

Applications must be submitted through the official online form,

The organizers also provide an offline downloadable version of the form.

However, the offline document is only intended to help applicants prepare responses.

It cannot be submitted as the final application.

Saving and Returning to Your Application

The application takes approximately:

30 minutes

Applicants do not necessarily have to complete it in one sitting.

The form allows candidates to save their progress and return later.

Applicants may need to hover near the left side of the “Next” button to reveal the “Save” option.

Can You Correct an Application After Submission?

Yes.

Before the deadline, candidates can either:

Submit a new application, or

Contact the organizers

If multiple applications are submitted, only the:

Most recent application

will be considered.

Questions can be directed to:

info@absw.org.uk

Required Fields Are Important

Applicants must provide all information marked with a red asterisk.

If necessary information or supporting documentation is missing and reviewers cannot assess eligibility or professional merit, the application may be excluded.

Candidates should therefore conduct a complete final check before submission.

AI Use in Applications

WCSJ2027 permits AI tools for a very limited purpose:

Translation or transcription of professional work originally published in another language.

The translation must remain faithful to the original.

However, applicants are expected to write their own:

Professional biography

Motivation statement

Knowledge-sharing plan

Funding statement

Other personal application responses

The organizers explicitly state that they do not expect perfect English.

Answers are evaluated primarily for substance rather than native-level language ability.

Key Dates

Applications open: 2026

Travel Fellowship deadline: October 23, 2026 at 23:59 BST

Conference: September 6–9, 2027

Travel Fellowship attendance requirement: Applicants should be available September 6–10, 2027

Location: London, United Kingdom

Important Pre-Application Checklist

Before submitting, applicants should confirm that they:

Meet one of the eligible professional or student categories.

Have journalism as part of their professional work, unless applying under the student provisions.

Can attend the entire required conference period.

Have or are applying for an appropriate passport.

Have checked whether they require a UK visa.

Can complete the application in English.

Have prepared a two-page CV.

Have selected three strong work examples.

Have obtained a supporting letter.

Have prepared a clear funding statement.

Have a credible plan to share knowledge after the conference.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive WCSJ2027 Travel Fellowship Application

1. Choose Your Three Strongest Journalism Examples

Do not automatically submit your three newest pieces.

Choose work that shows:

Strong reporting

Critical thinking

Clear communication

Scientific complexity handled accurately

Independent journalism

Public relevance

2. Make Your Motivation Specific to WCSJ2027

Read about the conference theme and consider why a global science journalism network matters to your work.

Explain why this particular conference, rather than any generic journalism event, is important.

3. Demonstrate Community Impact

If you already contribute to:

Journalism associations

Training

Mentorship

Newsroom development

Student journalism

Professional networks

explain this clearly.

It can show that the fellowship’s impact will extend beyond you.

4. Be Concrete About Knowledge Sharing

Instead of saying:

“I will share what I learn with colleagues,”

describe exactly how.

For example:

A newsroom workshop

Regional webinar

Training session

Professional association briefing

Journalism article

Mentoring programme

5. Be Transparent About Financial Need

The fellowship exists specifically to improve access.

Explain the financial barriers honestly.

If you have partial support, mention it and explain what gap remains.

6. Explain What You Bring to the Global Community

Your professional background, geography, language, expertise, or reporting experience may provide insights others do not have.

Explain that contribution confidently and specifically.

7. Do Not Ignore Travel Readiness

Passport and visa readiness are important.

Make sure you can realistically travel to London in September 2027 if selected.

Why the WCSJ 2027 Travel Fellowship Matters

Major international conferences can shape careers by giving journalists access to:

New reporting methods

Professional networks

Mentors

Editors

Collaborators

Training opportunities

International perspectives

Yet access to these conferences remains unequal.

Journalists in countries or institutions with limited travel funding may have fewer opportunities to participate in international professional networks despite producing high-quality work.

The WCSJ 2027 Travel Fellowship seeks to reduce this inequality by supporting people whose professional contribution and potential are strong but whose financial resources are limited.

Conclusion

The WCSJ 2027 Travel Fellowship is an important international opportunity for science journalists, media professionals, journalism students, and eligible researchers or educators who want to participate in the World Conference of Science Journalists 2027 in London but would otherwise be unable to afford the associated costs.

Successful applicants may receive support covering approved travel, visa application costs, limited local transportation, up to six nights of accommodation, full conference registration, refreshments, and official conference lunches.

The fellowship does not provide per diem payments and does not cover personal expenses, travel insurance, health expenses, additional hotel nights, or unrelated local transport.

The opportunity is open internationally and does not impose geographic quotas. Applicants from countries classified by the World Bank as low-income or lower-middle-income will receive additional consideration as part of the programme’s commitment to broader global participation.

Eligible applicants include journalists and media professionals covering science and related subjects, students in journalism and related fields, and researchers or educators with a proven professional journalism track record.

Applicants must submit a two-page CV, professional biography, examples of recent journalistic work, a supporting letter, professional-development responses, a knowledge-sharing plan, and a financial-needs statement.

Applications are assessed through a competitive two-stage international process based on professional merit, science-journalism commitment, motivation, professional contribution, quality of work, knowledge-sharing potential, and financial need.

The application deadline is:

23 October 2026 at 23:59 BST

The conference will take place in London in September 2027 under the theme:

“Strengthening science journalism through global networks.”

To know more information about this opportunity, VISIT HERE.

To explore more global fellowship opportunities, VISIT HERE.

TITLE: Singapore FinTech Festival Global FinTech Hackcelerator 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: August 14, 2026

Applications are open for the Singapore FinTech Festival Global FinTech Hackcelerator 2026. The Global FinTech Hackcelerator is organised by Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and Global Finance & Technology Network (GFTN). Now in its 11th edition, the programme pairs market-ready fintech startups with Corporate Champions who set the problem statements and puts the best solutions on stage at the Singapore FinTech Festival.

There are three problem statements:

Credit and fraud risk share common signals, yet are assessed in silos — creating blind spots that lead to missed risks and mounting losses. As financial behaviours shift, static and disconnected models fall further behind. How might we build an adaptive risk modelling system that unifies credit and fraud assessment into a single, continuously learning framework?

US$84 trillion in wealth is set to transfer to a generation that has never known banking without a smartphone. Yet private banking’s client experience remains largely manual, relationship-dependent, and slow to personalise at scale. How might we use AI to deliver a seamless, hyper-personalised digital journey — from onboarding to portfolio advisory — that meets next-generation wealth clients where they are?

Most SMEs don’t know what they don’t know. Gaps in coverage against cyber, supply chain, and asset risks go unnoticed until a claim is denied or a loss hits — and as businesses grow, those gaps quietly compound. How might we use AI to give SMEs a clear, real-time picture of their risk exposure and coverage gaps, and guide them to the right protection at every stage of their growth?

Benefits

The Global FinTech Hackcelerator 2026 provides an unmatched opportunity for early-stage fintech startups to gain global visibility, market access, and unlock growth, mentorship, funding and partnership opportunities.

Finalists will receive:

SGD 20,000 stipend for each finalist team.

Complimentary exhibition kiosk at Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 (SFF 2026).

Mentorship by senior leaders from financial institutions and leading corporates.

Dedicated investment network access

Masterclasses and workshops to sharpen investment readiness and operational expansion strategies.

Pitch your startup at the Demo Day before an international audience of investors, corporate executives, and regulators.

Networking and Deal flow: Access to Investor Hours and curated closed-door networking sessions.

Winners will additionally receive:

SGD 80,000 prize money for each of the top 3 winners.

Opportunity for pilot projects with Corporate Champions post-programme.

Eligibility

Global Fintech Hackcelerator 2026 is looking for early stage fintech startups that:

Have a market ready solution answering to the problem statement posted.

Currently in Bootstrapped, Pre-Seed, Seed, or Series A.

Based in, operating in, or intending to enter Southeast Asia.

Open to external funding opportunities.

Application

Application to Global FinTech Hackcelerator 2026 is free. Shortlisted finalists will benefit from the full programme without equity dilution. Investment opportunities are subject to negotiations between finalists and investors.

Click here to apply

For more information, visit Global FinTech Hackcelerator.

TITLE: Global Prize for Innovation in Water (GPIW) 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: September 30, 2026

Applications for the Global Prize for Innovation in Water (GPIW) 2026 are now open. The Global Prize for Innovation in Water (GPIW) is the largest of its kind in the world. It was launched in 2023 as an initiative by the Saudi Water Authority, reaffirming the Kingdom’s pioneering role in promoting research, fostering innovation, and adopting new breakthroughs in the water sector. The prize aims to honor participants and support pioneers from around the globe.

Categories

The Global Prize for Innovation in Water honors innovative solutions that drive the water sector toward sustainability and efficiency, covering 6 main categories:

Advanced Water Production and Desalination Technologies

Water Reclamation, Circular Economy, and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD)

Water Efficiency, Conservation, and Consumption Management

Digitalization, Automation, and Smart Water Management

Environmental Sustainability and Water Resource Conservation

Accessible and Cost-Effective Wastewater Solutions

Awards

The GPIW offers a financial prize purse, dedicated recognitions, and selected piloting support to advance the development, validation, and market adoption of high-potential water innovations. Awards are distributed as follows:

Grand Prizes – USD $100,000 per winner: Two winners in total, one winner from Track A (TRL 1-3) and one winner from Track B (TRL 4-7)

Impact Medals – USD $50,000 per winner: Twelve winners in total, six winners from Track A (TRL 1-3) and six winners from Track B (TRL 4-7)

Special Mentions – non-monetary recognition: Up to 6 winners in total under Track C (TRL 8–9), with up to two recognitions in each category.

Eligibility

The GPIW is designed to be open, inclusive, and accessible to a broad range of applicants working to advance innovation in the water sector. Applications are welcomed from, among others:

Early-stage startups and venture-backed scale-ups;

Multinational corporations and small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs);

Universities, public or private research institutes, and laboratories;

Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and civil society groups;

Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs), municipal water utilities, and utility consortia;

Individual innovators, research teams, and project teams.

Applicants must ensure that their submission is aligned with at least one Prize track and category and complies with all eligibility requirements set out in these Guidelines.

Application

The application is organized into 8 sections and can be completed at your own pace: your progress can be saved as a draft, allowing you to leave the form and return at any time before the submission deadline. TITLE: Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme 2026 for African Students Applying to the University of Oxford.

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Are you an African student considering applying to the University of Oxford but unsure about where to begin, how the application process works, or what you should do to prepare a competitive application?

The Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme 2026 provides an opportunity for prospective African applicants to receive personalised guidance from people who have direct experience with Oxford. Through the programme, selected mentees will be connected with current Oxford students or Oxford alumni who can share their experiences, answer questions and provide guidance as participants navigate the Oxford application process.

The mentorship programme will run from September to December 2026 and will provide one-to-one mentorship support to African students who are considering applying to the University of Oxford.

Interested applicants are required to complete the programme’s application form by 20 September 2026.

What Is the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme?

The Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme is designed to help prospective African applicants approach the University of Oxford application process with greater confidence.

Applying to Oxford can be a complex process, particularly for students who may not have direct access to someone who has previously studied at Oxford or gone through the university’s application process. Applicants may have questions about where to start, how to prepare, what the experience of applying is like, and how to navigate the various stages involved.

The mentorship programme seeks to bridge that information gap by connecting prospective applicants with individuals who have first-hand experience of Oxford.

Selected participants will receive one-to-one mentorship from a current Oxford student or an Oxford alumnus/alumna. This provides mentees with an opportunity to have conversations with someone who understands the Oxford environment and can share personal experiences and insights.

What Does the Mentorship Programme Offer?

The programme focuses on providing prospective applicants with support as they consider and prepare for an Oxford application.

Through the mentorship relationship, participants can benefit from:

One-to-one mentorship support.

Guidance from a current Oxford student or Oxford alumnus/alumna.

The opportunity to ask questions about applying to Oxford.

First-hand perspectives and experiences from people who have studied at Oxford.

Support in navigating the application process with greater confidence.

An opportunity to gain a better understanding of what the Oxford application journey can involve.

Personalised conversations with a mentor matched to the participant.

Rather than simply providing general information, the programme is structured around a mentor-mentee relationship, allowing participants to engage directly with someone who can answer questions and share their own experiences.

Who Can Apply for the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme?

The programme is aimed at African students who are considering applying to the University of Oxford.

It may be particularly valuable for prospective applicants who:

Are African students.

Are considering submitting an application to the University of Oxford.

Want to understand the Oxford application process better.

Would like to speak with someone who has direct experience with Oxford.

Have questions about preparing for an Oxford application.

Would benefit from individual guidance and mentorship.

Want to approach the application process with greater confidence.

The programme is therefore not intended as a general mentorship opportunity for all students. Its specific focus is on African applicants interested in applying to the University of Oxford.

Why Oxford Application Mentorship Can Be Valuable

For prospective applicants, one of the biggest challenges can be knowing where to begin.

Students may find themselves researching Oxford independently and encountering large amounts of information without knowing which aspects are most relevant to their individual circumstances. Speaking directly with someone who has experienced Oxford as a student can provide an additional perspective.

A mentor can offer insight based on their own experience, help a mentee think through questions and provide a clearer understanding of the application journey.

The Afox-AfriSoc programme therefore gives prospective applicants an opportunity to learn from people who have first-hand knowledge of Oxford rather than having to navigate every question alone.

How the Mentorship Programme Works

The programme is scheduled to take place between September and December 2026.

Applicants first need to complete the designated mentorship programme form. Following submission, the organisers will review applications and determine which applicants are accepted onto the programme.

According to the programme information, applicants will be contacted by early October 2026 to be informed about whether they have been accepted.

For applicants who are selected, additional information will then be provided about their mentor match.

The overall process can therefore be understood in the following stages:

1. Complete the Application Form

Interested prospective applicants must complete the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme form.

The form requests basic personal and contact information, including:

First name

Surname

Email address

Nationality

Country of residence

Gender

WhatsApp number

Applicants should ensure that the information they provide is accurate and that their contact details are active.

2. Submit the Form Before the Deadline

The application form must be completed by:

20 September 2026

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day where possible, particularly if they need additional time to review their information before submitting the form.

3. Application Review

After the deadline, applications will be considered by the programme organisers.

The information provided in the form will be used as part of the programme’s selection process.

4. Receive the Selection Outcome

The organisers state that applicants will be contacted by early October 2026 to inform them whether they have been accepted onto the programme.

5. Mentor Matching

Applicants who are accepted will receive further information about their mentor match.

The programme aims to connect mentees with current Oxford students or alumni, creating an opportunity for participants to receive guidance from someone with direct Oxford experience.

6. Participate in the Mentorship Programme

The programme will run from September to December 2026.

During this period, selected mentees will receive one-to-one mentorship support as they navigate questions surrounding their potential Oxford application.

What Kind of Questions Can Prospective Applicants Explore With a Mentor?

The programme description specifically highlights the opportunity for mentors to share their experiences, answer questions and help mentees navigate the application process.

This means prospective applicants can use the mentorship relationship to better understand aspects of the Oxford application journey that they may otherwise find difficult to navigate independently.

Potential areas of discussion could include understanding the overall application journey, learning about a mentor’s personal experience at Oxford, discussing questions about preparing to apply and gaining a better understanding of the university from the perspective of someone who has studied there.

The mentorship should therefore be viewed as an opportunity to learn, ask questions and gain perspective, rather than simply as a formal application service.

Who Will the Mentors Be?

Selected mentees will be matched with either:

A current University of Oxford student, or

An Oxford alumnus/alumna.

This is one of the central features of the programme.

Instead of receiving guidance exclusively from general admissions resources, participants have the opportunity to interact with someone who has direct experience of Oxford.

A current student may be able to share their experience of being at Oxford at present, while an alumnus or alumna can provide insight based on their own time at the university and application journey.

Important Dates for the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme 2026

Prospective applicants should take note of the following dates:

Application deadline: 20 September 2026

Expected notification: Early October 2026

Mentorship period: September to December 2026

Applicants should make sure that their application form is submitted before the stated deadline.

Information Required on the Application Form

The application form begins by requesting applicants’ personal and contact information.

Applicants are asked to provide:

Contact Information

Applicants are also required to provide:

Applicants should therefore provide an active contact number that they regularly monitor.

Why African Students Considering Oxford Should Consider Applying

The programme offers an opportunity for prospective African applicants to access a form of guidance that can be difficult to obtain independently.

Students considering Oxford may have questions that are difficult to answer simply by reading general information online. A conversation with someone who has actually experienced the university can provide a different perspective.

The mentorship programme can potentially help participants:

Become more familiar with the Oxford application journey.

Ask questions directly to someone with Oxford experience.

Learn from the experiences of current students or alumni.

Gain confidence while considering an application.

Better understand what it may be like to study at Oxford.

Think more carefully about their application preparation.

Access individual rather than purely general guidance.

For students who are serious about exploring an Oxford application, having access to a mentor can therefore be a valuable addition to their preparation.

Application Deadline

The deadline to complete the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme 2026 form is:

20 September 2026

Because the programme organisers indicate that they will communicate the outcome by early October, applicants should also ensure that the email address and WhatsApp number they provide remain accessible after submitting the form.

When Will Applicants Hear Back?

According to the information provided by the programme organisers, applicants will receive an update by early October 2026.

The update will inform applicants whether they have been accepted onto the mentorship programme.

Those who are accepted will receive additional information regarding their mentor match.

Mentorship Period

The Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme is scheduled to run from:

September to December 2026

This gives selected participants several months during which they can receive mentorship and engage with their matched Oxford student or alumnus/alumna.

The programme is therefore intended to provide ongoing support rather than a single information session.

What Applicants Should Do Before Applying

Prospective mentees should take the opportunity to think carefully about why they are interested in Oxford and what they hope to gain from mentorship.

Before submitting the form, applicants can consider:

Why they are interested in applying to Oxford.

What questions they have about the application process.

What areas they would like guidance on.

What they hope to learn from an Oxford student or alumnus/alumna.

Whether their contact details are correct and active.

Having clear questions and goals can help a mentee make better use of a mentorship opportunity if selected.

Is This a Scholarship?

No.

The Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme is not described as a scholarship. The information provided describes it as a mentorship programme designed to connect prospective African Oxford applicants with current Oxford students and alumni.

There is no information in the provided announcement indicating that the programme provides tuition funding, living expenses, application fee funding or a scholarship award.

Students should therefore understand this opportunity primarily as an application guidance and mentorship programme.

Is This an Oxford Admission Programme?

The mentorship programme should also not be confused with an official Oxford admissions offer or an admissions decision.

Participation in mentorship does not mean that a student has been admitted to the University of Oxford.

Instead, the purpose of the programme is to support prospective applicants as they consider and navigate the application process.

Students who participate should still follow the official University of Oxford admissions requirements and deadlines relevant to the course or programme they eventually choose to apply for.

Programme: Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme

Opportunity type: Mentorship programme

Target participants: African students considering applying to the University of Oxford

Format: One-to-one mentorship

Programme period: September to December 2026

Application deadline: 20 September 2026

Expected selection notification: Early October 2026

Purpose: To help prospective African Oxford applicants gain guidance, ask questions, learn from Oxford experiences and navigate the application process with greater confidence.

How to Apply

Interested African students should complete the Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme application form provided by the organisers.

Applicants should carefully provide the requested personal and contact information and submit the completed form before the deadline of 20 September 2026.

Because the programme organisers indicate that successful applicants will receive further information about their mentor match, applicants should monitor the email address and contact information provided on their application after submission.

Final Thoughts

The Afox-AfriSoc Mentorship Programme 2026 provides prospective African applicants to the University of Oxford with an opportunity to receive individual guidance from people who have direct experience of the university.

For students who are interested in Oxford but are uncertain about how to begin, the programme can provide an important opportunity to ask questions, learn from current students or alumni and approach the application process with greater confidence.

The programme will run from September to December 2026, with accepted participants receiving one-to-one mentorship from a current Oxford student or alumnus/alumna.

African students considering an Oxford application should take note of the 20 September 2026 application deadline and complete the mentorship programme form before the closing date.

TITLE: Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 7: Apply for a 12-Week Virtual Mental Health Leadership Fellowship in Africa

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 7 is inviting applications from emerging and established changemakers who want to deepen their understanding of mental health and develop practical leadership skills to address mental health challenges within their communities. The 12-week virtual fellowship brings together participants interested in mental health, community development, advocacy, education, healthcare, research, humanitarian work and related fields.

Designed with a strong focus on African realities while incorporating African and global perspectives, the fellowship goes beyond basic mental health awareness. Participants will engage with mental health experts, practitioners, researchers and leaders while exploring subjects ranging from community mental health and lived experience to neuropsychology, learning how the brain, mind, environment and society interact to influence wellbeing.

The programme also places a strong emphasis on turning knowledge into community action. At the end of the fellowship, participants will develop and implement a Community Impact Capstone Project designed to address a mental health challenge and create measurable benefits within their communities.

About the Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship

The Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship is a 12-week virtual leadership and learning programme intended for people who want to become more effective changemakers in the mental health space.

Rather than limiting participants to theoretical discussions about mental health, the fellowship is structured around learning, leadership, community engagement and practical action.

Participants will be exposed to perspectives from:

Mental health experts

Practitioners

Researchers

Leaders

People with lived experience

Diverse communities and professional backgrounds

The fellowship examines mental health through both African and global perspectives, giving participants an opportunity to understand mental health challenges within the broader social, cultural and environmental contexts in which people live.

This approach is particularly relevant to individuals who recognize that mental wellbeing cannot be addressed solely through clinical interventions. Community structures, education, social environments, policy, culture, advocacy and access to information can all influence mental health outcomes.

What Participants Will Learn

The fellowship covers a broad range of mental health-related themes.

These include:

Community Mental Health

Participants will explore mental health from a community perspective, considering how communities can better identify, discuss and respond to mental health challenges.

Lived Experience

The programme recognizes lived experience as an important form of knowledge and leadership. Participants will have opportunities to engage with perspectives shaped by real-world experiences of mental health.

Neuropsychology

The fellowship also introduces participants to neuropsychology and the relationship between the brain, mind and behaviour.

Learning and Wellbeing

Participants will develop a deeper understanding of how learning, environments and social conditions can influence wellbeing.

African and Global Perspectives

A central feature of the programme is its grounding in African realities while drawing on broader global perspectives. This can help participants consider how mental health approaches can be adapted to the contexts in which their communities operate.

From Mental Health Awareness to Community Action

One of the defining features of the Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship is its focus on moving beyond awareness.

The programme is designed to help participants understand how to act on mental health challenges within their communities.

Throughout the fellowship, participants can strengthen their ability to:

Identify mental health challenges.

Understand the needs of their communities.

Engage with different perspectives.

Develop practical approaches to mental health challenges.

Communicate mental health information effectively.

Build networks with other changemakers.

Apply learning to community-level action.

Develop initiatives capable of reaching people beyond the fellowship itself.

This practical orientation culminates in the Community Impact Capstone Project.

Community Impact Capstone Project

The Community Impact Capstone Project is a central component of the fellowship.

Fellows will take knowledge gained during the programme and apply it to a real mental health issue affecting their communities.

The project is intended to create a tangible community impact rather than remaining solely as an academic or theoretical exercise.

Previous fellows have reportedly undertaken initiatives including:

Community dialogues

Radio programmes

Mental health awareness campaigns

School-based interventions

Outreach activities

The fellowship seeks to create a ripple effect in which one participant’s knowledge and leadership can reach and positively influence many other people.

For Cohort 7, applicants will need to demonstrate that they can design and implement a project that benefits their community. The selection criteria specifically consider the strength and feasibility of the proposed project, including its potential to positively influence at least 200 community members.

Who Should Apply for the Nivishe Fellowship?

The programme is seeking passionate individuals committed to addressing mental health disparities and promoting mental wellbeing.

Applicants should ideally demonstrate one or more of the following characteristics:

A commitment to reducing mental health disparities.

An interest in improving mental wellbeing in their communities.

Current or potential leadership responsibilities.

An interest in community development.

Experience or interest in advocacy.

Experience or interest in education.

Experience or interest in healthcare.

Experience or interest in research.

Experience or interest in humanitarian work.

A desire to create positive social change.

An appreciation for diversity and inclusion.

Willingness to learn from different perspectives and lived experiences.

Formal mental health employment or professional experience is not required. The application specifically states that leadership and commitment to community wellbeing can be demonstrated in different ways.

Age Requirements

Applicants must be 18 years or older.

The fellowship is primarily aimed at young leaders between 18 and 35 years old.

However, people above 35 should not automatically rule themselves out. The programme specifically encourages applicants over 35 who have a strong track record of:

Community leadership

Advocacy

Social impact

This makes the opportunity accessible to both emerging young leaders and more experienced changemakers who can demonstrate meaningful community impact.

Professional and Sectoral Backgrounds

The application form accommodates applicants from a wide range of professional and community sectors.

Relevant sectors include:

Mental health

Healthcare

Education

Research

Humanitarian response

Community development

Advocacy and activism

Government and public service

Youth leadership

Faith-based organizations

Media and communications

Private sector

Other related fields

This broad range demonstrates that the fellowship is not exclusively intended for psychologists, psychiatrists or other clinical mental health professionals.

Professionals working in communication, education, public service, youth leadership, community development and other sectors can also be relevant applicants if they have a genuine interest in mental health and community impact.

Eligibility Requirements

To be considered for the fellowship, applicants should meet the following requirements:

1. Be at Least 18 Years Old

The minimum age is 18.

2. Demonstrate Commitment to Mental Health

Applicants should demonstrate a genuine commitment to addressing mental health disparities and promoting mental wellbeing.

3. Have an Interest in a Relevant Field

Applicants may be involved in or interested in mental health, community development, advocacy, education, healthcare, research, humanitarian work or related areas.

4. Demonstrate Leadership Potential

Applicants should hold or aspire to leadership positions and demonstrate the ability to influence positive change in their communities or institutions.

5. Value Diversity and Inclusion

Applicants should be willing to learn from people with different identities, cultures, professions and lived experiences.

6. Have Reliable Internet Access

Because the fellowship is conducted virtually, applicants need access to a computer and reliable internet connection.

7. Commit to a Community Project

Applicants should be able to design and implement a Community Impact Capstone Project that applies their fellowship learning to benefit their community.

Selection Criteria

Applications will be evaluated against several criteria.

1. Leadership Potential and Community Impact

The selection team will look for evidence of leadership experience, initiative and commitment to creating positive change.

Applicants should therefore explain not only what positions they have held but also what they have actually done and the results their actions produced.

2. Commitment to Mental Health Advancement

Applicants should demonstrate a clear interest in mental health, wellbeing or related social issues.

This commitment can be demonstrated through professional activities, volunteering, advocacy, community initiatives, education, research or other relevant experiences.

3. Availability and Engagement

The fellowship requires active participation.

Applicants will be assessed on their ability to participate in:

Fellowship sessions

Collaborative activities

Assignments

Group discussions

4. Lived Experience and Personal Motivation

The programme recognizes lived experience as a valuable source of expertise.

Applicants who have personal, family, professional or community experiences that have shaped their interest in mental health may choose to explain how those experiences influence their commitment to mental health advocacy and systems change.

However, this section is optional.

5. Diversity and Inclusion

The fellowship aims to create a cohort representing diverse:

Identities

Geographies

Cultures

Professions

Lived experiences

This means the selection process is not based solely on professional credentials but also considers the diversity of perspectives applicants can bring to the cohort.

6. Community Impact Capstone Proposal

The proposed capstone project is another important part of the selection process.

Applicants should present a project that is:

Relevant to a genuine community mental health challenge

Practical

Feasible

Capable of implementation

Designed to create meaningful impact

The selection criteria indicate that the project should have potential to positively influence at least 200 community members.

Fellowship Schedule and Time Commitment

The Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship will run for 12 weeks.

Sessions will take place:

Every Saturday, from 10:00 AM to 12:30 PM EAT.

Selected fellows are expected to attend weekly virtual sessions throughout the programme.

In addition to the weekly sessions, fellows should expect to commit approximately six hours per month to assignments, collaborative activities and group discussions.

Participants should therefore assess their schedules carefully before applying and ensure that they can maintain consistent participation throughout the entire programme.

Expectations for Selected Fellows

Those selected for Cohort 7 will be expected to:

Attend weekly virtual fellowship sessions for 12 weeks.

Commit approximately six additional hours per month to assignments and collaborative activities.

Participate actively in peer learning.

Engage in networking opportunities.

Communicate effectively in English.

Complete the required assignments.

Design and implement a Community Impact Capstone Project.

Address a mental health issue relevant to their community.

Contribute to the Nivishe Fellowship Network after completing the programme.

Continue advancing mental health leadership beyond the fellowship period.

Language Requirement

The fellowship will be conducted in English.

Selected fellows are therefore expected to be proficient in English and able to participate effectively in virtual sessions, discussions, assignments and collaborative activities.

Application Questions

The application requires candidates to provide detailed responses demonstrating their motivation, understanding of mental health, leadership experience and plans for community impact.

Question 1: Personal Motivation and Commitment

Applicants will be asked why they want to join the Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship and how the programme aligns with their personal, professional or community leadership goals.

The response should be between 100 and 200 words.

Candidates should use this section to communicate their motivation and explain how the fellowship could help them grow as changemakers.

Question 2: Mental Health Understanding and Community Context

Applicants will be asked to explain what good mental health means to them and identify pressing mental health challenges affecting their community, institution or the population they work with.

The response should be 100–200 words.

This question provides an opportunity to demonstrate understanding of mental health within a specific community context.

Question 3: Leadership, Experience and Impact

Applicants will need to describe their current or previous involvement in areas such as:

Mental health

Community development

Advocacy

Education

Healthcare

Research

Related areas

They should also explain the impact they have made and the leadership lessons they have gained.

The response should be 100–200 words.

Importantly, formal mental health experience is not mandatory. Applicants can demonstrate leadership and commitment to community wellbeing through different types of experiences.

Question 4: Community Impact Capstone Project

Applicants will be asked to propose a mental health initiative they would like to implement during the fellowship.

The response should be 150–300 words.

Applicants should describe:

The community mental health challenge they want to address

The proposed initiative

The community they hope to reach

The expected impact

Possible approaches include awareness campaigns, community dialogues, radio programmes, school activities, digital campaigns, support groups, workplace initiatives, research dissemination and advocacy efforts.

The application also notes that project ideas may evolve during the fellowship as fellows gain additional knowledge and mentorship.

Question 5: Community Reach and Ripple Effect

Applicants must explain how they intend to share knowledge, skills and networks gained through the fellowship with people beyond themselves.

The response should be 100–200 words.

Candidates can discuss how they plan to engage:

Community members

Organizations

Institutions

Professional networks

Youth groups

Other relevant stakeholders

The purpose is to demonstrate how participation in the fellowship can produce a wider community impact rather than benefiting only the individual fellow.

Question 6: Lived Experience and Perspective

Applicants may optionally discuss personal, family, professional or community experiences that have shaped their interest in mental health.

This is an optional question requiring a response of 100–200 words.

Applicants should only share what they are comfortable discussing. The programme recognizes lived experience as a valuable form of expertise and leadership.

Question 7: Commitment Statement

Applicants must indicate whether they can commit fully to the fellowship’s requirements.

The programme requires:

Weekly attendance

Active participation

Assignment completion

Community Impact Capstone Project implementation

Applicants who answer yes must briefly explain how they will ensure their participation throughout the 12-week programme.

The response should be 50–100 words.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should approach the application as an opportunity to demonstrate not just interest in mental health but also their potential to create community-level impact.

Demonstrate Genuine Motivation

Clearly explain why mental health matters to you and why this particular fellowship is relevant to your goals.

Connect Your Experience to Community Impact

Whether your background is in communications, education, healthcare, advocacy, research, government, youth leadership or community development, explain how your experience has helped you contribute to positive change.

Identify a Specific Community Challenge

For the capstone project, avoid proposing an overly broad initiative. Identify a specific challenge and explain how your project could address it.

Think About Measurable Impact

Because the fellowship emphasizes community reach, applicants should think about how their proposed project could reach and positively influence at least 200 people.

Demonstrate Leadership

Leadership does not necessarily mean holding a senior job title. Applicants can demonstrate leadership through volunteering, community organizing, advocacy, educational initiatives, youth engagement, research or other forms of social impact.

Show Commitment

The programme requires consistent participation over 12 weeks. Applicants should demonstrate that they have considered the time commitment and can participate fully.

Application Timeline

The application timeline for Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 7 is:

Applications open: September 9, 2026

Applications close: September 18, 2026

Fellowship sessions: Every Saturday, 10:00 AM–12:30 PM EAT

Fellowship duration: 12 weeks

The application deadline is therefore September 18, 2026.

Application Support

Nivishe states that it is committed to making the application process accessible and inclusive.

Applicants who experience challenges completing or submitting the application, or who require reasonable accommodation because of a disability, language barrier or other circumstances, can contact the Nivishe team for support.

The organization states that it will make efforts to assist applicants and provide an equitable opportunity to apply.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should complete the official Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 7 Application Form and provide the information and written responses requested in the application.

Applicants should carefully review each question, observe the specified word limits and ensure that their responses clearly demonstrate motivation, leadership, mental health understanding and potential community impact.

For application support, the fellowship provides the following email address:

partnerships@nivishefoundation.org

APPLY HERE

Why You Should Consider the Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship

The fellowship can be particularly valuable for emerging leaders who want to combine personal development with practical community impact.

Key opportunities include:

Deepen your understanding of mental health: Explore mental health through African and global perspectives.

TITLE: WSAI Fellowships 2026 at IIT Madras: Postdoctoral and Post-Baccalaureate Research Opportunities in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Through its fellowship programmes, the School seeks to develop scientific talent while creating an environment where fellows can pursue meaningful research and build long-term academic and professional careers.

Host Institution: Wadhwani School of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (WSAI), IIT Madras, India

Location: IIT Madras, India

About the Wadhwani School of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

The Wadhwani School of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (WSAI) is an academic and research school at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras).

Founded in 2024, the School brings together faculty members with expertise in different areas of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. Its work is focused on addressing impactful problems that have practical and societal relevance.

WSAI’s interdisciplinary structure is particularly important for researchers working in modern AI and Data Science because many emerging research challenges cannot be addressed effectively through a single academic discipline.

The School’s research environment provides fellows with opportunities to:

Work with faculty members specializing in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence.

Develop research projects and independent research directions.

Collaborate across disciplines.

Interact with researchers and scientists from around the world.

Access advanced computing infrastructure.

Participate in workshops and academic colloquia.

Develop publication records through high-quality research.

Build connections with researchers in academia and industry.

For candidates interested in building a research-oriented career in AI or Data Science, the WSAI fellowships can provide an environment for developing both technical expertise and research independence.

WSAI Post Doctoral Fellowship 2026

The WSAI Post Doctoral Fellowship is designed for outstanding researchers who have already completed a PhD and want to continue developing their research careers in Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, or related application areas.

The programme is particularly suited to candidates who have demonstrated strong academic or research capabilities and are interested in developing independent research lines under supportive mentorship.

According to WSAI, the fellowship environment is designed to nurture scientific leadership. Fellows are encouraged to move beyond simply contributing to existing projects and instead develop their own research directions with guidance and support from experienced faculty.

The Post Doctoral Fellowship is intended for:

Outstanding candidates who hold a PhD degree.

Researchers whose doctoral research is related to Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, or allied application domains.

Researchers interested in developing independent research programmes.

Candidates seeking mentorship from leading faculty in Data Science and AI.

Researchers who want access to advanced high-performance computing infrastructure.

Individuals interested in publishing research and participating in an interdisciplinary academic environment.

A PhD in a relevant field is therefore the central academic requirement described for this fellowship.

The fellowship includes a monthly stipend of INR 1 lakh.

This financial support is intended to provide fellows with funding while they undertake their research at WSAI.

Fellows become part of a highly interdisciplinary environment where researchers working in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence can interact and collaborate.

This can expose researchers to different methodologies, perspectives, technical approaches, and application areas.

Postdoctoral fellows receive the opportunity to work with and receive mentorship from leading faculty members in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence.

Mentorship can be particularly valuable for researchers seeking to establish independent research programmes and develop their scientific leadership.

The fellowship also provides fellows with opportunities to mentor bright students.

This can allow postdoctoral researchers to gain additional academic experience while contributing to the development of the next generation of researchers.

In addition to the monthly stipend, the fellowship includes additional allowances for research and travel.

Such support can help fellows participate in research-related activities and academic events.

WSAI regularly organizes workshops and colloquia involving international experts.

Fellows can benefit from exposure to current research developments and opportunities to interact with experts working in different areas of AI and Data Science.

7. High-Performance Computing Infrastructure

Researchers receive access to state-of-the-art high-performance computing infrastructure.

This is particularly significant for researchers working with computationally intensive AI and Data Science projects that require substantial CPU or GPU resources.

The programme can provide an opportunity to spend up to two years undertaking research in an advanced academic environment.
