TITLE: Call for Youth Researchers: Apply to Support Youth Participation and Policy Research Under the Youth Voice Naija Project

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Network of Youth for Sustainable Initiative (NGYouthSDGs) has opened a call for Youth Researchers to support field research, youth engagement, interviews, data collection and documentation under the Youth Voice Naija Project.

This opportunity is designed for young people who are passionate about research, youth participation, public policy and inclusive decision-making and who are willing to work directly with young people whose voices are often missing from formal policy and decision-making processes.

Through the project, selected Youth Researchers will contribute to efforts aimed at strengthening the participation and leadership of underrepresented young people and creating meaningful opportunities for them to contribute to the development, implementation and monitoring of the National Youth Policy 2026–2030.

If you are a young person interested in research and community engagement and are motivated to help ensure that young people’s experiences and perspectives are represented in policy processes, this call may provide an opportunity to gain practical research experience while contributing to an important youth-focused initiative.

About the Youth Voice Naija Project

The Youth Voice Naija Project focuses on increasing the meaningful participation of young people in policy and decision-making spaces.

Young people represent an important part of society, but not all youth have equal opportunities to participate in discussions and processes that affect their lives. Some groups face barriers related to geography, socioeconomic circumstances, access to information, limited representation or other forms of exclusion.

As a result, policy processes can sometimes fail to adequately capture the experiences and priorities of young people who are most difficult to reach.

The Youth Voice Naija Project seeks to address this challenge by supporting greater participation from underrepresented and often-overlooked youth groups.

A key focus of the project is enabling young people to directly engage in processes related to the National Youth Policy 2026–2030. By collecting young people’s perspectives and documenting their experiences, the initiative aims to contribute to more inclusive youth policy processes.

The Youth Researchers recruited through this call will therefore play an important role in connecting the project with young people in selected communities and locations.

What Will Youth Researchers Do?

Selected Youth Researchers will support several aspects of the project’s field research and youth engagement activities.

Their responsibilities will focus on reaching young people, collecting information, conducting engagements and ensuring that the experiences and perspectives shared by participants are properly documented.

Key activities may include:

1. Participant Outreach

Youth Researchers will help identify and reach potential participants for the project’s research and engagement activities.

This is particularly important because the project is interested in reaching young people who may not normally have access to policy discussions or youth participation opportunities.

Researchers may therefore be expected to:

Identify relevant youth groups and individuals.

Connect with young people within selected communities and locations.

Encourage eligible young people to participate in research activities.

Communicate information about the research process to potential participants.

Help ensure that underrepresented youth groups are adequately reached.

Support inclusive participation throughout the research process.

The ability to communicate respectfully with different groups of young people will therefore be important.

2. Field Data Collection

Youth Researchers will participate in collecting information from young people in selected locations.

The information gathered may help the project understand young people’s:

Experiences;

Challenges;

Priorities;

Aspirations;

Views on youth participation;

Perspectives on policy processes;

Capacity-building needs; and

Experiences with decision-making and leadership opportunities.

Researchers will be expected to approach data collection responsibly and accurately, ensuring that information gathered from participants is properly recorded and documented.

3. One-on-One Engagements With Young People

The opportunity specifically involves one-on-one engagements with young people.

These interactions can provide participants with space to share their individual experiences and perspectives in greater depth.

Youth Researchers may be required to engage participants through structured conversations or interviews and capture relevant information arising from those discussions.

Strong listening and interpersonal communication skills can therefore be valuable for anyone interested in applying.

4. Interviews

Youth Researchers will also support interviews with young people.

Through interviews, the project can gather detailed information about the realities facing young people, particularly those whose experiences may not be adequately reflected in mainstream policy discussions.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating with people from different backgrounds and asking questions in a respectful and appropriate manner.

5. Documentation

Another important responsibility will be documenting the experiences and perspectives of participating young people.

Accurate documentation can help transform individual experiences into useful research findings that can inform youth participation and policy processes.

Researchers should consequently be:

Detail-oriented;

Responsible;

Organized;

Accurate when recording information; and

Committed to representing participants’ views fairly.

Research Training for Selected Applicants

Selected Youth Researchers will participate in a Research Training before supporting data collection across the selected locations.

The training is intended to prepare researchers for their responsibilities and help create a common understanding of the project’s research and data-collection processes.

Participation in the training is particularly important because field research requires researchers to understand how to interact with participants, collect information appropriately and document findings consistently.

The training may therefore help selected researchers develop or strengthen practical skills relevant to:

Field research;

Data collection;

Interviewing;

Youth engagement;

Documentation;

Community outreach; and

Research ethics and responsible engagement.

For young people seeking to build practical experience in research, public policy, youth development or community engagement, participation in such training can also provide useful professional exposure.

Who Is NGYouthSDGs Looking For?

The organization is looking for young people who demonstrate a genuine interest in research, youth participation and policy processes.

According to the call, successful applicants should be:

Curious and interested in learning;

Responsible in carrying out assigned responsibilities;

Willing to engage directly with young people;

Interested in research and data collection;

Comfortable reaching out to youth groups and individuals;

Willing to support field research activities;

Interested in youth participation and policy processes; and

Prepared to work with young people in communities and locations that are often overlooked.

An applicant does not simply need to be interested in research in theory. The opportunity requires a willingness to participate in practical activities involving outreach, interviews, data collection and documentation.

Why This Opportunity May Be Valuable for Young Researchers

Participating as a Youth Researcher can provide practical exposure to the intersection of research, youth development and public policy.

Unlike opportunities that are primarily classroom-based, this role involves engaging directly with young people and gathering information from communities.

Some of the potential benefits include:

Practical Research Experience

Researchers will gain practical exposure to field research activities, including participant outreach, interviews, data collection and documentation.

This can be particularly useful for young people interested in careers or further study in:

Social sciences;

Development studies;

Public policy;

International development;

Governance;

Political science;

Sociology;

Youth development;

Community development;

Research and evaluation; and

Related fields.

Exposure to Youth Policy Processes

The project is connected to efforts surrounding the National Youth Policy 2026–2030, giving participants an opportunity to contribute to a youth-focused policy process.

This can help researchers understand how young people’s experiences and perspectives can be gathered and incorporated into policy discussions.

Community Engagement Experience

The role requires researchers to engage with young people, including those in communities that are often overlooked.

This can strengthen applicants’ practical experience in community outreach, stakeholder engagement and inclusive participation.

Research and Interview Skills

Through fieldwork and one-on-one engagements, selected researchers can develop valuable skills in conducting interviews, asking questions, listening actively and documenting information.

Contribution to Youth Representation

Perhaps one of the most important aspects of the opportunity is the opportunity to help ensure that the voices of underrepresented young people are heard.

By reaching young people who may otherwise be excluded from policy discussions, Youth Researchers can contribute to a more inclusive understanding of young people’s experiences and needs.

Qualities That Could Strengthen an Application

Although applicants are not provided with a detailed scoring framework in the announcement, individuals considering applying should ensure that their responses clearly demonstrate their suitability for the role.

Applicants can emphasize relevant experience or interests such as:

Research experience — Any previous academic, community or independent research experience may be relevant.

Youth engagement — Experience working with youth groups, student organizations, community initiatives or youth-led organizations can demonstrate the ability to engage the target population.

Community outreach — Applicants who have participated in awareness campaigns, mobilization activities or community-based initiatives can highlight this experience.

Communication skills — Researchers will interact directly with participants, making clear and respectful communication important.

Data collection experience — Experience conducting surveys, interviews, focus groups or other forms of information gathering can be useful.

Documentation skills — Applicants should demonstrate that they can accurately record and organize information.

Interest in public policy — A genuine interest in how policies are developed, implemented and monitored can strengthen an application.

Commitment to inclusion — Applicants should show an understanding of why it is important to include young people who are often excluded from decision-making processes.

Who Can Apply?

The call is targeted at young people interested in research, youth participation and policy processes, particularly those who are willing to support outreach and engagement with underrepresented youth.

The announcement emphasizes the importance of reaching young people in locations and communities that are often overlooked.

Geographic Eligibility

The opportunity is associated with the Youth Voice Naija Project and the National Youth Policy 2026–2030, indicating a Nigeria-focused research and youth engagement context.

The supplied announcement does not explicitly provide a detailed list of eligible countries, nationalities, ethnic groups or continental eligibility categories. Applicants should therefore rely on the official application form and information provided by NGYouthSDGs when determining whether they meet the geographic requirements.

Educational Qualifications

The announcement does not specify a mandatory academic degree, field of study or minimum educational qualification.

Instead, the emphasis is on applicants being young people who are:

Curious;

Responsible;

Interested in research;

Willing to conduct field activities;

Able to engage young people; and

Interested in youth participation and policy.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that a specific university qualification is required unless the application form or organization provides additional requirements.

Application Process

Interested applicants are required to complete the application form carefully.

The application form requests an email address and contains required questions that applicants must answer before submitting their responses.

Applicants should take time to provide accurate and thoughtful information rather than submitting incomplete or rushed responses.

The application form provided in the call is hosted through Google Forms.

Application form: Youth Researchers Application Form

APPLY HERE

What Happens After Applying?

Submitting the application does not automatically mean that an applicant has been selected.

According to the announcement, shortlisted applicants will be contacted for further assessment or an interview.

The selection process may therefore involve additional evaluation after the initial application.

Applicants should monitor the email address they provide in the application and ensure that they can receive communications from the organizing team.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Before submitting the form, prospective Youth Researchers can take several steps to improve the quality of their application.

Demonstrate Your Interest in Research

Explain why research matters to you and, where applicable, mention previous research activities you have participated in.

This could include academic research, community surveys, independent projects, volunteer research or other relevant activities.

Highlight Youth Engagement Experience

If you have worked with young people, youth-led organizations, student groups, community organizations or development initiatives, make this clear in your application.

Show That You Understand the Purpose of the Project

Applicants should demonstrate an understanding of why the project seeks to amplify the voices of underrepresented young people.

Avoid providing generic responses that could apply to any opportunity. Instead, connect your motivation to youth participation, inclusive decision-making and policy engagement.

Demonstrate Responsibility

Because Youth Researchers will collect and document information from participants, applicants should demonstrate that they can handle responsibilities carefully and professionally.

Be Specific

When describing previous experiences, provide concrete examples where possible.

For example, instead of simply stating that you have “research experience,” explain what type of research you conducted, your responsibilities and what you learned.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Applicants should carefully review the official application form before submitting their responses.

In particular:

Ensure all required questions are completed.

Provide accurate personal and professional information.

Use an email address that you regularly monitor.

Review your answers before submitting the form.

Make sure your responses clearly communicate your interest in youth research and policy.

Do not submit passwords or confidential login information through the form.

Keep a record of your application where appropriate.

The form itself also reminds applicants that passwords should never be submitted through Google Forms.

Visit HERE for more information about the Youth Voice Naija Project.

Deadline

Deadline: Not specified in the supplied call.

The announcement provided does not state a closing date for applications. Applicants should therefore check the official application form or the organization’s official communication channels for any deadline or subsequent update before applying.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Youth Voice Naija Project?

The Youth Voice Naija Project is an initiative focused on strengthening the participation and leadership of underrepresented young people and creating opportunities for them to contribute to policy and decision-making processes, including engagement around the National Youth Policy 2026–2030.

What will Youth Researchers do?

Youth Researchers will support participant outreach, field data collection, one-on-one engagements, interviews and documentation of young people’s experiences, perspectives and capacity-building needs.

Will selected researchers receive training?

Yes. Selected Youth Researchers will participate in a Research Training designed to support them in carrying out data collection across selected locations.

Is previous research experience mandatory?

The supplied announcement does not state that previous research experience is mandatory. However, applicants should demonstrate curiosity, responsibility and a genuine interest in research, youth participation and policy processes.

Is there an application fee?

No application fee is mentioned in the supplied announcement.

Is there a deadline?

No deadline is stated in the information provided. Applicants should check the official application form and NGYouthSDGs’ official communications for the latest deadline information.

What happens after submitting an application?

Shortlisted applicants will be contacted for further assessment or an interview.

Who is the opportunity intended for?

It is intended for young people who are passionate about research, youth participation and policy processes and who are willing to engage with young people, particularly those in underrepresented or overlooked communities.

Final Thoughts

The Youth Voice Naija Youth Researchers call provides an opportunity for young people to move beyond simply participating in conversations about youth development and instead contribute directly to the research and engagement processes that can inform youth policy.

By supporting participant outreach, conducting interviews, collecting information and documenting young people’s experiences, selected researchers can help bring the perspectives of underrepresented youth into policy discussions.

The opportunity may be particularly valuable for young people interested in research, public policy, governance, youth development, community engagement, social development and inclusive decision-making.

Those interested should carefully complete the application form, clearly communicate their motivation and relevant experience, and monitor their email for possible follow-up regarding assessment or interviews.

Apply through the official application form: Youth Researchers Application Form

TITLE: 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program at Bank of America: Apply in São Paulo

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program offers university students an opportunity to gain practical experience in investment banking with Bank of America in São Paulo, Brazil. The internship is designed for students pursuing disciplines such as Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, or related fields who want to build experience in corporate finance, mergers and acquisitions, debt and equity financing, financial analysis, and client advisory.

The position is listed as an Off-cycle Internship under Job ID JR-14454 and is based in São Paulo, Brazil. According to the official Bank of America careers listing, applications are open until December 31, 2027.

For students interested in pursuing careers in investment banking, corporate finance, financial advisory, capital markets, or related areas, this opportunity can provide exposure to the type of transactions and financial solutions that support companies and contribute to the broader global economy.

Opportunity Overview

Opportunity: 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program

Position: Investment Banking Intern

Organization: Bank of America

Location: São Paulo, Brazil

Job ID: JR-14454

Internship type: Off-cycle internship

Work arrangement: In-person or hybrid

Working hours: 30 hours per week

Minimum age: 18 years

Application deadline: December 31, 2027

Required language: Fluent English

Eligible academic backgrounds: Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, and related courses

The official listing confirms that the role is intended for students who are currently studying, attend classes in the morning, and expect to graduate in one year or more.

About the Bank of America Brazil Investment Banking Group

Investment banking is an area of financial services focused on helping companies, institutions, and other organizations make significant financial and strategic decisions.

The Brazil Investment Banking group at Bank of America provides advisory expertise across major corporate finance activities. According to the vacancy announcement, the team works around Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A), Debt underwriting, and Equity underwriting, providing integrated financial solutions to clients.

This means an intern joining the team may be exposed to an environment where financial analysis, corporate strategy, market knowledge, communication, and client service come together.

Mergers and Acquisitions

Mergers and acquisitions involve transactions in which companies combine, acquire other businesses, sell businesses, or restructure ownership.

Investment banking professionals supporting M&A transactions may be involved in activities such as:

Financial analysis

Company and industry research

Valuation

Preparation of financial models

Analysis of potential transactions

Preparation of presentations and transaction materials

Supporting due diligence processes

Monitoring market developments

Preparing information for clients and senior bankers

For an intern, exposure to M&A can provide valuable insight into how major corporate transactions are evaluated and executed.

Debt Underwriting

Debt underwriting involves helping companies and institutions raise capital through debt markets.

Investment banking teams may help clients evaluate financing requirements, structure transactions, assess market conditions, and connect borrowers with investors.

Students interested in corporate finance can therefore gain a better understanding of how businesses finance expansion, acquisitions, operations, and other strategic objectives.

Equity Underwriting

Equity underwriting involves helping companies raise capital through the issuance of shares or other equity-related securities.

This area requires an understanding of financial markets, company performance, valuation, investor considerations, and broader economic conditions.

Exposure to equity transactions can help students understand how businesses access capital markets and how investors evaluate investment opportunities.

Who Is Bank of America Looking For?

The internship is targeted at university students with relevant academic backgrounds and an interest in investment banking.

According to the official vacancy, applicants should meet several important requirements.

1. Students in Relevant Academic Disciplines

Applicants should be studying:

Business

Economics

Accounting

Engineering

Related courses

This broad academic requirement means that the opportunity is not restricted exclusively to traditional finance or economics students. Students from other related disciplines may also be considered if their academic background and skills are relevant to investment banking.

Engineering students, for example, may bring quantitative, analytical, problem-solving, and technical skills that can be valuable in financial analysis.

2. Morning Shift Students

The vacancy specifically states that applicants should be morning shift students.

This requirement is important because candidates should assess their university timetable before applying. The internship requires availability for 30 hours per week, so applicants need to determine whether their academic schedule can accommodate the required working hours.

3. Students With at Least One Year Remaining Before Graduation

Applicants are expected to graduate in one year or more.

This is an important eligibility condition. Students who are very close to graduation should carefully evaluate whether they satisfy the requirement before submitting an application.

The program is particularly relevant to students who still have sufficient time remaining in their degree to undertake an internship while continuing their studies.

4. Fluent English

Fluent English is mandatory for the position.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating in English in a professional environment.

Strong English communication can be particularly important in investment banking because professionals may need to:

Communicate with colleagues

Prepare written materials

Participate in meetings

Understand financial documentation

Present analysis

Communicate with clients and stakeholders

Work in an international business environment

Applicants whose English is not yet at a professional level should consider strengthening their written and spoken communication skills before applying.

5. Availability for 30 Hours Per Week

Candidates must be available to work 30 hours per week.

The internship can be undertaken in an in-person or hybrid format, according to the vacancy information.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to commit substantial weekly time to the internship while continuing their studies.

Key Skills Required for the Investment Banking Internship

Beyond academic qualifications, Bank of America identifies several skills that are relevant to the position.

Strong Knowledge of Corporate Finance

A strong understanding of corporate finance is one of the most important foundations for an investment banking career.

Applicants should ideally understand concepts such as:

Financial statements

Cash flow

Capital structure

Cost of capital

Valuation

Debt financing

Equity financing

Corporate investment decisions

Profitability

Financial performance

Risk and return

Students who can demonstrate practical understanding rather than simply memorizing definitions may be better prepared for the demands of the role.

Macroeconomic Knowledge

The vacancy also highlights macroeconomic knowledge.

Investment banking decisions do not happen in isolation. Economic conditions can influence companies, investors, capital markets, financing costs, mergers, acquisitions, and investment decisions.

Applicants should therefore develop an understanding of issues such as:

Economic growth

Inflation

Interest rates

Monetary policy

Fiscal policy

Exchange rates

Employment

Global economic trends

Financial market conditions

Keeping up with major economic developments can also help candidates demonstrate genuine interest in financial markets during recruitment.

Strong Communication Skills

Professionals must communicate complex financial information clearly to colleagues, clients, executives, investors, and other stakeholders.

Strong communication skills can include:

Clear writing

Presentation skills

Active listening

Ability to explain complex concepts

Attention to detail

Team communication

Client Focus

Candidates should therefore demonstrate an understanding of:

Professionalism

Confidentiality

Responsiveness

A candidate who can demonstrate that they understand the importance of delivering high-quality work for clients can strengthen their overall profile.

An investment banking internship can be valuable for students who want to understand how the financial sector operates in practice.

Although the exact responsibilities assigned to an intern will depend on the team and business needs, working within an investment banking environment can provide exposure to areas such as financial analysis, corporate transactions, market research, client service, and professional financial communication.

Potential areas of professional development include:

Practical Corporate Finance Exposure

Students can move beyond classroom theory and gain an understanding of how financial concepts are applied in real business situations.

The Brazil Investment Banking group works across M&A, debt, and equity activities, giving the role a strong connection to major corporate finance transactions.

Professional Workplace Experience

The internship provides an opportunity to work within a major global financial institution and experience professional expectations around communication, teamwork, deadlines, accuracy, and client service.

The experience can therefore be useful for students considering a long-term career in finance or related business fields.

Why São Paulo Is an Important Location for This Opportunity

São Paulo is one of Brazil’s most important financial and business centers.

For students pursuing financial careers, an internship in São Paulo can provide exposure to Brazil’s corporate and financial environment while allowing participants to work within an international financial institution.

The location is particularly relevant to applicants interested in emerging markets, Latin American finance, multinational corporations, and cross-border business.

Applicants who are not currently based in São Paulo should pay close attention to the position’s in-person or hybrid requirements and determine whether they can realistically meet the workplace expectations.

Candidates who are below 18 should therefore not assume that they qualify simply because they meet the academic requirements.

Work Arrangement

The flexibility of a hybrid arrangement may be useful for some students, but applicants should not interpret “hybrid” as meaning that the internship is fully remote.

Candidates should be prepared to participate in the working arrangement required by the employer.

December 31, 2027

The official Bank of America careers page currently lists December 31, 2027 as the application deadline.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should apply through the official Bank of America careers platform.

When applying, candidates should carefully review the official vacancy requirements and provide accurate academic, professional, and personal information.

Applicants should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates:

Their relevant academic knowledge.

Their interest in investment banking.

Their understanding of corporate finance.

TITLE: Vacancies – Video Editors; Animation & Motion Graphics Designers; and Camera Men for the Association of African Universities’ Television (AAU TV)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
About the Association of African Universities (AAU)

The AAU is an international non-profit, non-governmental organization created by African Universities to promote cooperation among them on one hand, and between them and the international academic community on the other. Created in 1967, the AAU has served as the voice of higher education in Africa and aims to improve the quality of African higher education, and to strengthen its contribution to Africa’s development by supporting the core functions of higher education institutions and facilitating critical reflection and consensus building on issues affecting higher education. The AAU is headquartered in Accra, Ghana, and has a membership of more than 400 Higher Education Institutions and is the technical implementing arm of the African Union Commission (AUC) in higher education. The Association is also the coordinating agency of the Higher Education Cluster of the Continental Education Strategy for Africa (CESA 16-25). Through our guidance, our member universities are also responsible for implementing the Science, Technology, and Innovation Strategy for Africa (STISA 2024) of the AUC.

In 2018, the AAU established the AAU Television (AAU TV) as a virtual platform to stimulate dialogue, create visibility for African Higher Education Institutions, document success stories from African Higher Education and advance African academic scholarship. The AAU TV leverages the wealth of research and development knowledge that AAU member universities and collaborators have churned out over the years, thereby creating a space where both the academic community and general public may access the benefits that these innovations hold for the continent.

About DW Akademie

DW Akademie is Deutsche Welle’s centre for international media development, journalism training and knowledge transfer. DW Akademie works with journalists, media organizations, civil society actors and other partners in developing and emerging economies, with support that includes funding from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, the German Federal Foreign Office and the European Union.

The opportunities below reflect that broad mandate. Some seek individual experts to deliver specialist training; others seek an organization able to host a programme; one invites young Ukrainians to take part in a media-literacy and stand-up comedy experience.

1. Podcast Storytelling and Production Trainers for Independent Media in the Western Balkans

The most urgent call is the DW Akademie opportunity for podcast trainers in the Western Balkans. DW Akademie intends to contract up to four experienced trainers to create and deliver a practical capacity-building programme for independent media organizations participating in SustainMedia II, a project concerned with the economic sustainability and innovation of independent media in the Western Balkans.

Purpose of the assignment

The programme is intended to strengthen both the editorial and technical abilities of journalists and media professionals. Participants should leave with the practical capacity to plan, produce, publish and improve audience-oriented podcasts that support public-interest journalism, expand audience reach and help independent outlets diversify their content.

The selected trainers will jointly develop a three-day programme that may be delivered online or offline. The official terms allow up to two preparation days, while implementation is expected between September and November 2026.

Expected training content

The assignment covers the full podcast workflow through three broad modules:

Podcast storytelling and editorial development

Finding viable podcast concepts

Understanding audience needs

Editorial and content planning

Script development

Interviewing techniques

Narrative structure and storytelling

Selecting suitable podcast formats

Adapting content for different audiences

Podcast production

Studio recording

Field recording

Mobile podcast production

Equipment selection

Sound quality

Editing workflows

Production planning

Publishing and distribution

Technical quality standards

Audience development and practical production

Podcast branding

Audience engagement

Content promotion

Hands-on production exercises

Review of participant productions

Editorial feedback

Recommendations for sustainable podcast development

Selected trainers will be expected to collaborate on the training concept and agenda, combine theory with demonstrations and practical work, facilitate group and peer-learning activities, provide individual feedback, review participant assignments, monitor progress and coordinate closely with DW Akademie and the other trainers.

The required deliverables include a detailed concept and agenda, learning materials, practical exercises, delivery of the three-day programme, recommendations for participants’ continued development and a report on the training.

Professional experience in journalism, storytelling and podcast production

Create practical safety policies, incident-response procedures and continuity plans

Protect journalists, community correspondents, confidential sources and organizational information

Prepare for the responsible adoption and governance of AI tools

Continue serving women, young people and rural communities in a safer digital environment

Secure storage, data-retention and data-destruction practices

Confidential-source and whistleblower protection

Metadata and digital footprints

Backup strategies, disaster recovery and continuity of operations

AI governance and newsroom policies

Practical application checklist

Before applying for any current DW Akademie opportunity, candidates and organizations should:

Open the individual opportunity page rather than relying only on the central hub.

Download and read the complete Terms of Reference.

Confirm the exact deadline, time zone, subject line and submission email.

Tailor the CV, interest letter or proposal to the stated thematic area and deliverables.

Include every requested financial detail, tax component and supporting document.

Respect page limits and file-format instructions, including merged-PDF requirements.

Demonstrate relevant regional or contextual knowledge with specific examples.

Provide evidence of previous assignments, productions or training work where requested.

Check that references, cost estimates, contact information and attachments are complete.

Frequently asked questions

Are all listings on the DW Akademie opportunities page still open?

No. The official hub can display opportunities with recently passed deadlines. Applicants must read the date on each individual page and its downloadable Terms of Reference. As of August 31, 2026, six calls were still actionable, including the Western Balkans podcast trainer deadline later that same day.

Can applicants based outside the advertised country apply?

It depends on the call. The Tanzania Terms of Reference explicitly permit facilitators based in Tanzania or elsewhere, provided they have the necessary expertise and understand the East African media context. Other calls may require local delivery capacity, regional knowledge, language skills or residence in a specific city. Applicants should follow the exact wording of the relevant terms.

Does joining a trainer pool guarantee paid work?

No. The SANA and Media Emergency Kit calls state that admission to a qualified-trainer pool does not guarantee a contract. Assignments will depend on project needs, trainer expertise and availability.

Are financial offers required?

Most professional calls request some form of financial information. This may be a daily rate, preparation-day rate, total cost, or detailed programme budget. The Tanzania call specifically requires the applicant to include the stated withholding tax in the rate.

Where should applicants obtain the final application instructions?

The controlling source should be the individual official opportunity page and its linked Terms of Reference. Applicants should copy email addresses and subject lines carefully from the downloadable document and check the page again immediately before submission.

Conclusion

The 2026 DW Akademie opportunities and tenders currently provide several distinct routes into international media-development work. Experienced podcast producers can support independent media in the Western Balkans; digital-security and responsible-AI specialists can work with Tanzanian media houses; Arabic-speaking journalists and trainers can join Syria-focused trainer pools; a Phnom Penh organization can design a culturally grounded programme for a regional conference; and Ukrainian young people in Berlin can develop media literacy through stand-up comedy.

TITLE: Celebrating 50 Years of ESF: A Milestone in Catalysing Research

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
ESF News | News

On 26 June 2024, ESF – the European Science Foundation, celebrated its 50th anniversary with a conference at the Villa Sturm in Strasbourg. This event not only marked half a century of ESF’s presence in the scientific landscape but also set the stage for envisioning its future in terms of sustainable and impactful research management.

A Glance Back and a Look Forward

The program kicked off with opening speeches by representatives of the City Council of Strasbourg and of the Grand Est Region. Véronique Halloin, President of ESF and Nicolas Walter CEO of ESF then took the audience on a journey through the history of ESF and research management, before outlining the organisation’s strategic vision for the future.

Download Véronique Halloin’s presentation

Catalysing Research in a Changing Environment

This retrospective set the tone for the keynote address by Ursula Bassler from CNRS, former CERN Council President, who emphasised the importance of science in addressing global challenges such as climate change, health, and economic welfare. She highlighted the need for boldness, collaboration, and investment in research, stressing the importance of interdisciplinary approaches and the free circulation of scientific knowledge. Bassler celebrated European research milestones, such as the creation of CERN and the European Research Area, and discussed the socio-economic impact of research. She also underscored the necessity of maintaining high ethical standards and the critical role of science in fostering peace and societal trust.

Tackling Contemporary Challenges

The afternoon featured a series of thought-provoking panels addressing the pressing issues in research today. The first panel, moderated by Erzsébet Toth-Czifra, CoARA programme manager and Julia Boman, Grant evaluation partnerships manager at ESF, delved into “Addressing New Challenges in the Assessment of Research Proposals.” The panellists, including Jean-Emmanuel Faure from the European Commission, Rosemary Deem from Royal Holloway University of London and Olivier Boehme, FWO, shared their perspectives on enhancing evaluation processes to better meet contemporary demands.

The discussion continued with a panel on “Sustained Infrastructures for European Research.” Moderated by Oguz Ozkan coordinator of the Research infrastructure cluster at ESF, experts Jana Kolar from CERIC, Thomas Ruhtz from EUFAR, and Nigel Mason from the University of Kent explored the importance of robust research infrastructures in fostering long-term scientific progress.

The last session was the panel on “Embedding Inclusivity in Science,” moderated by Ildi Ipolyi, coordinator of the Inclusive science cluster at ESF. This session featured insightful contributions from Gitte Kragh of Aarhus University related to inclusion of citizens, Andjela Pepic from Banja Luka University on gender equality, and Veikko Ikonen from VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland on research ethics. The panellists emphasized the critical need for inclusivity and diversity in research to ensure that science benefits all sectors of society.

Concluding Insights and Networking

The event wrapped up with key messages from Alain Beretz of the University of Strasbourg. His reflections summarised the day’s discussions and highlighted the overarching theme of sustainable science management. The conference concluded with a networking reception, where attendees had the opportunity to further discuss ideas and celebrate ESF’s 50th anniversary!

A Lasting Impact

ESF’s 50th-anniversary event was not just a celebration of the past but a forward-looking conference that addressed the evolving challenges in research management. By bringing together a diverse group of stakeholders, the event exemplified ESF’s commitment to fostering a collaborative and inclusive research environment. As ESF moves into its next 50 years, it continues to catalyse impactful research, ensuring that science remains responsive to societal needs and sustainable for future generations.

TITLE: High Energy and Particle Theory

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The goal of high-energy and particle theory research in the MIT Center for Theoretical Physics — a Leinweber Institute (CTP-LI) is to enable discoveries of physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM), both through precision tests of the Standard Model itself and through detailed studies of possible new phenomena. With the momentous discovery of the Higgs boson at the Large Hadron Collider in 2012, the Standard Model of particle physics is now complete, yet its shortcomings loom larger than ever. For example, the Standard Model cannot account for the nature and origin of dark matter, nor does it address the puzzling hierarchy between the electroweak and Planck scales. On cosmological scales, questions remain about what drives the accelerating expansion of the universe, both today and during the inflationary epoch.

For this reason, high-energy and particle theorists in the CTP-LI are developing new theoretical frameworks to address physics in and beyond the Standard Model. The current effort in the CTP-LI includes research that has a direct impact on experiments as well as research that pursues more formal theoretical directions. CTP-LI researchers study possible new physics signatures at dark matter detection experiments, cosmological observatories, accelerators like the Large Hadron Collider, high intensity experiments, and small-scale table-top devices. At the same time, research in particle theory offers opportunities to push the boundaries of knowledge in quantum field theory (QFT), and innovations and creativity in QFT has long been a theme that unites the research conducted in the CTP-LI.

The CTP-LI has a long history of leadership in high-energy and particle theory. Emeritus faculty Dan Freedman, Jeffrey Goldstone, and Roman Jackiw are responsible for some of the fundamental theoretical ideas – especially those associated with symmetries and symmetry breaking – which lie at the heart of the Standard Model and its extensions. Frank Wilczek is one of the authors of the Standard Model and a pioneer in the study of axions and anyons, with long-standing interests in unification and supersymmetry. Eddie Farhi and Robert Jaffe have taken techniques developed in particle theory and applied them to the fields of quantum computation and fluctuation physics, respectively. Tracy Slatyer and Jesse Thaler represent the next generation of particle theorists, whose work draws on experimental and theoretical developments in areas ranging from dark matter detection to quantum chromodynamics to formal supergravity.

Successful high-energy and particle theorists have an appreciation and understanding of experimental and observational methods. The CTP-LI prides itself on maintaining close connections to experimental research conducted in the Laboratory for Nuclear Science and the MIT Kavli Institute for Astrophysics and Space Research.

Dark Matter and BSM Model Building

Dark matter is a key research direction in the CTP-LI, bridging particle physics and astroparticle physics (see Cosmology page). The gravitational evidence for dark matter is overwhelming, but the nature and origin of dark matter is still unknown. The two leading paradigms for dark matter are axions and massive stable relics (possibly of supersymmetric origin), but given the lack of any conclusive dark matter signals to date, CTP-LI researchers are taking imaginative approaches to dark matter and its potential signatures. Jesse Thaler and Tracy Slatyer have developed innovative models for dark matter in the context of expanded “dark sectors”, where the dark matter interacts with other new particles and forces. These scenarios can produce new and unexpected signals in Earth-based experiments – at particle accelerator laboratories or underground neutrino detectors – as well as in astrophysical and cosmological data. Jesse Thaler proposed the original idea for the ABRACADABRA experiment searching for ultralight axion dark matter, which is led by Lindley Winslow of the Laboratory for Nuclear Science. Iain Stewart and Tracy Slatyer are collaborating to apply powerful techniques from effective field theory, originally developed to study physics at the Large Hadron Collider, to the case of signals from heavy colliding dark matter particles.

ABRACADABRA-10 cm Axion Experiment. Credit: Jonathan L. Ouellet et al. Phys. Rev. D99:052012 (2019), arXiv:1901.10652

QCD and Collider Physics

Jet physics is an area of continued importance for particle phenomenology, especially at hadron colliders like the LHC. Jets are collimated sprays of particles that arise when quarks and gluons are produced at high energies, and copious jet production is a potential smoking gun for various scenarios beyond the Standard Model. Jesse Thaler has been at the forefront of the emerging field of jet substructure, developing new jet analysis techniques to capitalize on the exceptional ability of the LHC experiments to resolve jet constituents. These jet substructure methods can enhance BSM signals above Standard Model backgrounds, and they are currently being implemented in new physics searches by the MIT CMS pp group. These methods have also revealed fascinating new insights into the dynamics of QCD at high energies. Iain Stewart and Jesse Thaler have developed new techniques to perform precision jet calculations, capitalizing on recent development in applying resummation techniques to hadronic collisions. Jet substructure has offered new probes of the phenomena of jet quenching in the quark/gluon plasma, an area of considerable interest to the MIT CMS heavy ion group. More recently, machine learning techniques have offered new ways to disentangle and visualize jet properties.

Energy Flow Networks. Credit: Patrick T. Komiske, Eric M. Metodiev, and Jesse Thaler. JHEP 1901:121 (2019), arXiv:1810.05165.

Higgs Precision Physics

Higgs physics is another area of continued importance, especially with plans for precision Higgs measurements at the high-luminosity LHC and at possible future colliders. Percent-level measurements of the Higgs boson couplings are needed to test the Higgs boson’s role in generating fundamental particle masses. Frank Wilczek has long emphasized that BSM scenarios such as supersymmetry predict small deviations in these couplings as well as additional Higgs particles. Frank Wilczek and Jesse Thaler have shown how the Higgs boson and related Higgs-like states can act as the portal to dark matter. The connection between Higgs physics and BSM physics remains an active area of research. Precision calculations are crucial for studying the detailed characteristics of the Higgs boson, and Iain Stewart has applied effective field theory methods to calculate key Higgs cross sections and thus reduce theory uncertainties in Higgs measurements. Other areas of precision investigations in the CTP-LI include electroweak effects, CP violation, and flavor physics.

Higgs to Two Photons. Credit: © 2020 CERN, for the benefit of the CMS Collaboration

Quantum Field Theory

Particle theory also connects to more formal developments in QFT (as well as string theory). Almost all collider studies involve the calculation of scattering amplitudes, but independent of collider applications, scattering amplitudes themselves have a rich mathematical structure with hidden symmetries. Iain Stewart’s work with effective fields theories has enabled advances in this area, particularly for results beyond the leading order in collinear and soft limits. Supersymmetry is a hypothetical extension of space-time that introduces additional “quantum” dimensions, and many QFT properties are easier to understand in a supersymmetric context. Inspired by potential LHC signatures of supersymmetry, Jesse Thaler has shown that the dynamics of supersymmetry breaking can be richer than previously thought, leading to new results in formal supergravity. Strong dynamics is a feature of many extensions of the Standard Model, and one can gain some analytic handles on these scenarios by treating them as if they were conformal field theories (i.e. special QFTs with a scaling symmetry). Conformal field theories may also be relevant for understanding jet physics, since the interactions of quarks and gluons can sometimes be approximated as having a scaling symmetry. A new understanding of symmetry in quantum field theory is being developed by a combination of high-energy and condensed matter theorists, leading to an improved understanding of phase transitions, anomalies, and strongly-coupled dynamics. Daniel Harlow has made several contributions to this field, including the discovery of a new order parameter for confinement/deconfinement transitions, an improved understanding of the dynamics of the neutral pion in the standard model, and a proof that internal global symmetries which act in nonunitary representations on fields must be spontaneously broken. More generally, techniques developed in particle theory have the potential to offer new insights in other fields.

Courtesy of Jesse Thaler

TITLE: UNC Chapel Hill PhD in Public Policy 2027: Applications Open for Doctoral Study in the United States

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are open for the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill PhD in Public Policy for Fall 2027, offering prospective doctoral students an opportunity to pursue advanced interdisciplinary study and research focused on some of the most significant domestic and global public policy challenges.

Offered through UNC Public Policy in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, the PhD program is designed for students who want to contribute new knowledge, conduct rigorous policy research, and develop theoretical and analytical approaches that can help address complex public problems.

The program combines foundations in theory, empirical research, normative analysis, economics, political science, research design, statistics and specialized policy study. Students can develop expertise across a broad range of fields, including education, innovation and entrepreneurship, labor markets, health and social policy, immigration, environmental policy, national security, international development and global health.

Importantly for prospective applicants, GRE scores will not be required or reviewed for the Fall 2027 admissions cycle.

The application deadline for Fall 2027 admission is December 1, 2026.

About the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, commonly known as UNC-Chapel Hill or UNC, is located in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States.

The PhD in Public Policy is housed within UNC Public Policy in the university’s College of Arts and Sciences. The department combines perspectives from multiple social science disciplines to train researchers capable of analyzing important public policy questions.

UNC Public Policy’s doctoral program has approximately 30 students actively pursuing PhD degrees across a variety of policy interests. Graduate students work closely with faculty members on policy-relevant research and receive extensive training in the theoretical, methodological and substantive foundations necessary for advanced public policy scholarship.

About the UNC PhD in Public Policy

The UNC PhD in Public Policy is intended for students who want to develop new knowledge about major domestic and global policy problems and contribute to solving them through rigorous research.

The program brings together multiple academic disciplines. Its coursework incorporates areas including:

Economics

Political science

Philosophy and normative analysis

Research design

Statistics and quantitative methods

Public policy theory

Specialized substantive policy fields

Students ultimately undertake doctoral research intended to create new knowledge, social science theory and/or methods that can contribute to understanding significant domestic and international public policy challenges.

Graduates are prepared for careers that can include academic appointments, policy research positions, government roles and other positions requiring advanced policy analysis and research expertise.

Policy Areas Students Can Explore

One of the important features of the UNC Public Policy PhD is the ability for doctoral students to build expertise around their individual policy interests.

Potential areas identified by UNC Public Policy include:

Education

Innovation and entrepreneurship

Labor markets

Health policy

Social policy

Immigration

Environmental policy

National security

International development

Global health

Rather than limiting every doctoral student to the same substantive specialization, the program combines a common methodological and theoretical foundation with an individualized policy field.

Students therefore receive broad training in public policy analysis while developing specialized expertise appropriate to their research interests and future careers.

Who Is the PhD Program Designed For?

The program is particularly relevant to applicants interested in becoming researchers, academics and policy professionals capable of conducting independent scholarly research.

UNC states that students enter its doctoral program from diverse backgrounds in academic preparation and experience, and that this diversity is welcomed and encouraged.

Although the supplied program requirements do not establish calculus, microeconomics and statistics as admission prerequisites, UNC explains that students who have successfully completed:

A first course in calculus

Introductory microeconomics

Introductory statistics

will be best prepared for the program’s core curriculum.

All entering students are also required to take PLCY 800, which provides mathematical preparation for economic and statistical analysis.

Structure of the UNC PhD in Public Policy

The doctoral program follows a structured progression from coursework and field specialization to independent research and dissertation completion.

Broadly, students must:

Define a policy field.

Successfully complete core and policy-field coursework.

Receive a passing grade on a field paper written examination.

Orally defend a dissertation proposal.

Orally defend the completed dissertation.

Each stage must be successfully completed before the student proceeds to the next stage.

This progression is designed to move students from foundational doctoral training toward increasingly independent research.

PhD Coursework Requirements

UNC Public Policy requires PhD students to complete 44 credit hours of coursework, consisting of:

26 credit hours of core courses

18 credit hours in a self-defined substantive policy field

Students generally undertake two years of full-time coursework. Graduate courses previously completed elsewhere that duplicate required courses may potentially be considered, with students able to petition the Director of Graduate Studies to have up to nine such hours counted toward the PhD, subject to program approval.

Core Academic Training

The core curriculum provides extensive preparation across politics, institutions, economics, ethics, research design and quantitative methods.

Core courses include:

PLCY 816 – Politics and Public Policy Theory

PLCY 817 – Institutional Analysis for Public Policy

PLCY 880 – Normative Dimensions of Public Policy

PLCY 888 – Advanced Economic Analysis for Public Policy I

PLCY 889 – Advanced Economic Analysis for Public Policy II

PLCY 801 – Design of Policy Research

PLCY 810 – Public Policy Seminar

PLCY 881 / HPM 881 – Linear Regression Models

PLCY 882 / HPM 882 – Advanced Panel Data Methodology for Public Policy

Together, these core courses account for 26 credit hours.

Mathematical Preparation

Students entering the program take PLCY 800 Math Camp, an intensive preparation course covering mathematical and statistical analysis relevant to economics and public policy.

Topics include:

Linear algebra

Calculus

Optimization

Mathematical statistics

The course prepares students for advanced economic analysis and quantitative methods courses.

Individual Policy Field Specialization

In addition to the common core curriculum, every doctoral student develops an individualized substantive policy field.

Students work with their academic advisor and relevant faculty members to begin defining their field and planning their coursework during their first year.

UNC defines a field as a recognized substantive area of public policy research supported by a coherent body of scholarly literature. The specialization should be sufficiently broad to support a longer-term career in research and teaching rather than being narrowly constructed around a single dissertation topic.

The policy specialization requires 18 credit hours, normally consisting of:

At least 3 credit hours in research methods

At least 9 credit hours in theory and substantive policy content

Normally 6 credit hours of doctoral dissertation research through PLCY 994

Students can draw on appropriate graduate-level courses at UNC and neighboring universities, subject to program requirements and approval.

Research and Teaching Experience

The doctoral experience extends beyond classroom study.

According to the program’s illustrative course sequencing, many PhD students hold teaching or research assistantship responsibilities of approximately 20 hours per week while completing their studies.

Students holding such positions are required to maintain full-time student status.

This provides an environment in which doctoral students can combine advanced academic study with research or teaching experience.

Prospective applicants should note, however, that the information supplied does not state that an assistantship is automatically guaranteed to every admitted student.

Academic Advising

Each admitted student is assigned a primary academic advisor upon entering the program.

Students may nominate a member of the Public Policy core faculty to serve as their program advisor, and the advisor is generally expected to teach or conduct research in an area related to the student’s prospective specialization.

The advisor supports the student’s academic development throughout the doctoral program.

Academic progress is also formally reviewed. Advisors are expected to meet students regularly and at least once per semester, while the Director of Graduate Studies conducts annual progress reviews.

Field Paper Written Examination

An important milestone in the UNC Public Policy PhD is the field paper written examination.

The examination evaluates a student’s ability to undertake significant independent academic work.

The field paper must be solo-authored and can take forms recognized within public policy scholarship, including:

Quantitative empirical research

Qualitative empirical research

Critical literature review

Normative analysis

Theoretical analysis

Methodological research

The paper must be a substantial work of at least 30 double-spaced pages, excluding tables, figures and references.

It should demonstrate the student’s capacity for independent scholarly activity and meaningfully advance their engagement with their chosen policy field.

Students generally begin planning their field paper during their second year and are expected to defend it orally during the fall semester of their third year.

Dissertation Research

Students who successfully progress through the field paper stage move toward their dissertation proposal.

The dissertation must make an original scholarly contribution to a substantive area of public policy.

Students are expected to identify a research question with theoretical and/or policy relevance, connect the research to existing scholarship, and employ methods appropriate to the research problem.

Dissertations may use:

Quantitative research

Qualitative research

Mixed-methods research

The research should ultimately contribute to public policy scholarship, research or practice.

The dissertation proposal is developed in collaboration with the student’s advisor and committee and must eventually be defended orally.

After completing the research and dissertation, the student must undertake a final oral examination. The examination primarily focuses on defending the research and writing contained in the dissertation, although questions may also connect the dissertation to the broader field of public policy.

Time Available to Complete the PhD

Under UNC regulations, PhD students have a maximum of eight calendar years from their first Graduate School registration to complete their doctoral degree.

The program also has residency requirements, including a minimum of four semesters of residency, with at least two earned through continuous registration on the UNC campus.

UNC also notes that students are not guaranteed funding beyond their fifth year.

Applicants should therefore consider both the academic and financial implications of a multi-year doctoral commitment when preparing to apply.

The Hammer Fund for the Enrichment of the PhD Curriculum in Public Policy

UNC Public Policy also highlights the Philip and Jane Hammer Fund for the Enrichment of the PhD Curriculum in Public Policy.

Established in 1991 by Jane R. Hammer, the fund supports the recruitment and support of exceptional graduate students in the Public Policy PhD program.

Prospective applicants interested in funding should review current UNC Public Policy and Graduate School funding information carefully to determine what support may be available for their admission cycle.

Career Opportunities After the UNC Public Policy PhD

The program is designed to prepare graduates for careers requiring sophisticated research, policy analysis and subject-matter expertise.

UNC Public Policy reports that its doctoral graduates have obtained positions in:

Universities and academic institutions

Policy research organizations

Government agencies

Public-sector organizations

Private-sector organizations

Non-profit organizations

The program’s mission specifically emphasizes preparing graduates to hold academic positions, conduct policy research useful to decision-makers, and advance knowledge within public policy and their chosen substantive fields.

Fall 2027 Admission Requirements

Prospective students applying for Fall 2027 admission must complete the UNC Graduate School application and select Public Policy as their intended program.

According to UNC Public Policy’s admissions instructions, applicants are required to provide supplemental application materials including:

1. Statement of Purpose

Applicants must submit a Statement of Purpose as part of the online application.

This is an important component of a doctoral application and provides applicants with an opportunity to explain their academic and research interests and reasons for pursuing advanced study in public policy.

2. Three Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must provide three letters of recommendation.

UNC specifies that at least two should normally come from faculty members familiar with the applicant’s academic ability.

For applicants who have accumulated substantial professional experience after college, letters from individuals capable of describing the applicant’s potential to succeed in doctoral-level work may be substituted.

GRE Is Not Required for Fall 2027

A particularly important point for applicants is that GRE scores will not be required or reviewed for the 2027 admissions cycle.

Applicants therefore do not need to submit GRE scores for consideration under the stated Fall 2027 Public Policy admissions requirements.

English Language Requirements for International Applicants

The program is open to international applicants, but applicants subject to UNC’s international English-language testing requirements need to pay close attention to the accepted tests.

According to the admissions information provided, international applicants must submit acceptable official scores from either:

TOEFL, reported directly from ETS; or

IELTS, reported directly from IELTS.

UNC states that no other English-language tests are accepted under these requirements.

The stated minimum total scores are:

Internet-based TOEFL: 90

IELTS: 7

International applicants should review UNC Graduate School’s complete international applicant instructions to determine how these testing rules apply to their individual circumstances.

Application Deadline for Fall 2027

The application deadline for the UNC Chapel Hill PhD in Public Policy for Fall 2027 admission is:

December 1, 2026

Prospective applicants should not wait until the deadline to begin preparing their applications.

Doctoral applications require substantial preparation, particularly because applicants must coordinate recommendation letters, prepare a strong Statement of Purpose, gather academic information and, where applicable, arrange official TOEFL or IELTS scores.

International applicants should allow additional time for official English-language test reporting.

How to Apply for the UNC PhD in Public Policy 2027

Applications must be completed online through the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Graduate School.

Applicants should:

Visit the UNC Graduate School degree programs/application website.

Locate and select Public Policy from the relevant program options.

Complete the online graduate application.

Upload the required Statement of Purpose.

Arrange for three Letters of Recommendation.

Complete all additional Graduate School application requirements.

If applicable, arrange for official TOEFL or IELTS scores to be submitted according to UNC’s instructions.

Review the application carefully for completeness.

Submit the completed application by December 1, 2026.

Application/Program Information:

https://publicpolicy.unc.edu/admissions/

UNC Graduate School:

https://gradschool.unc.edu/academics/degreeprograms/

Applicants should always review the official Graduate School and UNC Public Policy pages before submitting an application because university requirements, procedures and supporting documentation may be subject to change.

Important Considerations Before Applying

A PhD is a substantial academic commitment, and prospective applicants should carefully consider whether the UNC Public Policy program aligns with their research interests and career objectives.

Potential applicants may particularly want to evaluate:

How their proposed research interests align with UNC Public Policy faculty expertise.

Which substantive policy field they might eventually pursue.

Their preparation in quantitative methods, statistics, economics and research design.

Their readiness for intensive doctoral-level research.

Their long-term academic, policy or research career objectives.

Funding arrangements and the expected duration of doctoral study.

English-language testing requirements if applying internationally.

The availability of faculty members whose research overlaps with their intended specialization.

Because doctoral education involves close collaboration with academic advisors and faculty committees, research alignment can be an important consideration when evaluating a PhD program.

APPLY NOW

Contact for Questions About the Application

Applicants with questions concerning application requirements or the admissions process can contact the Student Services representative listed by UNC Public Policy:

Meredith Albright

Student Services

The PhD Program, UNC Public Policy

University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

Campus Box #3435, Abernethy Hall

Chapel Hill, NC 27599-3435

United States

Email: merealb@unc.edu

Telephone: (919) 962-1600

Conclusion

The UNC Chapel Hill PhD in Public Policy 2027 provides an opportunity for aspiring scholars, researchers and policy professionals to undertake rigorous interdisciplinary doctoral training at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

Through a combination of public policy theory, economics, political science, normative analysis, research design, quantitative methods and individualized policy specialization, the program is structured to prepare students to conduct independent research addressing important domestic and global policy problems.

Students progress from intensive coursework to a specialized policy field, an independent field paper, a dissertation proposal and ultimately an original doctoral dissertation. The ability to develop expertise in areas ranging from education and labor markets to health, immigration, environmental policy, international development and global health gives students considerable scope to align their doctoral training with their long-term research interests.

The absence of a GRE requirement for the Fall 2027 admissions cycle may also make the application process more accessible to prospective candidates. International applicants can apply, although those subject to English-language testing requirements must meet UNC’s TOEFL or IELTS requirements.

Prospective students interested in research-intensive careers in academia, government, policy organizations, non-profits or related fields should carefully review the program, identify potential areas of research alignment and begin preparing their application well before the deadline.

Applications for Fall 2027 admission must be submitted by December 1, 2026.

TITLE: Demographics & Planetary Health Story Prize 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: October 9, 2026

Applications are open for the Demographics & Planetary Health Story Prize 2026. The Demographic & Planetary Health Story Prize contest is designed to recognize original published journalism that connects demographic change to planetary health, whether through population dynamics, reproductive health, migration, climate, or the economic and geopolitical forces tying them together.

Hosted by the Johns Hopkins Institute for Planetary Health and the Planetary Health Alliance, the Hopkins Population Center, and the William H. Gates Sr. Institute for Population and Reproductive Health at Johns Hopkins University, this prize takes a wider lens and seeks to honor all types of reporting, journalism, and content creation that reaches outside a typical sector audience.

Categories

Print, Podcast, Digital News, & Newsletters: This category is for journalists or reporters who take a more traditional approach to journalism, whether self-publishing or publishing for a recognized media outlet.

Social Media, Blogs, & Video: This category is for content creators who utilize social networks or personally-driven content outlets to engage their audiences.

Prize

An award of $500 will be given in each category.

Eligibility

Open to journalists, freelancers, community reporters, and student journalists reporting for a digital, print or social outlet.

Submissions from NGO or organizational blogs are not eligible.

Submissions to the Demographic & Planetary Health Story Prize should engage substantively with the intersection of demographics and planetary health.

Examples might include (but not limited to):

Population trends and their environmental or health consequences

Migration driven by climate or resource pressure

Reproductive health access in the context of environmental change

Solutions and innovations to mitigate forced migration

Energy/urbanization, designing cities that meet demographic trends

Impacts of rising heat levels and increased pollution on maternal health

Climate impacts on marginalized populations and gender disparities

Evaluation Criteria

Originality and rigor: Is the reporting sourced beyond press releases and does it bring new information or framing to the topic?

Clarity of the demographics–planetary health connection: Does the story make that link legible to a general audience, not just specialists?

Craft: Is the writing well structured, and does it use data or visual storytelling effectively?

Potential for impact: Is the piece likely to reach and inform readers who wouldn’t otherwise encounter this topic?​

Substantive power of the piece: Does the reporting surface something that moves the conversation forward?

Application

The Demographic & Planetary Health Story Prize accepts submissions in multiple formats, including:

Published or broadcast news stories

Features or op-eds

Explanatory pieces

Short-form documentary or audio pieces
