TITLE: Resilience Fund for Women 2026 Grants: Apply for Up to $50,000 in Flexible Funding for Women-Led Climate Resilience Organizations

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Resilience Fund for Women has opened a new 2026 funding round offering US$15,000 to US$50,000 in flexible, unrestricted grants to eligible women- and non-binary-led community-based organizations working in Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, and Vietnam.

The funding is designed for grassroots and community-based organizations whose work connects three critical areas: women’s health, safety and economic resilience; community-led climate adaptation; and communities connected to global value chains.

Successful organizations will receive funding over a two-year period, giving them greater flexibility to strengthen existing programs, build institutional capacity, respond to changing community needs, deepen climate adaptation work, and invest in the long-term resilience of the women and communities they serve.

Unlike many conventional funding opportunities that require organizations to design an entirely new project, this funding is unrestricted. Applicants do not have to create a standalone project solely for the grant. Instead, selected organizations can use the funding to strengthen, expand, deepen, or adapt their existing work according to their organizational priorities and the needs of the communities they serve.

Phase 1 Application Deadline: 12 October 2026

Applications opened on 18 September 2026 and must be submitted through the official online application system. Organizations selected to proceed will be invited to a second application phase beginning around the end of October 2026, with final grant decisions expected in January 2027.

About the Resilience Fund for Women

The Resilience Fund brings together companies, foundations, women’s funds, civil society organizations, and women leaders to invest in the health, safety, wellbeing, economic resilience, and climate resilience of women and communities connected to global supply chains.

The Fund seeks to move resources and decision-making closer to women-led and community-based organizations that understand the realities facing their own communities.

Its funding model differs from many conventional philanthropic approaches because it emphasizes:

Flexible funding

Long-term organizational resilience

Trust-based philanthropy

Community leadership

Participatory grantmaking

Women’s leadership

Language accessibility

Shared learning

Community-led solutions

Collaborative approaches to defining and measuring impact

Rather than requiring grantees to follow rigid funding structures designed entirely by donors, the Fund aims to provide organizations with greater freedom to determine how resources can be used most effectively.

A Funding Model Focused on Local Women-Led Solutions

The Resilience Fund was developed around the principle that communities closest to social, economic, health, and environmental challenges are often best positioned to determine appropriate solutions.

The Fund therefore provides flexible, multi-year support that allows community organizations to respond to changing circumstances rather than being restricted to a narrow project plan.

This approach allows organizations to make decisions about where resources can create the greatest impact, including investing in organizational systems, staffing, existing programs, emerging priorities, or new approaches to climate adaptation.

The Fund also uses participatory grantmaking, bringing community representatives into the process of assessing applications and influencing funding decisions.

Funding Available Under the 2026 Resilience Fund Round

Eligible organizations may request between:

US$15,000 and US$50,000

in total funding.

All grants awarded during this funding cycle will cover a:

Two-year period.

The grants are intended to provide organizations with longer-term and flexible support rather than short-term emergency assistance.

Maximum Grant Relative to Organizational Revenue

An important rule applies to the size of the grant that an organization may request.

Applicants may request funding equivalent to up to 150% of their organization’s annual revenue, subject to the overall maximum grant of US$50,000.

For example, an organization with most recent annual revenue of US$20,000 could request up to:

US$30,000

because this represents 150% of its annual revenue.

Even if 150% of an organization’s revenue would exceed US$50,000, the maximum available grant remains US$50,000.

Organizations must have annual income of at least US$10,000 to qualify.

Income from 2024, 2025, or 2026 may be used as the baseline for determining eligibility.

Three Priority Areas for the 2026 Funding Round

The Resilience Fund is seeking organizations whose work brings together three interconnected areas.

Applicants should demonstrate that their work addresses all three areas, although they are not expected to have the same depth of experience in each one.

1. Women’s Health, Safety and Resilience

The first priority area concerns work that strengthens women’s overall wellbeing and their ability to participate fully in their workplaces and communities.

Relevant work may address areas such as:

Women’s health

Safety

Livelihoods

Financial security

Leadership

Decision-making

Mobility

Economic participation

Workplace wellbeing

Community participation

Resilience to economic or social shocks

The objective is to strengthen conditions that allow women to live safely, build economic security, exercise greater agency, and participate meaningfully in community and workplace life.

2. Community-Led Climate Adaptation

The second priority is work that helps women and their communities prepare for, respond to, and adapt to environmental and climate-related impacts.

Examples of relevant climate risks include:

Extreme heat

Flooding

Drought

Storms

Changing rainfall patterns

Changing weather conditions

Environmental degradation

Climate-related livelihood disruption

The Fund recognizes that climate impacts are not gender-neutral.

Environmental shocks can affect women disproportionately through changes in working conditions, health risks, safety, migration patterns, income security, care responsibilities, and access to essential services.

The Fund therefore aims to support locally designed climate adaptation strategies that place women and community leadership at the center of resilience building.

Organizations Do Not Need to Be Long-Established Climate Organizations

One particularly important aspect of this funding round is that applicants do not need many years of experience running formal climate programs.

Organizations that are still in the early stages of incorporating climate adaptation into their work may apply.

Applicants should, however, be able to demonstrate:

Some existing experience responding to environmental or climate impacts affecting their communities; and

An interest in strengthening or deepening climate adaptation within their work.

The Fund specifically states that applicants do not need to identify primarily as climate-focused organizations.

This provision may significantly broaden access to the funding for grassroots women’s rights, worker rights, health, economic empowerment, migration, safety, or community organizations that increasingly encounter climate-related challenges through their existing work.

3. Connection to Global Value Chains

The third essential component is a connection to global value chains.

For the purposes of this funding round, the Fund is particularly interested in organizations working with communities located in, near, or connected to businesses and workplaces producing products for global export.

These can include sectors involving:

Apparel

Food

Agriculture

Technology

Manufacturing

Other export-oriented industries

Relevant communities can include women who are:

Factory workers

Farm workers

Migrant workers

Informal workers

Gig workers

Organizations can also work with the families and communities surrounding these workers.

The Fund’s definition is intentionally broad.

Organizations do not necessarily have to work directly inside factories or formal workplaces. They may work in communities surrounding manufacturing or agricultural operations or in communities from which women migrate significant distances for employment.

Why Global Supply Chains Matter to the Fund

Millions of women across South and Southeast Asia participate directly or indirectly in global supply chains.

Their economic opportunities can be influenced by workplace safety, healthcare access, mobility, environmental conditions, gender-based violence, migration, extreme weather, and changing economic circumstances.

The Resilience Fund’s approach recognizes that improving women’s workforce participation cannot be separated from their health, safety, family wellbeing, community resilience, and ability to respond to climate risks.

Supporting women-led community organizations can therefore strengthen both individual workers and the broader communities upon which global value chains depend.

Who Can Apply?

The 2026 funding round is open to eligible:

Women- and non-binary-led, community-based, non-governmental organizations

operating in:

Bangladesh

Cambodia

India

Vietnam

Organizations must be formally registered and should be embedded in and representative of the communities they serve.

Applicants must also meet the Fund’s financial and regulatory requirements.

Organization Registration Requirements

Applicants must generally be:

Formally registered organizations

Non-governmental organizations

Community-based

Legally authorized to operate

Legally authorized to receive foreign funding

Organizations also need to comply with applicable government regulations governing foreign financial support.

Minimum Organizational Income

Applicant organizations must have annual income of at least:

US$10,000

The Fund may use income figures from 2024, 2025, or 2026 to assess this requirement.

Requirements for Women- and Non-Binary-Led Organizations

The Resilience Fund places women’s and non-binary leadership at the center of this funding cycle.

Its current eligibility guidance describes a women/non-binary-led organization as having a woman or non-binary Executive Director or CEO and at least 50% of staff identifying as women or non-binary.

The application page additionally describes its definition of a women-led organization as having a woman CEO or director and at least 50% of senior leadership positions held by women.

Organizations close to, but not obviously within, these definitions should carefully review the official application guidance. The Fund states that an organization that believes it is genuinely women-led despite not precisely matching the stated definition may provide supporting information for consideration.

Inclusive Understanding of Women

The Fund states that the term women includes women in all their diversity.

This encompasses, among others:

Women with disabilities

Women of diverse sexual orientations and gender identities

Women of color

Indigenous women

Women from oppressed castes

Younger women

Older women

Women affected by racism

Women affected by poverty

Migrant women

Women belonging to other marginalized communities

This reflects the Fund’s broader emphasis on intersectionality and community representation.

Foreign Funding Authorization Requirements

Organizations generally must possess the legal approvals necessary to receive foreign funding.

The Fund states that organizations without the required foreign funding authorization are generally not eligible.

Special Provision for Applicants in India Without FCRA Registration

There is an important exception affecting Indian applicants.

For eligible organizations in India without an existing Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) authorization, the Fund states that if the grant application is successful and the organization chooses to submit a prior-permission request to the Government of India, the Resilience Fund team can support the organization with that process.

Indian organizations should carefully review the official funding and FCRA requirements before applying.

Previous Resilience Fund Grantees Can Apply Again

Organizations that have already received funding from the Resilience Fund are allowed to apply during this round.

However, previous receipt of a grant does not guarantee future selection.

Returning organizations must:

Meet the current eligibility requirements

Submit a new application

Participate in the current selection process

Be evaluated alongside other eligible applicants

All proposals will be reviewed under the same selection process.

No New Standalone Project Is Required

Organizations do not need to design a completely new project to qualify for this funding opportunity.

This is one of the most important characteristics of the grant.

The funding can be used to:

Strengthen existing work

Deepen existing programs

Adapt existing interventions

Develop organizational capacity

Integrate climate adaptation more intentionally

Respond to changing community priorities

Strengthen internal systems

Support programmatic needs

Address institutional priorities

Applicants will be asked to explain how they expect to use the funding and what they hope the support will allow them to achieve.

What Does “Unrestricted Funding” Mean?

The Resilience Fund describes its grants as flexible and unrestricted.

This means selected organizations will have considerable discretion to determine where funding can best strengthen their organization and mission.

Funds may potentially support both:

Programmatic needs; and

Organizational needs.

Rather than requiring every dollar to be tied to a predetermined project budget, organizations can adjust the use of funding when circumstances or community needs change.

This type of funding is particularly valuable for smaller grassroots organizations, which often face difficulty obtaining funding for essential institutional costs.

Restrictions on Grant Funding

Although the grants are flexible, they are not completely without restrictions.

Grant funds cannot be used for:

Lobbying

Electioneering

Political campaigning

Microcredit

Microfinance

All grant funds must also be used in accordance with applicable national laws, foreign-funding regulations, and the terms of the final grant agreement.

Two-Phase Application Process

Applications will be assessed through a two-stage selection process.

This structure is intended partly to prevent smaller organizations from having to invest substantial time in a highly detailed proposal before knowing whether their application is competitive.

Phase 1: Initial Application

Opening Date: 18 September 2026

Deadline: 12 October 2026

Organizations submit an initial application containing the information required to determine eligibility and assess alignment with the Fund’s priorities.

Applications will then undergo screening and review.

A selected group of organizations will be invited to continue to Phase 2.

Phase 2: Detailed Application

Phase 2 is expected to:

Open: End of October 2026

Close: Mid-November 2026

Organizations invited to this stage will provide more detailed information regarding:

Their organization

Their work

Programmatic activities

Proposed use of grant funding

Relevant organizational and program details

Organizations invited to Phase 2 are expected to be notified by the end of October 2026.

Final Funding Decisions

Final grant decisions are expected to be communicated in:

January 2027

All applicants will be informed of the final funding decision.

Organizations selected for funding will then proceed through additional due diligence.

This can include:

Additional organizational information

Reference checks

Compliance review

Grant documentation

Signing a grant agreement

The exact grant-processing timeline may differ according to legal and regulatory requirements in each country.

Participatory Grantmaking Process

A distinctive element of the Resilience Fund is its approach to deciding which organizations receive funding.

Instead of leaving grant decisions entirely to conventional donor staff, the Fund uses participatory grantmaking.

Eligible proposals progressing through the process are reviewed with involvement from community representatives and peer reviewers.

Peer Panelists can include:

Local gender activists

Labor activists

Value-chain experts

Representatives familiar with relevant communities

The Fund states that final grantmaking decisions are made through collaborative workshops involving Peer Panelists, Advisory Board members, and members of the Fund’s operations team.

The intention is to give people with community knowledge and lived experience a meaningful role in deciding how financial resources are distributed.

Learning Hub for Successful Grantees

Organizations selected for funding will also join the Resilience Fund Learning Hub.

The Learning Hub is designed to connect:

Grantee organizations

Corporate investors

Women’s funds

Community organizations

Civil society organizations

Fund stakeholders

Participants can share experiences, examine challenges, exchange resources, identify lessons, and create new professional relationships.

Over the two-year grant period, grantee organizations are expected to participate in approximately three to four virtual meetings with other grantees, investors, and Fund stakeholders.

Translation and other support are intended to help participants communicate as much as possible in their preferred languages.

Reporting Requirements

The Fund states that reporting for selected grantees will be intentionally light-touch.

Rather than imposing an identical set of fixed indicators on every organization, the Fund plans to collaboratively develop metrics and learning priorities with its grantee partners.

This recognizes that organizations:

Operate in different contexts

Address different community priorities

May define impact differently

May require different approaches to measuring progress

The Fund therefore emphasizes learning and useful information rather than imposing unnecessarily burdensome reporting systems.

Application Language

The final application must be submitted in:

English

However, applicants can access free application and language assistance.

Support is available in languages including:

Bengali/Bangla

Hindi

Tamil

Khmer

Vietnamese

Odia

Marathi

Support can include assistance with translating application responses and submitting the application.

The Fund states that applicants who receive language or application assistance will be assessed in the same way as applicants who complete their applications without such support.

Application Support Contacts

Applicants from India and Bangladesh can seek application assistance through the support arrangements listed on the Fund’s official page.

Applicants from Vietnam and Cambodia can similarly access language and application support through the Resilience Fund.

Candidates should consult the official application page for the latest support contact information and translated application materials.

Informational Webinar

The Resilience Fund has scheduled an informational webinar for:

30 September 2026 at 8:30 a.m. EST

Prospective applicants can register through the link provided on the official funding page.

Organizations considering an application may benefit from attending the webinar, particularly if they have questions about eligibility, grant size, climate adaptation requirements, unrestricted funding, or the application process.

Applications Must Be Submitted Online

The Resilience Fund will accept only applications submitted through its official online portal.

Applications cannot be submitted:

By email

On paper

Through alternative offline arrangements

Applicants with connectivity problems are encouraged to seek application support.

Applicants Can Save Their Progress

Organizations do not have to complete the online application in a single session.

The online system allows users to save progress and return later using the same email address.

The Fund recommends drafting application answers in a separate document before copying them into the application system.

This can reduce the risk of losing work because of connectivity or browser problems.

Application Confirmation

After successfully submitting an application, applicants should receive an email containing confirmation and a copy of their submitted responses.

The Fund asks applicants not to submit multiple applications for the same organization.

What Happens If Your Organization Is Selected?

Successful organizations will undergo a short due-diligence process.

This can include:

Verification of organizational information

Reference checks

Regulatory review

Completion of grant documentation

Once due diligence has been completed, successful organizations will receive a formal grant agreement.

After signing the agreement, grantee partners will be introduced to the Resilience Fund’s Learning Hub through an orientation process.

The Fund also plans individual conversations with participating organizations to understand:

How they define impact

What they want to learn

Their organizational objectives

Their learning priorities

The Resilience Fund’s Track Record

The Fund has already developed a substantial portfolio of support for women-led and community-focused organizations.

Since 2021, the Resilience Fund reports investing approximately US$4.27 million in 66 direct and indirect grantee partners, primarily in Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, and Vietnam.

Its grantees work with groups including:

Industrial workers

Agricultural workers

Migrants

Children and families of workers

Formal workers

Informal workers

Community members

The Fund evaluates its broader impact across organizational resilience, learning, and philanthropy.

Why This Funding Opportunity Is Different

The Resilience Fund’s 2026 funding round stands out because it combines several features that are often difficult for grassroots organizations to find in a single funding opportunity.

These include:

Two years of funding

Flexible and unrestricted support

Grants of up to US$50,000

Support for existing work rather than only new projects

Opportunities for relatively early-stage climate-adaptation organizations

Community-led decision-making

Participatory grantmaking

Language support

Reduced reporting burden

Organizational development support

Peer learning

Connections with other grantees and investors

The combination is intended to strengthen not only individual projects but also the organizations delivering them.

Key Dates at a Glance

Phase 1 Opens: 18 September 2026

Informational Webinar: 30 September 2026

Phase 1 Application Deadline: 12 October 2026

Phase 2 Opens: End of October 2026

Phase 2 Deadline: Mid-November 2026

Final Funding Decisions: January 2027

Grant Duration: Two years

Grant Amount: US$15,000–US$50,000

How to Apply for the Resilience Fund for Women 2026 Grant

Organizations interested in applying should first carefully review the full eligibility requirements.

Applicants are encouraged to download the application form in advance and prepare their responses before beginning the online submission.

The recommended process is:

Confirm that the organization operates in Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, or Vietnam.

Confirm that it satisfies the women/non-binary leadership requirements.

Confirm formal NGO registration.

Check foreign-funding authorization requirements.

Confirm annual organizational income of at least US$10,000.

Confirm that the organization’s work relates to women’s health, safety, and resilience.

Demonstrate existing or emerging work on community-led climate adaptation.

Demonstrate a connection with communities involved in global value chains.

Review the application questions in advance.

Prepare responses offline.

Submit the Phase 1 application through the official online portal before 12 October 2026.

Only applications submitted through the online application portal will be considered.

Official Funding Information and Application:

https://www.resiliencefundforwomen.org/apply

Conclusion

The Resilience Fund for Women 2026 funding round represents a major opportunity for women- and non-binary-led grassroots organizations in Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, and Vietnam that are working at the intersection of women’s wellbeing, climate resilience, and global supply-chain communities.

Selected organizations can receive between US$15,000 and US$50,000 in flexible, unrestricted funding over two years, giving them the ability to strengthen their existing programs and institutions rather than being forced to create a new standalone project solely to satisfy donor requirements.

The Fund is particularly relevant for organizations working with women workers, migrant communities, informal workers, factory communities, agricultural workers, and communities affected by increasing climate and environmental risks.

Its participatory grantmaking structure, flexible funding model, Learning Hub, language support, and light-touch reporting system distinguish it from more conventional project-based funding opportunities.

Organizations do not need decades of experience in climate programming. Groups beginning to integrate climate adaptation into existing work are explicitly encouraged to apply if they can demonstrate some experience responding to climate or environmental challenges and a commitment to deepening this work.

Interested organizations should review the eligibility conditions carefully and submit their Phase 1 application through the official portal no later than 12 October 2026.

TITLE: Amazon Solutions Architect Intern, AWSI – 2027

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is offering a Solutions Architect Intern opportunity for students interested in cloud computing, software development, machine learning, analytics, security, DevOps, and related technical fields.

The internship is a 12-week, full-time program based in Dallas, Texas, or Seattle, Washington, where interns will receive AWS technical training, mentorship, and hands-on experience working on real customer and business challenges.

Opportunity Overview

Position: Solutions Architect Intern, AWSI – 2027

Company: Amazon Web Services, Inc.

Job ID: 10550494

Location: Dallas, TX or Seattle, WA

Duration: 12 consecutive weeks

Work Schedule: Full-time, up to 40 hours per week

Program Format: Cohort-based

Tentative Start Dates: May 24 or June 21

Degree Level: Bachelor’s degree or higher

Expected Graduation: December 2027 – September 2028

About the Amazon Solutions Architect Internship

The Solutions Architect Intern role is designed for students who want to understand how technology can be used to solve real-world customer and business problems.

During the internship, participants will learn how to design and architect solutions using the AWS Cloud while developing both technical and interpersonal skills.

Interns will work alongside experienced AWS professionals and receive guidance as they learn how to approach cloud architecture, customer engagement, and technology implementation.

The program combines:

Technical training

Mentorship

Cloud computing education

Customer engagement

Hands-on projects

Software and architecture development

Professional development

What Will You Learn?

The internship’s three-month mentorship program is designed to help participants develop practical Solutions Architect skills.

Participants will:

Learn how to architect solutions on AWS.

Develop skills for leading customer engagements.

Work alongside experienced Solutions Architects and other professionals.

Gain practical experience with AWS services.

Learn how to translate customer problems into technical requirements.

Develop technical and business knowledge.

Gain experience communicating with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

As a Solutions Architect Intern, you may be responsible for helping develop solutions to customer problems and supporting the adoption of AWS services.

Designing Solutions

Interns will work on solutions that address customer business challenges and help customers adopt AWS technologies.

This means understanding the customer’s needs and considering how AWS services can be combined to create an appropriate technical solution.

Working With Customers

The role involves interaction with both internal and external customers.

You may communicate with:

Developers

Technical teams

Team leads

Business stakeholders

Other AWS professionals

Strong communication and interpersonal skills are therefore an important part of the position.

Translating Customer Feedback

Interns will also learn how to gather useful feedback from customers and transform that feedback into clear:

Business requirements

Technical requirements

Product requirements

Engineering requirements

This helps connect customer needs with the teams responsible for developing products and technical solutions.

What Does a Typical Internship Day Look Like?

The internship is designed around practical experience rather than only classroom learning.

During the program, interns may:

Work on Real Business Challenges

Participants can engage directly with actual business problems and learn how technology can be used to address them.

Build on AWS

Interns gain hands-on experience working with the AWS Cloud and applying AWS services to practical situations.

Apply Architecture Best Practices

Participants will learn how established cloud architecture principles can be applied when designing solutions.

Solve Customer Problems

The program emphasizes working backwards from customer needs.

Rather than simply starting with a technology and looking for somewhere to use it, interns learn to understand the problem first and then develop an appropriate solution.

Work With Mentors

Interns work with experienced professionals who provide guidance throughout the program.

This mentorship is intended to help participants develop the skills required for customer-facing technical roles.

About the AWS Emerging Talent Team

The internship is part of the Emerging Talent team within AWS Industries and Strategic Accounts.

The team focuses on developing the next generation of professionals for roles such as:

Solutions Architects

Customer Solutions Managers

Sales professionals

These professionals work with some of AWS’s large and influential customers across different industries.

The team uses a cohort-based approach to talent development, providing participants with resources such as:

Education

Mentorship

Job-shadowing opportunities

Practical experience

The objective is to help emerging talent develop the skills needed to work in customer-facing roles.

Basic Qualifications

Applicants must meet the basic requirements specified for the position.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be:

18 years of age or older.

Education

Applicants must currently be enrolled in a:

Bachelor’s degree program, or

Higher degree program

The degree must be in:

Computer Science

Computer Engineering

A related technical field

Applicants are expected to graduate between:

December 2027 and September 2028.

Internship Commitment

Applicants must be able to:

Work 40 hours per week

Commit to the full 12-week internship

The position is a full-time internship.

Programming Experience

Applicants need experience with at least one of the following programming languages:

Java

Python

Node.js

C#

C++

Experience may come from academic work, projects, internships, or other relevant technical experiences, provided it meets the employer’s requirements.

Technical Experience

Applicants must have experience in at least one of the following technical domains:

Analytics

Security

Storage

DevOps

Application development

Machine learning

The position therefore targets students who already have some technical foundation rather than applicants with no technical experience.

Generative AI and Machine Learning

The position also specifically lists experience with emerging technologies such as:

Generative AI

Large Language Models (LLMs)

Machine Learning (ML)

Students who have worked with these technologies through coursework, projects, research, internships, or other relevant experiences may find this requirement particularly relevant to their background.

Customer Service and Communication Skills

Technical ability is only one part of the role.

Applicants are also expected to have experience demonstrating:

Customer service

Communication

Interpersonal skills

This reflects the customer-facing nature of a Solutions Architect position.

Solutions Architects need to communicate technical concepts to customers and collaborate with different teams, so the ability to work effectively with people is an important part of the internship.

Preferred Qualifications

Amazon also identifies several qualifications that can strengthen an applicant’s profile.

AWS Certification

An AWS certification is preferred.

Although it is listed as a preferred qualification rather than a basic requirement, applicants with relevant AWS certifications may be able to demonstrate additional familiarity with AWS technologies and cloud concepts.

Communicating Complex Ideas

Applicants who have experience communicating complex technical concepts to both:

Technical audiences

Non-technical audiences

are preferred.

This could include explaining technical projects to classmates, customers, managers, judges, or other stakeholders.

Frameworks and Design Patterns

Amazon also prefers candidates who have experience applying established:

Frameworks

Design patterns

Software development approaches

to produce working software.

This experience can come from:

University coursework

Personal projects

Hackathons

Previous internships

Location

The internship is available in two locations:

Dallas, Texas

The position is available in Dallas, TX.

Seattle, Washington

The position is also available in Seattle, WA.

Applicants should consider the location requirements when applying because the internship is described as an onsite role.

Work Schedule

Amazon states that its internships are full-time positions.

Interns should expect to work:

Monday through Friday

for up to:

40 hours per week

The internship lasts:

12 consecutive weeks.

The typical working hours are described as approximately 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Cohort-Based Start Dates

This is a cohort-based program, meaning participants are expected to begin together.

The supplied job description lists tentative start dates of:

May 24

June 21

Applicants should confirm the applicable start date during the recruitment process.

APPLY HERE

Salary Information

The supplied listing states a starting annualized pay figure of:

$103,275 USD annually for Dallas, Texas.

Because this is an internship, applicants should confirm how compensation is applied to the internship period and whether the amount varies by location or other factors.

Amazon Benefits and Support

The job listing states that Amazon provides several benefits beginning on the first day of employment, including:

Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Mental Health Support

Medical Advice Line

401(k) matching

Benefits and eligibility can depend on applicable employment terms and location.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

Amazon states that it is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Applicants who have a disability and require an accommodation or adjustment during the application or hiring process can request support.

How to Prepare for This Internship

Students interested in the Solutions Architect Intern position can strengthen their preparation by developing experience across both technical and communication areas.

1. Build Cloud Computing Knowledge

Learn the fundamentals of cloud computing and become familiar with AWS services and architecture concepts.

2. Develop Programming Skills

Gain practical experience in at least one of the programming languages listed by Amazon:

Python

Java

Node.js

C#

C++

3. Work on Personal Projects

Personal technical projects can help demonstrate your ability to turn concepts into working applications.

Projects involving cloud computing, AI, machine learning, data, security, or software development can be particularly relevant.

4. Participate in Hackathons

Amazon specifically identifies hackathons as one way candidates may gain experience applying frameworks and design patterns to working software.

5. Learn Generative AI and LLMs

Since the job description specifically mentions Generative AI, LLMs, and ML, students can develop familiarity with these technologies through coursework, projects, or practical experimentation.

6. Improve Communication Skills

Practice explaining technical concepts in simple language.

A Solutions Architect needs to communicate with people who may have very different levels of technical knowledge.

7. Consider an AWS Certification

An AWS certification is listed as a preferred qualification.

Students interested in the role may therefore consider learning about AWS certification pathways and determining which certification aligns with their existing experience.

Learn more HERE

or HERE

Who Is This Internship Suitable For?

This opportunity is particularly relevant to university students studying technical disciplines who are interested in combining:

Cloud computing

Software development

Technology consulting

Customer engagement

Solutions architecture

Artificial intelligence

Machine learning

DevOps

Data and analytics

The position is especially focused on developing future customer-facing technical professionals.

Application Information

Job Title: Solutions Architect Intern, AWSI – 2027

Job ID: 10550494

Applicants should search for Job ID 10550494 on Amazon’s official careers platform to locate the current application listing.

The supplied information does not provide a specific application deadline. Because internship recruitment timelines can vary, applicants should check the official Amazon Jobs listing for the current application status and closing date.

Conclusion

The Amazon Web Services Solutions Architect Intern – 2027 program offers a 12-week, full-time opportunity for students pursuing computer science, computer engineering, or related technical degrees.

The program combines AWS technical training, mentorship, hands-on cloud experience, customer interaction, and practical problem-solving. Interns can work on real business challenges while learning how Solutions Architects design cloud-based solutions and translate customer requirements into technical solutions.

Applicants need to be at least 18 years old, enrolled in an eligible technical degree program, graduating between December 2027 and September 2028, and able to commit to the full 12-week, 40-hour-per-week internship. Experience with programming, cloud-related technical domains, and Generative AI, LLMs, or machine learning is also required according to the listing.

The internship is based in Dallas, Texas or Seattle, Washington, making it an opportunity for students seeking practical experience within AWS’s customer-facing technology environment.

TITLE: European Student Think Tank (EST) Academy 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: June 26, 2026

Applications are open for the European Student Think Tank (EST) Academy 2026. The EST Academy 2026 is an international, interdisciplinary, and impact-oriented programme bringing together young researchers, students, and professionals from across Europe and beyond.

The Academy responds to one of the defining challenges of our time: understanding and communicating policy complexity in an increasingly multipolar and fragmented world. As global governance becomes challenged by competing centres of power, fragmented information ecosystems, geopolitical rivalry, and diverging narratives, the ability not only to analyse policy but also to communicate it effectively has become essential.

EST Academy 2026 combines policy analysis, institutional understanding, public communication, and applied learning through a coherent and highly interactive learning pathway. Rather than functioning as a traditional lecture-based programme, the Academy places participants at the centre of the learning experience through debates, policy simulations, policy labs, media analyses, stakeholder mapping exercises, collaborative group work, and hands-on communication activities.

Participants will engage directly with world-class experts coming from policymaking institutions, think tanks, academia, international organisations, journalism, and civil society. The programme is specifically designed to expose participants to a plurality of professional perspectives, governance traditions, and regional experiences.

Benefits

Selected participants will:

Engage directly with internationally recognised experts from policymaking institutions, think tanks, academia, international organisations, journalism, and civil society;

Gain exposure to a broad range of professional experiences, governance systems, and policy approaches from different world regions;

Develop practical skills in policy analysis, institutional analysis, strategic communication, public speaking, and policy proposal development;

Strengthen competencies in teamwork, leadership, collaborative problem-solving, and interdisciplinary cooperation;

Explore how competing narratives, misinformation, and fragmented media ecosystems shape policymaking and public understanding;

Participate in simulations, debates, policy labs, and hands-on applied exercises;

Join a pan-European and international network of highly motivated students, researchers, and young professionals;

Deliver a TED-style public presentation within the framework of the final Science Slams organised in partnership with universities across Europe

Eligibility

Applications are open to:

Bachelor’s students

Master’s students

PhD candidates

Young professionals

Early-career researchers

from across Europe and neighbouring regions with a strong interest in policymaking, governance, international affairs, communication, and public engagement.

Application

Applicants must upload the following supplementary documents:

Curriculum Vitae (CV);

Motivation Letter specifying:

their motivation for participating in the Academy;

their relevant experience and credentials.

TITLE: Commonwealth Fellowship Programme 2026/2027 (Funded)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: August 25, 2026

Applications are open for the Commonwealth Fellowship Programme 2026/2027. From 2026/27, the CSC has launched a new ‘Commonwealth Fellowship Programme’ featuring two strands: the current Professional Fellowships alongside a new strand of Academic Fellowships.

Commonwealth Academic and Professional Fellowships are for citizens of Commonwealth countries to spend a period of time in the UK at an organisation working on a programme of professional or academic development which will have a developmental impact upon their return home.

Benefits

Each fellowship provides:

Approved return airfare from the Fellow’s home country to the UK.

Reimbursement of the standard visa application fee.

Stipend (living allowance) payable monthly (or pro rata) for the duration of the award at the rate of £2,218 per month, or £2,753 per month for those at organisations in the London metropolitan area (rates quoted at 2025/26 levels).

If a Fellow declares a disability, a full assessment of needs and eligibility for additional financial support will be offered by the CSC.

Arrival allowance of up to £1,247.09 (rates quoted at 2025/26 levels), including an element for warm clothing.

Additional fees can be agreed for costs associated with Fellows attending short courses/conferences as well as travel to visit other UK organisations where this forms an integral part of the programme. Programmes from six weeks to two months can claim up to £1,000 and programmes of two months to three months can claim up to £2,000.  These costs will be paid directly to the host organisation.

Eligibility

To be eligible for these Fellowships, prospective Fellows must:

Be a citizen of or have been granted refugee status by an eligible Commonwealth country, or be a British Protected Person.

Be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country. Prospective Fellows should not have indefinite leave to remain in the UK.

Professional Fellows: have at least five years’ full-time, or equivalent part-time, relevant work experience, in a profession related to the subject of the Fellowships programme, by the proposed start of the fellowship – voluntary work experience will not be counted towards this minimum.

Academic Fellows: hold a PhD and be employed by a university in a Commonwealth country other than the UK.

Be in employment at the time of application at an organisation that they will return to upon completion of the fellowship.

Provide at least two references, one of which must be from their current employer. Any applications for which references are not received will be considered ineligible.

Not have undertaken a Commonwealth Fellowship within the last five years (at the time of taking up the award).

Be available to undertake their fellowship from the prescribed start date.

Application

Applications for Fellows open at 9:00 BST Tuesday 28 July and close at 16:00 BST Tuesday 25 August.

TITLE: About the Fulbright Program

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
About the Fulbright Program

Senator Fulbright’s proposal to the U.S. Congress was simple yet remarkable: using proceeds from the sales of surplus war property to fund the “promotion of international good will through the exchange of students in the fields of education, culture and science.”

The Fulbright Program is now the largest educational scholarship program in the world and operates between the U.S. and more than 150 countries.

India has one of the largest Fulbright Programs worldwide, with approximately 22,000 fellowships and grants awarded to Indians and Americans to date.

The Fulbright Program, in collaboration with universities, schools, binational Fulbright Commissions, government agencies, non-governmental organizations and private sector agencies awards students, scholars, teachers and professionals whose achievements and potential make them outstanding representatives of their societies merit-based grants to study and/or do research in a variety of academic fields and disciplines.

The primary source of funding for the Fulbright Program comes from the U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs through an annual appropriation by the U.S. Congress.

TITLE: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University 2027: Fully Funded Innovation and Technology Master’s Scholarship for African Students

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University (ASU) is offering fully funded graduate scholarship opportunities for young African professionals seeking to pursue master’s degrees in technology, innovation, engineering, data science, computing, sustainable energy and related fields in the United States.

For the 2027–2028 academic year, the Innovation and Technology Scholarship is offering 30 graduate study opportunities to eligible African students admitted through the scholarship selection process. The programme is designed to provide not only financial support for graduate education but also leadership development, mentorship, professional development, community engagement and other forms of academic and career support.

The scholarship provides an opportunity to undertake a full-time, two-year, in-person graduate degree at Arizona State University’s Tempe campus in Arizona, USA. The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at ASU describes its current third phase as focused on preparing young African leaders with skills and knowledge in technology and sustainable innovation.

Application Deadline: Sunday, September 27, 2026, at 23:59 GMT

Applicants interested in this opportunity should carefully review the eligibility requirements, degree options, scholarship coverage and application instructions before submitting their applications.

About the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is a global initiative designed to expand access to higher education for talented young people who have the potential to become transformative leaders.

At Arizona State University, the partnership has operated through different phases. The current phase, known as Phase III: Innovation and Technology, focuses particularly on technology, innovation and entrepreneurship and provides pathways through graduate education, professional learning and related opportunities.

The broader ASU programme is built around more than simply paying for a student’s education. Scholars receive holistic support intended to help them succeed academically, professionally and personally. The programme places significant emphasis on leadership development, community engagement and the expectation that scholars will use their knowledge and skills to contribute to positive social and economic development in their communities and home countries.

For the 2027–2028 Innovation and Technology Scholarship cycle, selected scholars will have the opportunity to study in technology- and innovation-related master’s programmes at ASU.

What Makes the 2027 Innovation and Technology Scholarship Important?

Graduate education in highly specialised areas such as computer science, artificial intelligence, data science, robotics, information technology and sustainable energy can be expensive, particularly for international students studying in the United States.

This scholarship is designed to remove many of those financial barriers by providing comprehensive support to selected scholars.

The programme is therefore particularly relevant to young African professionals who have demonstrated:

Strong academic achievement

Leadership potential

Commitment to community service

An interest in technology, innovation or sustainable development

A desire to use advanced education to contribute to positive change in Africa and beyond

The programme’s emphasis is not only on what applicants have achieved academically but also on the impact they hope to create through their education and leadership.

The official ASU programme describes the scholarship as an opportunity for young African professionals to pursue master’s degrees focused on technology and innovation, with women, refugees and displaced persons, and people with disabilities strongly encouraged to apply.

Number of Scholarships Available

For the 2027–2028 academic year, the programme is offering:

30 graduate study opportunities.

These opportunities are intended for eligible African applicants seeking to pursue selected full-time, on-campus master’s programmes at Arizona State University.

The current ASU Innovation and Technology Scholarship page confirms the availability of 30 graduate study opportunities for the 2027–2028 cycle.

Study Location

Successful scholars will undertake their graduate studies at:

Arizona State University

Tempe, Arizona, United States

This is an in-person, on-campus programme. Applicants must therefore be prepared to relocate to Tempe and reside on the ASU campus for the duration of their programme.

This is important because the opportunity is not simply an online scholarship. Applicants must be able to participate in the traditional campus-based graduate experience.

Master’s Degree Programmes Covered by the Scholarship

The scholarship is available for selected full-time, on-campus graduate programmes in technology, computing, engineering, energy and related areas.

The programmes listed for the 2027–2028 scholarship cycle are:

1. Master of Science in Global Technology and Development

The MS in Global Technology and Development focuses on the relationship between technology, development and global challenges.

The programme is particularly relevant to applicants interested in understanding how technological innovation can be applied to address development challenges and improve social and economic outcomes.

Learn more about the MS Global Technology and Development programme

2. Master of Science in Information Technology

The MS in Information Technology provides advanced study in information technology and related technical areas.

It may be particularly relevant to applicants seeking careers involving information systems, technology management, digital transformation and other technology-related fields.

Learn more about the MS Information Technology programme

3. Master of Science in Human Systems Engineering – Intelligent Systems

This programme focuses on intelligent systems and the interaction between people and technological systems.

It provides an option for applicants interested in areas involving human-centred technological systems, intelligent technologies and the design of systems that interact effectively with people.

Learn more about the Human Systems Engineering – Intelligent Systems programme

4. Master of Science in Computer Science

The MS in Computer Science provides graduate-level study in computing and computer science.

It is suitable for applicants interested in developing advanced technical knowledge that can support careers and research in areas of computing and technology.

Learn more about the Computer Science master’s programme

5. Master of Science in Data Science, Analytics and Engineering

The scholarship includes the Computing and Decision Analytics pathway within ASU’s Data Science, Analytics and Engineering programme.

This area is relevant to applicants interested in using data, computational methods and analytical approaches to address complex problems and support better decision-making.

Learn more about the Data Science, Analytics and Engineering programme

6. Master of Science in Robotics and Autonomous Systems

The MS in Robotics and Autonomous Systems provides advanced study related to robotics and autonomous technologies.

It is particularly relevant to applicants interested in emerging technologies, intelligent machines, automation and technological systems capable of operating with varying degrees of autonomy.

Learn more about the Robotics and Autonomous Systems programme

7. Master of Science in Civil, Environmental and Sustainable Engineering

This programme provides graduate-level study connected to civil engineering, environmental challenges and sustainability.

It may be especially relevant to applicants interested in developing engineering solutions to infrastructure, environmental and sustainable-development challenges.

Learn more about the Civil, Environmental and Sustainable Engineering programme

8. Master of Science in Clean Energy Systems

The MS in Clean Energy Systems focuses on technologies and systems associated with clean and sustainable energy.

The programme is relevant to applicants who want to contribute to the transition toward more sustainable energy systems and address energy-related challenges.

Learn more about the Clean Energy Systems programme

9. Master of Science in Modern Energy Production and Sustainable Use

This programme focuses on modern approaches to energy production and sustainable energy use.

It provides another pathway for applicants interested in energy innovation, sustainability and the development of more effective energy systems.

Learn more about the Modern Energy Production and Sustainable Use programme

What Does the Mastercard Foundation Scholarship Cover?

One of the most significant features of this opportunity is the breadth of financial and academic support available to selected scholars.

The scholarship covers several major expenses associated with studying in the United States.

Full Tuition and Required Fees

Selected scholars receive support toward full tuition and required student fees for the programme.

This removes one of the largest financial barriers associated with pursuing a master’s degree at a US university.

Required Books

The scholarship includes support for required books, helping scholars obtain the academic materials needed for their studies.

On-Campus Housing

Selected scholars receive on-campus accommodation.

This is particularly important for international students relocating to Arizona because housing can represent a substantial part of the cost of studying in the United States.

Medical Support

The scholarship provides medical support/healthcare coverage as part of the comprehensive support package.

Visa-Related Costs

The scholarship covers visa application processing costs, helping reduce the financial burden associated with obtaining the necessary visa to study in the United States.

Airfare

The scholarship provides airfare to and from Phoenix, Arizona, supporting scholars with the international travel required to begin and complete their studies.

English Language Test Support

An English language proficiency test voucher may be provided if the applicant is required to take such a test.

ASU Graduate Application Fee Waiver

Applicants who are selected to advance to the stage where they are invited to apply for ASU admission will receive an ASU application fee waiver.

Applicants should therefore not pay an ASU application fee if they have been invited to apply through the scholarship process and provided with the waiver.

Leadership Development and Signature Programming

The scholarship goes beyond traditional financial assistance.

Scholars participate in leadership development and signature programming intended to strengthen their personal, professional and leadership capabilities.

The ASU programme also identifies academic advising, support and leadership development among the elements of the scholarship experience.

Internship and Practical Experience

The current ASU programme information also identifies a two-month internship between the first and second years as part of the scholarship experience.

This practical component can help scholars connect classroom learning with professional experience and develop skills that can be applied after graduation.

Leadership, Mentorship and Community Engagement

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is structured around the idea that higher education should contribute to broader social transformation.

As a result, scholars are expected to engage in leadership development, professional development and community-oriented activities.

The ASU programme places emphasis on developing leaders who can use their education to contribute to economic growth and social development, particularly in Africa.

The wider ASU Mastercard Foundation programme also highlights:

Leadership development

Professional development

Community service

Academic support

Peer mentorship

Transition support

Career preparation

Community engagement

Giving back to communities

Development of social ventures and impactful initiatives

This means that applicants should not think of the scholarship purely as a financial award. The programme seeks candidates who have demonstrated a commitment to leadership and service and who can articulate how their education will contribute to positive change.

Eligibility Requirements for the 2027 Scholarship

Applicants must satisfy the programme’s eligibility requirements before submitting an application.

1. Bachelor’s Degree Requirement

Applicants must have earned, or be on track to earn, a bachelor’s degree by August 2027 from a recognised institution.

The scholarship specifically states that higher education diplomas, certificates and other non-degree credentials are not considered equivalent to a bachelor’s degree for this requirement.

Applicants who do not hold a bachelor’s degree should therefore not assume that another post-secondary qualification will satisfy the requirement.

2. Strong Academic Record

Applicants must demonstrate a strong academic record equivalent to a minimum:

3.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic records clearly demonstrate strong performance.

Because international grading systems differ, applicants should carefully consider how their academic credentials correspond to the stated requirement and provide accurate academic documentation.

3. English Language Proficiency

Applicants must satisfy Arizona State University’s English language proficiency requirements for graduate admission.

Applicants who are required to demonstrate English proficiency should therefore be prepared to provide the relevant evidence.

The scholarship application also indicates that an English language proficiency test voucher may be available if testing is required.

4. African Citizenship

Applicants must be citizens of an African country.

This scholarship is specifically designed as part of ASU’s Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program focused on young African leaders.

The ASU programme describes the current Innovation and Technology scholarship as supporting young African professionals pursuing master’s degrees in technology and innovation.

5. Age Requirement

Applicants must be:

18 to 33 years old on or before September 27, 2026, the scholarship application deadline.

Applicants outside the stated age range should carefully review the official programme guidance before applying.

6. Leadership and Community Service

Applicants must demonstrate a record of:

Leadership

Service

Community engagement

Commitment to creating positive change

This is an important part of the scholarship because the programme is designed to develop future leaders who will use their education to contribute to their communities.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate concrete examples rather than simply stating that they are leaders.

Examples may include community projects, volunteer work, professional initiatives, entrepreneurship, social-impact activities, student leadership, advocacy or other forms of meaningful service.

7. No Previous Graduate or Master’s Degree

Applicants must not have previously enrolled in or completed a graduate or master’s degree programme.

This requirement is important for applicants who already hold postgraduate qualifications.

Applicants with an existing master’s degree should not assume that they are eligible simply because they meet the academic or professional requirements.

8. No Concurrent Graduate Degree

Applicants must not be enrolled in, or begin, another graduate or master’s degree programme while applying for this scholarship.

9. Ability to Relocate to Arizona

Applicants must be able to relocate to Tempe, Arizona, USA, and reside on the ASU campus for the duration of the programme.

Because this is a full-time, on-campus graduate opportunity, applicants should be prepared for an international relocation and the demands of studying in a different academic and cultural environment.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This scholarship is particularly relevant to young African professionals and graduates who want to build advanced expertise in technology, innovation, computing, engineering, data, robotics, sustainable energy or related areas.

Potential applicants may include individuals with backgrounds or interests in areas such as:

Computer science

Information technology

Data science

Artificial intelligence

Robotics

Engineering

Sustainable engineering

Clean energy

Energy systems

Technology and development

Intelligent systems

Digital innovation

Technology-enabled development

Sustainable technology

However, applicants should not select a programme solely because it is covered by the scholarship. They should ensure that their academic background, interests, career objectives and future plans align with the requirements of the particular master’s programme.

Women, Refugees, Displaced Persons and People with Disabilities

The programme explicitly encourages women, refugees and displaced persons, and people with disabilities to apply.

This is consistent with the broader emphasis of the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program on expanding access to higher education and supporting talented young people who may face barriers to educational opportunity.

Eligible applicants from these groups should therefore not be discouraged from applying because of their background.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027–2028 Innovation and Technology Scholarship is:

Sunday, September 27, 2026, at 23:59 GMT.

Applications submitted after the stated deadline will not be considered.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit. Technical problems, incomplete documents, internet connectivity issues or errors in application information can create unnecessary risks close to the deadline.

Important: Apply for the Scholarship Before Applying to ASU

One of the most important instructions in the application process is that applicants should first complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program scholarship application.

Applicants should not independently apply for admission to Arizona State University or to one of the graduate degree programmes unless instructed to do so by the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program team.

This distinction is important.

Being interested in an ASU master’s programme does not mean that applicants should immediately submit a separate paid graduate admission application.

According to the application guidance, candidates who advance in the scholarship selection process will be invited to an interview and will receive guidance concerning the ASU admission process.

Applicants who are subsequently invited to apply for ASU admission will receive an application fee waiver and should not pay an application fee.

Learn More HERE

Admission to ASU Does Not Automatically Mean Scholarship Selection

Applicants should also understand that admission to an academic programme and receiving the Mastercard Foundation scholarship are not the same thing.

The application information makes clear that admission to the academic programme does not guarantee that an applicant will receive the scholarship.

Therefore, applicants need to approach both aspects carefully:

Meet the scholarship eligibility requirements.

Submit a strong scholarship application.

Demonstrate academic excellence and leadership.

Progress through the scholarship selection process if shortlisted.

Follow the instructions provided by the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program team regarding ASU admission.

Application Process

Applicants are encouraged to complete the scholarship application online.

The application process begins through the programme’s application system, where applicants can proceed by selecting NEXT at the bottom of the application page.

The programme also provides an alternative application route for applicants with limited internet access.

Learn More HERE

Online Application

Applicants with reliable internet access are encouraged to complete and submit the application online.

Before submitting, applicants should carefully check:

Personal information

Academic information

Eligibility responses

Leadership and service information

Supporting information

Uploaded documents

Contact information

Once the application is submitted, it is considered final.

Alternative PDF Application for Applicants With Limited Internet Access

Applicants who have limited internet access can use the PDF version of the application form.

The programme provides a downloadable PDF form for this purpose.

Applicants using the PDF option should not request editing access to the online document.

The completed application and required supporting documents should be submitted in PDF format to the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program team.

The listed supporting materials include:

CV or résumé

Letter of recommendation

Transcripts

Applicants should ensure that documents are clear, complete and properly attached before submission.

Application Documents

Applicants should prepare their supporting materials in advance rather than waiting until the application deadline.

CV or Résumé

The CV should present the applicant’s academic, professional, leadership, service and other relevant experiences clearly.

Because leadership and community engagement are important parts of the scholarship, applicants should make relevant activities visible rather than presenting only academic qualifications.

Academic Transcripts

Applicants should prepare their academic transcripts and ensure that the academic information provided in the application is accurate.

The academic record should demonstrate the required level of achievement.

Recommendation Letter

Applicants using the alternative PDF application route are required to provide a letter of recommendation.

Applicants should select a recommender who can provide meaningful information about their abilities, character, leadership, academic potential or commitment to service.

English Language Evidence

Where required, applicants should be prepared to satisfy ASU’s English language proficiency requirements.

The scholarship information indicates that an English language proficiency test voucher may be provided if testing is required.

How to Strengthen Your Application

Because this is a competitive scholarship with a limited number of opportunities, applicants should focus on demonstrating more than academic eligibility.

Demonstrate Your Leadership With Evidence

Do not simply describe yourself as a leader.

Explain:

What problem did you identify?

What did you do?

Who benefited?

What was your role?

What changed as a result?

What did you learn?

How did the experience influence your future goals?

Concrete examples are generally more convincing than broad claims.

Connect Technology to Social or Economic Impact

The scholarship is specifically focused on innovation and technology.

Applicants should therefore be able to explain how their chosen field can contribute to meaningful development.

For example, applicants might discuss how technology can contribute to:

Education

Healthcare

Agriculture

Financial inclusion

Energy access

Climate resilience

Public services

Employment

Entrepreneurship

Infrastructure

Digital transformation

The strongest applications should show a connection between the applicant’s academic interests, professional goals and broader community impact.

Explain Why the Specific Master’s Programme Matters

Applicants should research the programme they intend to pursue.

Rather than simply stating that they want to study technology, applicants should understand the specific degree they are interested in and explain how it fits into their long-term goals.

Demonstrate Commitment to Africa

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at ASU places significant emphasis on preparing scholars to contribute to economic and social development in Africa.

Applicants should therefore think carefully about how the knowledge and skills gained at ASU can contribute to their communities, countries or the wider African continent.

What Happens After the Initial Application?

Applicants should understand that submission is not necessarily the end of the selection process.

Candidates who are selected to advance may be:

Invited to an interview.

Given further guidance regarding the ASU graduate admission process.

Provided with an ASU application fee waiver if instructed to apply.

Evaluated through the subsequent stages of the scholarship and admission process.

Applicants should therefore monitor the contact information provided in their application and respond promptly to communications from the programme team.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this scholarship fully funded?

The programme describes the Innovation and Technology Scholarship as a fully funded graduate opportunity. The scholarship includes tuition and fees, on-campus housing and books, visa, airfare and medical expenses, along with leadership development and other programme support.

How many scholarships are available?

The 2027–2028 application cycle offers 30 graduate study opportunities.

Who can apply?

The scholarship is intended for eligible citizens of African countries who meet the academic, age, leadership, educational and other programme requirements.

Can someone who already has a master’s degree apply?

According to the stated eligibility requirements, applicants must not have previously enrolled in or completed a graduate or master’s degree programme.

Is the programme online?

No. The scholarship supports full-time, on-campus graduate study at Arizona State University’s Tempe campus.

Do applicants need a bachelor’s degree?

Yes. Applicants must have earned a bachelor’s degree by August 2027 from a recognised institution.

What GPA is required?

Applicants must demonstrate an academic record equivalent to at least 3.5 on a 4.0 GPA scale.

Is there an age requirement?

Yes. Applicants must be between 18 and 33 years old on or before the application deadline.

Can I apply directly to ASU before applying for the scholarship?

Applicants should not apply independently to ASU or to a graduate programme unless instructed to do so by the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program team.

Does ASU admission guarantee the scholarship?

No. Admission to an academic programme does not guarantee receipt of the scholarship.

When is the deadline?

The deadline is Sunday, September 27, 2026, at 23:59 GMT.

Application and Official Information

Applicants should begin with the official Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program information for Arizona State University and carefully review the programme’s current guidance before submitting an application.

Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University – Innovation and Technology Scholarship

Applicants should also review the official information concerning the relevant ASU master’s programme before making decisions about their preferred field of study.

Final Application Checklist

Before submitting the application, prospective applicants should confirm that they:

Hold or will hold a recognised bachelor’s degree by August 2027.

Meet the minimum academic requirement of 3.5/4.0 or equivalent.

Meet the English language requirements applicable to graduate admission.

Have prepared an accurate CV or résumé.

Have their academic transcripts available.

Have prepared the required recommendation letter.

Have carefully reviewed the application guidance.

Have checked all information before submitting.

Submit the completed application before September 27, 2026, at 23:59 GMT.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University.

Conclusion

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program Innovation and Technology Scholarship at Arizona State University provides a significant opportunity for talented young Africans to pursue advanced graduate education in technology, innovation, computing, engineering, data science, robotics, sustainable energy and related fields.

What makes the opportunity particularly valuable is that it combines comprehensive financial support with leadership development, academic guidance, professional development, mentorship, community engagement and practical experience. The programme is designed not only to help scholars earn a master’s degree but also to prepare them to use their knowledge and leadership capabilities to contribute to positive social and economic change.

For eligible African applicants with a strong academic record, demonstrated leadership, a commitment to community impact and a clear interest in technology or innovation, this scholarship can provide a pathway to graduate education at Arizona State University without the normal financial burden associated with studying in the United States.

The deadline is September 27, 2026, at 23:59 GMT. Applicants should begin preparing early, carefully review the eligibility requirements and application instructions, and ensure that every piece of information submitted is complete and accurate.

Most importantly, prospective applicants should remember that the scholarship application comes first. Applicants should not independently submit an ASU graduate admission application unless they are instructed to do so by the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program team.
