The Association of African Universities is proud to present 10 policy briefs aimed at driving impactful growth and development within African higher education. As universities across the continent navigate a dynamic landscape filled with both opportunities and challenges ranging from equitable access, quality and relevance of education, financial sustainability, infrastructure, research, governance, and faculty development these briefs seek to address the most pressing issues.

Policy Brief: Equitable access to higher education in sub-Saharan Africa

This policy brief addresses the socio-economic, regional, and gender-based disparities in access to higher education in Sub-Saharan Africa and offers recommendations to improve equity.

Download Policy Brief 1

Policy Brief: Enhancing the quality and relevance of higher education in Sub-Saharan Africa

This policy brief highlights the critical need for enhancing the quality and relevance of higher education in Sub-Saharan Africa to drive economic development and societal progress. Despite significant investments, many academic programs are misaligned with job market demands, and teaching methods often lack modern pedagogical approaches.

Download Policy Brief 2

Policy Brief: Securing adequate funding and financial sustainability for higher Education in Sub-Saharan Africa

This policy brief addresses the critical challenges of securing adequate funding and ensuring financial sustainability for higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa. Financial constraints significantly hinder universities’ ability to provide quality education and support socio-economic development.

Download Policy Brief 3

Policy Brief: Building infrastructure and facilities in higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa

This policy brief emphasizes the importance of infrastructure and facilities in enhancing the effectiveness of higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa. Inadequate physical and technological infrastructure—such as libraries, laboratories, and internet access—hinders the learning experience and research output.

Download Policy Brief 4

Policy Brief: Improving research and innovation in higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa

This policy brief highlights the critical role of research and innovation in driving socio-economic development and enhancing the global standing of higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa. Despite their potential, universities in the region face significant barriers related to funding, facilities, and collaboration, which hinder their research capabilities.

Download Policy Brief 5

Policy Brief: Advancing governance and management in higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa

This policy brief emphasizes the importance of effective governance and management for the success and sustainability of higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa. Many universities in the region face challenges related to administration, accountability, and leadership, which hinder their effectiveness.

Download Policy Brief 6

Policy brief: Boosting faculty development in higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa

his policy brief underscores the importance of faculty development in enhancing educational quality and fostering research excellence in higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa. Challenges such as limited professional development opportunities, difficulties in recruiting qualified staff, and inadequate salaries negatively affect the quality of education and research.

Download Policy Brief 7

Policy brief: Strengthening student support services in higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa

This policy brief emphasizes the crucial role of student support services in promoting academic success, personal well-being, and career readiness in Sub-Saharan Africa’s higher education institutions. Inadequate services such as counselling, career guidance, and academic assistance negatively impact student outcomes and institutional effectiveness.

Download Policy Brief 8

Policy brief: Enhancing internationalization and collaboration in higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan

This policy brief highlights the importance of internationalization and collaboration with global academic networks in enhancing the quality of higher education in Sub-Saharan Africa. Such efforts can improve educational standards, foster research excellence, and create valuable opportunities for students and faculty. However, many institutions in the region struggle to establish and sustain international partnerships.

This policy brief emphasizes the critical importance of aligning educational outcomes with labor market needs in Sub-Saharan Africa to reduce unemployment and underemployment. Many graduates face difficulties securing jobs that correspond to their skills and qualifications. Achieving this alignment requires a strategic collaboration between educational institutions, industry stakeholders, and policymakers.

Through this annual call for proposals, eligible non-governmental and non-political organisations can apply for a Czech financial contribution ranging from CZK 200,000 to CZK 500,000 to implement projects that respond to local development priorities, particularly initiatives focused on skills development, community development and job creation.

The programme forms part of the Development Cooperation of the Czech Republic and is designed to support practical, locally driven projects capable of producing sustainable benefits for communities.

Applications are open to eligible organisations in Angola, Botswana, Eswatini, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa.

The deadline for submission of complete proposals is 15 September 2026.

About the Czech Republic Small-Scale Development Projects 2027

The Small-Scale Project, commonly referred to as SSP, is one of the instruments used within the Development Cooperation framework of the Czech Republic.

The programme provides an opportunity for locally established organisations to propose relatively small but targeted development projects that can contribute meaningfully to communities.

Potential implementers submit their applications to the relevant Embassy of the Czech Republic. Proposed projects are identified by the respective Czech embassies and subsequently submitted for approval by the headquarters of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic.

For the 2027 funding round administered by the Embassy of the Czech Republic in Pretoria, the programme covers all countries accredited to the Embassy.

These are:

Angola

Botswana

Eswatini

Madagascar

Mauritius

Mozambique

Lesotho

Namibia

South Africa

The intention is not simply to provide short-term financial assistance. Proposed projects should contribute to local communities through development activities that correspond with the national development priorities of the country in which the project will be implemented.

How Much Funding Is Available?

Successful projects may receive a financial contribution from the Czech Republic ranging from:

CZK 200,000 to CZK 500,000 per project.

Applicants should develop realistic project budgets that demonstrate how the requested funding will be used to achieve clear development objectives.

The Embassy also states that co-financing from other sources is desirable, although the level of such co-financing is at the discretion of the applicant.

This means organisations that have access to their own resources or additional funding partners may incorporate those resources into the proposed project.

Applicants should, however, pay careful attention to the financial conditions of the programme, including restrictions on administrative expenses and personnel-related expenditure.

Priority Areas for Small-Scale Projects 2027

Projects submitted under the programme should align with the relevant development priorities of the country where implementation will take place.

Particular emphasis is being placed on projects addressing:

Skills development

Community development

Job creation

Local development priorities

Sustainable community impact

Applicants should therefore demonstrate a clear connection between their proposed activities and the needs of the communities they intend to support.

Projects should not be designed solely around short-term activities. Sustainability is an important requirement of the programme.

Sustainability Is a Key Requirement

One of the most important conditions of the Czech Republic Small-Scale Development Projects programme is sustainability.

According to the Embassy, a project must be capable of continuing without further financial support from the Czech Republic.

Applicants should therefore consider what will happen after the funding period ends.

A strong proposal should explain how the benefits, activities, skills, infrastructure or other outcomes created through the project will continue after Czech financial assistance has concluded.

Depending on the nature of the project, sustainability could involve strengthening the capacity of a local organisation, providing communities with skills they can continue using, establishing income-generating activities, developing systems that can operate independently or creating assets that provide benefits beyond the project period.

The precise sustainability model will depend on the proposed project, but applicants should make this an important part of their project planning.

Who Can Implement an SSP Project?

The programme is intended for organisations rather than individual applicants.

The implementer must be a non-governmental and non-political organisation with legal personality in the country where the project will be implemented.

This is particularly important because applicants are required to submit documentation proving their legal status.

The organisation must also be eligible to enter into a contract with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic (MFA CZ).

The resulting agreement establishes the jurisdiction of Czech laws and courts.

Applicants should carefully consider this requirement before submitting a proposal, as successful organisations will be entering into a formal contractual relationship.

Eligible Countries for the 2027 Call

The Embassy of the Czech Republic in Pretoria is accepting applications relating to projects in the following countries:

Angola

Botswana

Eswatini

Madagascar

Mauritius

Mozambique

Lesotho

Namibia

South Africa

Applicants should ensure that their organisation has the required legal personality in the country where the proposed project will be implemented.

Project Implementation Period

The anticipated implementation period for successful projects is:

March to October 2027.

However, implementation cannot begin simply because an applicant has been selected.

Projects may commence only after the relevant contract has been signed.

Successful applicants are expected to sign a contract with the Embassy of the Czech Republic during the first quarter of 2027.

Furthermore, the project must be fully implemented and all funds properly accounted for by:

15 October 2027.

Organisations developing their implementation schedules should therefore ensure that all proposed activities, procurement, programme delivery and financial accounting can realistically be completed within the permitted timeframe.

Important Financial and Implementation Conditions

Applicants should carefully review the programme’s financial and implementation requirements before preparing a budget.

1. Administrative Costs Cannot Be Funded

Administrative costs incurred by the implementing organisation cannot be covered by the SSP funding.

Applicants should therefore structure their budgets carefully and distinguish eligible project expenditure from general organisational administrative expenses.

2. Personnel and Expert-Related Costs Are Limited

Costs associated with experts should be kept as low as possible.

This includes:

Salaries or professional fees

Allowances

Accommodation

Travel costs

Insurance, where applicable

Vaccination expenses, where applicable

Collectively, these expenses must not exceed 25% of the project’s total costs.

Applicants should carefully calculate this proportion before submitting their budget.

3. The CZK Funding Amount Is Binding

The total amount of funding provided in Czech koruna (CZK) is binding when funds are converted into another currency.

Organisations working with local currencies should therefore be mindful of exchange rates and potential currency fluctuations when preparing and subsequently implementing their budgets.

4. Projects Must Be Sustainable

The project must be designed so that it can continue delivering benefits without requiring additional financial support from the Czech Republic after the funding period.

5. Czech Aid Visibility Requirements Apply

Tangible assets obtained or developed through the project must carry the Czech Aid logo.

Where a project produces intangible assets, the financial support provided through the Czech Republic Development Cooperation must be acknowledged.

Successful organisations should therefore incorporate appropriate donor visibility and acknowledgement into project implementation.

6. Full Terms Will Be Established by Contract

The complete terms and conditions governing successful projects will be detailed in the contract between the successful implementer and the relevant Czech authorities.

Required Application Documents

Applications must be submitted in English.

To be considered, applicants need to prepare a complete proposal containing all required documents.

1. SSP Identification Form

Applicants must provide two copies of the completed SSP Identification Form 2026.

The two copies must be submitted in different formats:

One copy must be completed, stamped, signed and scanned as a PDF file.

The second copy must be saved and submitted in its original XLSX spreadsheet format.

Applicants should ensure that the information contained in both versions is consistent.

2. Proof of Legal Status

Applicants must provide a copy of an official document proving the organisation’s legal status.

This requirement demonstrates that the applicant is a legally recognised entity and satisfies the requirement to have legal personality in the country where implementation will take place.

3. Authorisation of the Project Manager

Applicants must provide a document confirming that the designated contact person or project manager has been authorised to act on behalf of the institution.

The project manager must be authorised to:

Represent the institution in relation to the project

Sign the Identification Form

Oversee the project

Implement the project

Organisations should ensure that the authorisation documentation clearly establishes these responsibilities.

4. Identification Document or Passport

A copy of the ID document or passport of the designated project manager must be included with the application.

5. Evidence of Previous Development Project Experience

Applicants must provide at least three reference letters or other documentation demonstrating previous implementation of similar development projects.

This requirement means organisations should be prepared to demonstrate relevant experience rather than simply proposing a project without evidence of previous implementation capacity.

Applicants should select references or documentation that clearly demonstrate their ability to manage development activities similar to the project they are proposing.

How to Apply for the Czech Republic Small-Scale Projects 2027

Organisations interested in applying should follow the application process carefully.

Step 1: Confirm Organisational Eligibility

Before investing significant time in developing a proposal, confirm that your organisation:

Is non-governmental

Is non-political

Has legal personality in the country of project implementation

Operates in one of the nine eligible countries

Can enter into the required contractual arrangement

Has previous experience implementing similar development projects

Step 2: Develop the Project Concept

Identify a development challenge relevant to the community where the project will be implemented.

The proposal should align with national development priorities and preferably demonstrate a strong connection with the programme’s emphasis on:

Skills

Community development

Employment and job creation

Step 3: Develop a Sustainable Project Model

Applicants should explain how the project will create benefits beyond the funding period.

Consider what structures, skills, resources, partnerships or activities will remain after October 2027.

Step 4: Prepare a Realistic Budget

Develop the budget within the available Czech contribution of CZK 200,000 to CZK 500,000.

Remember that administrative costs cannot be funded and expert-related salaries, fees, allowances, accommodation, travel, insurance and vaccination expenses should be minimised and collectively must not exceed 25% of total project costs.

Co-financing from other sources may also be incorporated and is considered desirable.

Step 5: Complete the SSP Identification Form

Complete the required SSP Identification Form carefully.

Prepare:

One stamped and signed PDF version

One XLSX version

Applicants should review both copies before submission to make sure the information is accurate and consistent.

Step 6: Gather Supporting Documents

Prepare:

Proof of the organisation’s legal status

Proof of authorisation for the project manager

Project manager’s ID or passport copy

At least three reference letters or documents demonstrating previous implementation of similar development projects

Step 7: Submit the Complete Application

All required documents must be submitted electronically to:

smallscaleprojectscz@gmail.com

The email subject line should follow the format:

SSP 2027: [Name of the Implementer]

Applicants should make sure their submission is complete before sending it.

Application Deadline

The deadline to submit complete proposals is:

15 September 2026

Applicants should aim to submit before the deadline where possible to allow sufficient time to check that all required documentation has been attached and submitted in the correct formats.

Incomplete proposals may not satisfy the requirements for consideration.

What Happens After Applications Are Submitted?

The Small-Scale Projects are identified by the respective Czech embassies based on applications submitted by potential implementers.

Projects are subsequently subject to approval by the headquarters of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic.

Successful applicants under the Pretoria Embassy’s 2027 call are expected to enter into a contract with the Embassy during the first quarter of 2027.

Implementation can commence only after the contract has been signed.

Successful organisations will then have the March–October 2027 implementation period to deliver their approved activities, with projects and funding required to be fully accounted for by 15 October 2027.

Why Organisations Should Consider the SSP 2027 Opportunity

The Small-Scale Development Projects programme provides eligible African organisations with an opportunity to obtain international development funding for targeted initiatives at the local level.

The programme may be particularly relevant for established organisations that already have experience delivering community development initiatives and have identified practical interventions capable of producing sustainable outcomes.

The funding can help eligible organisations develop projects centred on areas such as skills development, community advancement and employment creation while contributing to national development priorities.

The requirement for sustainability also encourages organisations to design interventions whose impact can extend beyond the immediate funding period.

Important Dates at a Glance

Applicants should keep the following dates and periods in mind:

Call published: 28 August 2026

Call updated: 1 September 2026

Application deadline: 15 September 2026

Contract signing for successful applicants: First quarter of 2027

Project implementation period: March–October 2027

Final implementation and accounting deadline: 15 October 2027

Important Advice Before Submitting

Applicants should carefully review every requirement before sending their proposal.

In particular, organisations should ensure that:

The application is completed in English.

The organisation has legal personality in the project country.

The organisation is non-governmental and non-political.

The proposed project addresses relevant national development priorities.

The proposal clearly demonstrates sustainability.

The requested Czech contribution falls between CZK 200,000 and CZK 500,000.

Administrative expenses are not included as funded costs.

Relevant expert and personnel-related expenses remain within the 25% limit.

The SSP Identification Form is provided in both required formats.

The signed version contains the necessary stamp and signature.

All required supporting documents are attached.

At least three references or supporting documents showing previous similar development project experience are provided.

The correct email subject format is used.

The complete application is submitted by 15 September 2026.

APPLY NOW

Conclusion

The Czech Republic Small-Scale Development Projects 2027 call offers established local organisations across nine African countries an opportunity to secure CZK 200,000 to CZK 500,000 for targeted community development initiatives.

Administered through the Embassy of the Czech Republic in Pretoria as part of the Czech Republic’s development cooperation activities, the programme is particularly focused on projects that respond to national and local development priorities, with emphasis on skills development, community development and job creation.

Successful proposals will need to go beyond identifying an immediate community need. Applicants must demonstrate appropriate legal status, previous development project experience, realistic financial planning and, importantly, the ability of the proposed initiative to remain sustainable without further Czech financial support.

Eligible organisations in Angola, Botswana, Eswatini, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa should begin preparing their documentation as soon as possible because the application window is relatively short.

Complete applications must be submitted by 15 September 2026.

Interested organisations should consult the official announcement from the Embassy of the Czech Republic in Pretoria and download the required SSP Identification Form before preparing their submission.

Visit the OFY website for more Grant Opportunities.

TITLE: Youth Leadership for Democracy and Solidarity (YLDS) 2026

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: August 5, 2026

Applications are open for the Youth Leadership for Democracy and Solidarity (YLDS) 2026. The Horn of Africa (HoA) is home to one of the world’s youngest populations that are aspiring to shape political dialogue, civic action, and democratic change across the region. Yet despite their demographic strength, many remain excluded from meaningful engagement in governance, face shrinking civic space in the national landscape, and have limited opportunities to collaborate across borders.

To contribute to addressing these challenges, the Horn Center for Democracy (HCD) is launching the Youth Leadership for Democracy and Solidarity (YLDS)-a regional leadership initiative that brings together emerging youth leaders committed to promoting democratic governance and cross-border cooperation.

This initiative is part of HCD’s multiyear strategy-youth development program-composed of digital civic education and youth leadership cohorts. This program aims to advance youth engagement in democracy, foster cross-border collaboration, and increase the resilience of pro-democracy actors throughout the HoA region. Through intensive learning, peer exchange, leadership development, and collaborative action, the program will support a new generation of young leaders equipped to lead democratic transformation across the region.

About the Youth Cohort

The inaugural cohort will bring together 15 emerging youth leaders from across the HoA region and will take place in Addis Ababa from October 11-18th, 2026. Participants will engage in:

A week-long intensive residential leadership training;

Immersive online learning sessions (Hybrid guided model)

Interactive workshops led by regional experts, democracy practitioners, and academics

Peer learning and dialogue, collaborative problem-solving, and innovation labs

Continued mentorship, networking opportunities, and engagement through an alumni network

The program is designed not only as a training opportunity but as the foundation of a regional network of democratic leaders committed to long-term collaboration and solidarity.

Benefits

Participants will deepen their understanding of political and governance dynamics across the Horn of Africa

Strengthen their leadership and democratic governance skills

Exchange experiences with peers from across the region

Build lasting professional relationships and regional networks

Co-design innovative responses to shared democratic challenges

Join a growing alumni network of young democratic leaders

Eligibility

Applicants should (be):

A citizen of one of the IGAD member countries

Between the ages of 18 and 35

Demonstrate leadership potential and a commitment to democratic values, and adhere to non-violent approaches to political discourse

Have experience in civic engagement, youth leadership, community organizing, advocacy and policy engagement, social innovation and activism, movements, and political participation

Interested in working across borders to advance democratic governance and democratic values

Available to participate fully in all online and in-person program activities, and actively engage in group discussions and collaborative activities

Contribute to cross-border and community project development

Participate in program evaluations

Demonstrate a willingness to contribute actively to the program alumni network

Application

Applicants should submit a:

Completed online application form

Current CV (maximum two pages)

Motivation letter outlining their interest in the program, any relevant experience in community organizing, development, and commitment to democratic leadership

Any additional supporting documents requested in the application form

A 3-5 minute Video Showcasing or explaining your relevant work and experience in relation to this call, Upload to youtube and attach the video URL only

Click here to apply

For more information, visit Youth Leadership for Democracy and Solidarity.

TITLE: Climate and Health Catalyst Awards 2026: Apply for Up to USD 5,000 in Research Funding for Early Career Researchers in Africa

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Climate and Health Catalyst Awards 2026 provide catalytic research funding of up to USD 5,000 to support Early Career Researchers who are working at the intersection of climate change and health.

The programme is designed for researchers who have already collected climate-and-health data and now need support to transform that existing evidence into meaningful research, policy or practice outputs. Rather than funding the collection of new primary data, the awards focus on helping researchers analyse, interpret, write, disseminate and translate existing evidence into outputs that can influence decision-making and real-world practice.

The initiative is being implemented by the ARCH Program Consortium and Amref Health Africa, through the Pan-African Center for Research and Policy in Climate Change and Health (CPRCCH). It seeks to strengthen the next generation of African climate and health researchers by providing not only financial support, but also mentorship, technical guidance, capacity strengthening, networking and knowledge-translation support.

With a maximum individual award of USD 5,000 and a project implementation period of up to 12 months, the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards can help researchers move an existing dataset from the evidence-generation stage toward publication, policy influence and practical application.

What Are the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards 2026?

The Climate and Health Catalyst Awards are intended to bridge the gap between research evidence and real-world impact.

Many researchers already possess valuable datasets but may lack the resources required to complete secondary analysis, prepare manuscripts, develop policy briefs, disseminate findings or convert research evidence into practical recommendations.

This programme addresses that gap.

The award supports researchers who have already generated climate-and-health evidence and are ready to take the next steps, including:

Analysing existing datasets.

Conducting statistical work.

Interpreting research findings.

Preparing scientific manuscripts.

Developing policy briefs.

Producing evidence syntheses.

Managing and improving data quality.

Disseminating research findings.

Translating evidence for policy and practice.

Publishing research through open-access platforms.

Participating in approved conferences.

Supporting communication and collaboration activities.

The programme therefore focuses on moving research through the pathway of:

Research → Evidence → Policy → Practice

The central principle is that funding should help transform existing climate-and-health evidence into outputs that can contribute to better decisions and meaningful change.

A Catalyst Award, Not a Primary Data Collection Grant

One of the most important points applicants need to understand is that the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards are not designed to fund primary data collection.

Applicants must already possess an existing climate-and-health dataset.

The funding is instead intended to support the stages that come after data collection, including:

Secondary data analysis.

Statistical analysis.

Data management and quality assurance.

Interpretation of findings.

Scientific writing.

Manuscript development.

Policy brief preparation.

Evidence synthesis.

Research dissemination.

Knowledge translation.

Publication.

Communication and collaboration.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to researchers who have completed data collection but require additional resources to turn their findings into high-quality academic, policy or practical outputs.

Who Is Behind the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards?

The programme is offered through the ARCH Program Consortium and Amref Health Africa, through the Pan-African Center for Research and Policy in Climate Change and Health (CPRCCH).

The broader goal is to support the development of the next generation of African researchers working on climate and health.

The programme combines funding with a structured support ecosystem intended to strengthen research quality and increase the likelihood that research findings will reach policymakers, practitioners and other decision-makers.

What Does the Climate and Health Catalyst Award Provide?

Selected researchers can receive a range of financial and non-financial support.

1. Up to USD 5,000 in Catalytic Funding

Each successful applicant can receive a maximum award of USD 5,000.

The funding is intended to accelerate the process of transforming existing climate-and-health evidence into meaningful outputs.

The award is therefore not simply general research funding. Proposed expenditure should be directly connected to activities that move existing evidence toward publication, policy influence, dissemination or practical application.

2. Structured Mentorship

Award recipients receive structured mentorship throughout the programme.

The mentorship is intended to help researchers strengthen:

Research quality.

Interpretation of findings.

Scientific outputs.

Overall research impact.

This can be particularly valuable for Early Career Researchers who are developing their research careers and seeking guidance from experienced professionals.

3. Capacity Strengthening

Participants receive technical and research skills designed to help them move evidence toward impact.

Capacity strengthening can support researchers in developing the skills required to analyse evidence, communicate findings and translate research into useful outputs.

4. Networking Opportunities

The programme connects award recipients with a Pan-African community of:

Researchers.

Practitioners.

Climate and health leaders.

This creates opportunities for researchers to develop professional relationships and become part of a wider African climate-and-health research community.

5. Knowledge Translation Support

Researchers receive support in turning research findings into evidence that can be used by policymakers, practitioners and other decision-makers.

Knowledge translation is particularly important in climate and health because research findings can have significant implications for public health planning, climate adaptation and policy development.

6. Technical Guidance

The programme provides practical support across several stages of the research process, including:

Analysis.

Interpretation.

Scientific writing.

Dissemination.

Development of final outputs.

This technical support complements the financial award and is intended to strengthen the overall quality and impact of the research.

Who Can Apply for the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards?

The programme is specifically designed for Early Career Researchers who already possess climate-and-health evidence and are ready to transform that evidence into research, policy or practice outputs.

There are two main applicant profiles.

PhD Candidates

PhD candidates can apply if they have:

Completed the data collection phase of their research.

An existing climate-and-health dataset.

Enrolment in a PhD programme.

Registration at an eligible institution.

Residence in an eligible country.

The key requirement is that data collection must already be completed. Applicants cannot use this award to begin or finance primary data collection.

Postdoctoral and Early Career Researchers

Postdoctoral researchers and other Early Career Researchers can apply if they are:

Within five years of PhD graduation.

Already in possession of a climate-and-health dataset.

Affiliated with an eligible institution.

Based in an eligible country.

Their proposed work should focus on analysing and transforming their existing climate-and-health data into research, policy or practice outputs.

Geographic Eligibility: Which African Countries Are Eligible?

The Climate and Health Catalyst Awards have a specific geographic scope.

Applicants must either be citizens or legal residents of one of the nine eligible African countries, and they must currently reside in the country indicated in their application.

The nine eligible countries are:

Botswana

Ethiopia

Kenya

Malawi

Mozambique

Rwanda

South Africa

Tanzania

Uganda

The programme therefore brings together researchers from countries across East, Southern and other parts of Africa represented by the eligible-country list.

Residency Requirement

Being a citizen of an eligible country is not the only geographic requirement.

The source states that applicants must have citizenship or legal residence in one of the nine eligible countries and must currently reside in the country indicated in their application.

Applicants should therefore carefully confirm that their current residence and legal status satisfy the programme requirements before submitting an application.

What Research Activities Can the USD 5,000 Fund Support?

The award provides funding for specific research-related activities.

Eligible Activities

The programme identifies the following activities as eligible:

Secondary Data Analysis and Statistical Work

Researchers can use the award to analyse existing climate-and-health datasets and conduct relevant statistical work.

This is one of the central purposes of the programme because the award is specifically designed for researchers who have already completed data collection.

Manuscript Preparation and Scientific Writing

Funding can support the development of scientific manuscripts and other research writing.

This can help researchers move from completed analysis toward publication-quality research outputs.

Policy Briefs and Evidence Synthesis

Researchers can develop policy briefs and evidence syntheses that make research findings more accessible and useful to decision-makers.

This is particularly consistent with the programme’s emphasis on moving evidence toward policy and practice.

Data Management and Quality Assurance

Funding can support activities related to managing existing data and ensuring its quality.

Good data management is essential for producing credible and reliable research findings.

Research Dissemination and Knowledge Translation

The award can support activities that help researchers communicate their findings to relevant audiences and translate technical evidence into useful information.

Open-Access Publication Fees

Funding can be used for eligible open-access publication fees.

This can help researchers make their findings more accessible to wider academic and professional audiences.

Approved Conference Participation

The award can support participation in approved conferences.

This can give researchers opportunities to share their findings, receive feedback and connect with other professionals working in climate and health.

Communication and Collaboration Costs

Eligible communication and collaboration expenses can also be supported where they directly contribute to the approved research activities.

What Expenses Are Not Eligible?

Applicants must pay close attention to the programme’s financial restrictions.

The following expenses are listed as ineligible:

Salary top-ups.

Personal allowances.

Tuition fees.

Large equipment purchases.

Unapproved travel.

Entertainment.

Gifts.

Alcohol.

Political activities.

Religious activities.

Unrelated commercial activities.

Unapproved institutional overheads.

The programme requires proposed expenditure to be directly attributable to approved research activities and to remain within the conditions of the award.

Applicants should therefore develop a realistic and carefully justified budget rather than treating the USD 5,000 as unrestricted funding.

Award Duration

The maximum implementation period for a Climate and Health Catalyst Award is 12 months.

Researchers should therefore develop a realistic work plan showing how the available funding will be used throughout the project period.

The award parameters are:

Maximum funding: USD 5,000.

Maximum project duration: 12 months.

Focus: Transforming existing climate-and-health evidence into outputs.

Target: Early Career Researchers.

Geographic scope: Nine eligible African countries.

Application Process for the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards

The application process consists of five main stages.

Step 1: Check Your Eligibility

Before starting the application, applicants should carefully review the eligibility criteria.

You must fall within one of the qualifying Early Career Researcher categories and already have an existing climate-and-health dataset.

Applicants should also confirm that they satisfy the geographic and institutional requirements.

Step 2: Prepare Your Documents

Applicants should gather all required documents before beginning the application.

These include:

Motivation letter.

Curriculum vitae.

Concept note.

Institutional support or affiliation letter.

Two reference letters.

Ethics approval documentation where applicable.

Detailed work plan and budget.

The programme recommends preparing these materials in advance because the application requires multiple supporting documents.

APPLY HERE.

Step 3: Complete the Online Application

Applicants must complete all nine sections of the application form.

The application form allows applicants to save their progress and return later.

The estimated completion time is approximately 30–45 minutes.

Step 4: Review and Submit

Before submitting, applicants should carefully check:

All required fields.

Word and page limits.

Supporting documents.

File formats.

Budget information.

Work plan.

Eligibility information.

Incomplete, ineligible or late applications will not be considered, according to the application note provided in the source.

Step 5: Receive an Application Reference Number

After successfully submitting the application, applicants receive a unique application reference number.

The source gives the reference format as:

CHCA-2026-XXXXXX

Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

Documents Required for the Application

Applicants should prepare eight main submission items.

1. Motivation Letter

The motivation letter is required and must not exceed one page.

It should explain:

Why you are applying.

Why the award is relevant to your research.

How the award will support your career.

The limited length means applicants should focus on their strongest motivations and clearly connect the award to their research and career development.

2. Curriculum Vitae

The CV is required and should not exceed four pages.

It should include relevant academic and professional experience, particularly publications and research outputs.

Applicants should prioritize information that demonstrates their experience and potential as an Early Career Researcher.

3. Concept Note

The concept note is required and has a maximum length of five pages.

It should summarize:

The proposed project.

The data that will be used.

Expected research outputs.

Because this is a data-to-output award, the concept note should make it clear how existing data will be transformed into meaningful outputs.

4. Institutional Support or Affiliation Letter

Applicants must provide a letter from their institution confirming their affiliation and support for the proposed project.

There is no page limit specified for this document.

5. First Reference Letter

A professional or academic reference from a supervisor or senior colleague is required.

The letter should help demonstrate the applicant’s research capabilities, experience and potential.

6. Second Reference Letter

A second professional or academic reference is also required.

Applicants should select referees who can provide meaningful information about their academic, professional or research capabilities.

7. Ethics Approval Documentation

Ethics documentation is required where applicable.

Applicants may provide an approved ethics certificate or evidence demonstrating that approval is pending or not required, depending on the circumstances of their project.

8. Detailed Work Plan and Budget

Applicants must provide a detailed work plan and budget.

The document can be submitted as a PDF or as a spreadsheet converted to PDF.

The work plan should show activities on a month-by-month basis, while the budget should provide an itemized breakdown of expenditure within the USD 5,000 maximum award ceiling.

File Format and Naming Requirements

All application documents must be submitted as PDF files, with a maximum file size of 750 KB per file.

Applicants should ensure that every document is:

Legible.

Correctly named.

Complete.

Within the specified page limit where applicable.

Uploaded before final submission.

The recommended file naming convention is:

Surname_FirstName_DocumentType_ClimateHealthCatalystAwards_2026.pdf

For example:

Okonkwo_Adaeze_MotivationLetter_ClimateHealthCatalystAwards_2026.pdf

Using the recommended naming format can help applicants keep their submission organized and aligned with the programme’s document protocol.

How to Prepare a Strong Concept Note

The concept note is one of the most important documents because the programme is specifically focused on transforming existing data into outputs.

Applicants should clearly demonstrate:

What climate-and-health dataset they already possess.

How and when the data were collected.

What research question or problem the proposed analysis addresses.

What analysis will be conducted.

What outputs will be produced.

Who will use the findings.

How the findings can contribute to policy or practice.

How the proposed activities can realistically be completed within 12 months.

How the USD 5,000 budget will directly support those activities.

A strong concept note should make a clear connection between the existing evidence, proposed activities and expected impact.

How to Prepare a Strong Budget

Because the maximum award is USD 5,000, applicants should ensure that every proposed expense is justified.

The budget should be:

Specific.

Realistic.

Directly linked to the research activities.

Within the USD 5,000 ceiling.

Consistent with the proposed work plan.

Free of restricted expenses.

Applicants should avoid including costs such as tuition, personal allowances, salary top-ups, large equipment and other prohibited categories.

Why the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards Matter

Climate change and health are increasingly interconnected.

Changes in temperature, extreme weather, environmental conditions and other climate-related factors can have significant implications for health and wellbeing. However, producing useful evidence is only one part of the research process.

Research has greater potential for impact when findings are analysed rigorously, published, communicated effectively and translated into information that policymakers and practitioners can use.

This is the central role of the Catalyst Awards.

Instead of focusing on collecting more data, the programme seeks to help researchers make better use of evidence that already exists.

This approach can help address a common challenge faced by Early Career Researchers: having valuable research data but limited resources to complete the final stages of analysis, publication, dissemination and knowledge translation.

Career Development Opportunities for Early Career Researchers

The programme can also contribute to the professional development of researchers.

Through funding, mentorship, technical guidance, capacity strengthening and networking, award recipients can develop skills that extend beyond the immediate research project.

Participants can potentially strengthen their experience in:

Research analysis.

Scientific writing.

Research communication.

Policy engagement.

Evidence synthesis.

Knowledge translation.

Conference participation.

Research collaboration.

Publication.

Climate-and-health research.

These skills can help Early Career Researchers establish stronger academic and professional profiles.

Important Things Applicants Should Know

Before applying, prospective candidates should pay particular attention to the following requirements:

You Must Already Have Data

The programme does not fund primary data collection.

Applicants should already possess an appropriate climate-and-health dataset.

You Must Be an Early Career Researcher

The programme is intended for qualifying PhD candidates and postdoctoral/Early Career Researchers within five years of PhD graduation.

Your Research Must Relate to Climate and Health

The existing evidence and proposed activities should clearly fall within the climate-and-health research space.

You Must Meet the Geographic Requirement

Applicants must be citizens or legal residents of one of the nine eligible countries and currently reside in the country indicated in their application.

Your Budget Must Follow the Rules

The USD 5,000 award cannot be treated as unrestricted personal funding. Expenditure must directly support approved research activities.

Your Documents Must Follow the Submission Requirements

Applicants should respect page limits, file formats and the maximum 750 KB size per file.

Application Deadline

No application deadline is stated in the supplied source material.

Applicants should therefore consult the official application platform and full call information for the current submission deadline before applying. The source does state that incomplete, ineligible or late applications will not be considered.

How to Apply

Applicants can begin the application through the programme’s online application form.

The application process is designed to allow applicants to save their progress and return later. The estimated completion time is approximately 30–45 minutes.

For more information on Climate and Health Catalyst Awards 2026, click HERE.

Applicants should read the complete call and application guidance carefully before submitting their application.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this a grant or a fellowship?

The programme provides catalytic research funding to Early Career Researchers. Based on the categories commonly used for opportunities such as scholarships, conferences, awards, competitions, internships, fellowships, jobs and grants, the most appropriate classification is a grant/research award.

How much funding is available?

The maximum individual award is USD 5,000.

How long can the project last?

The maximum project implementation period is 12 months.

Can I use the funding to collect new data?

No. The programme specifically states that it is not for primary data collection. Applicants must already have an existing climate-and-health dataset.

Can PhD students apply?

Yes. PhD candidates can apply if they have completed data collection, are enrolled in a PhD programme, are registered at an eligible institution and meet the geographic requirements.

Can postdoctoral researchers apply?

Yes. Postdoctoral and Early Career Researchers within five years of PhD graduation can apply if they already have relevant climate-and-health data and meet the other eligibility conditions.

Can researchers from Kenya apply?

Yes. Kenya is one of the nine eligible countries listed by the programme. Applicants must also satisfy the citizenship/legal residence and current residency requirements.

Can the award pay tuition fees?

No. Tuition fees are specifically listed among the ineligible expenses.

Can the funding be used for salary top-ups?

No. Salary top-ups and personal allowances are listed as ineligible expenses.

Are conference expenses eligible?

Approved conference participation is listed among the eligible activities, subject to the programme’s conditions.

How many reference letters are required?

Two professional or academic reference letters are required.

What is the maximum CV length?

The CV must not exceed four pages.

How long can the motivation letter be?

The motivation letter must not exceed one page.

How long can the concept note be?

The concept note has a maximum length of five pages.

How large can each uploaded file be?

Each PDF file must be no larger than 750 KB.

Conclusion

The Climate and Health Catalyst Awards 2026 present a targeted research funding opportunity for Early Career Researchers who have already generated climate-and-health data and need support to turn that evidence into meaningful outputs.

With funding of up to USD 5,000, a maximum project duration of 12 months, structured mentorship, technical guidance, capacity strengthening, networking and knowledge-translation support, the programme goes beyond simply providing financial assistance.

Its central focus is on helping researchers move from existing evidence to research outputs, policy influence and practical application.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to PhD candidates who have completed data collection and to postdoctoral or Early Career Researchers within five years of PhD graduation. However, applicants must satisfy the programme’s geographic requirements and must be based in one of the nine eligible African countries: Botswana, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania or Uganda.

Prospective applicants should carefully prepare their motivation letter, CV, concept note, institutional letter, two references, ethics documentation where applicable, and detailed work plan and budget. They should also ensure that their proposed expenditure follows the programme’s funding restrictions.

Most importantly, applicants should remember that this is not a primary data collection award. The strongest applications will be those that clearly demonstrate how an existing climate-and-health dataset can be transformed into credible scientific, policy or practical outputs that have the potential to contribute to climate and health action in Africa.

TITLE: Call for Proposals 2026: Build Your AgriCanvas and Turn Your Cashew Business Idea into a Climate-Smart Venture

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Young and emerging entrepreneurs with innovative ideas for the cashew sector now have an opportunity to transform their concepts into investment-ready and climate-smart businesses through the e-MOVE Call for Proposals: Build Your AgriCanvas. Build Your Future.

The initiative is designed to support promising agripreneurs who are developing innovative solutions across the cashew value chain. Through a combination of free online learning, business development tools and potential kickstart prizes, participants can strengthen their entrepreneurial ideas and position themselves for future investment and growth.

Submission Window 3 is open from September to October 2026, giving eligible entrepreneurs the opportunity to develop and submit a viable business concept using the AgriCanvas framework.

Successful participants may receive valuable support, including EUR 2,000 in direct funding or business-enabling tools such as a laptop, tablet or software to support their operations.

The application deadline is 30 October 2026.

What Is the e-MOVE Call for Proposals?

The e-MOVE initiative encourages young and emerging entrepreneurs in the agricultural sector to convert knowledge gained through online learning into practical, investment-ready business ideas.

Participants are expected to build on the knowledge and tools acquired through free e-learning courses offered on the e-MOVE platform. The programme focuses on helping entrepreneurs understand important areas of modern agribusiness, including sustainable agricultural practices, investment readiness, business planning and climate resilience.

The Call for Proposals specifically invites innovative ideas connected to the cashew value chain.

Rather than simply submitting a general business idea, applicants are required to demonstrate how their proposed venture can operate as a viable enterprise. This includes developing a clear business model, identifying potential revenue streams, considering climate-smart practices and estimating the capital required to establish or expand the business.

The initiative aims to help promising entrepreneurs move from ideas to actionable business concepts that can potentially attract investment and contribute to sustainable agricultural development.

Why the Cashew Value Chain Matters

Cashew is an important agricultural commodity with significant economic potential across many countries, particularly in Africa and other OACPS member states.

However, the potential of the cashew sector extends beyond primary production. The wider value chain offers opportunities in areas such as:

Cashew farming and production

Sustainable agricultural practices

Processing and value addition

Cashew nut processing

Packaging

Storage and logistics

Marketing and distribution

Agricultural technology

Climate-smart production systems

Waste management and by-product utilization

Agribusiness services

Financial and investment solutions

Digital platforms supporting farmers and businesses

Through this Call for Proposals, entrepreneurs are encouraged to think creatively about challenges and opportunities within the cashew ecosystem.

Applicants can develop ideas that improve productivity, increase value addition, strengthen resilience, create employment or introduce innovative business solutions within the sector.

What Are the Benefits of the e-MOVE Call for Proposals?

The programme provides more than just an opportunity to compete for financial support. Participants also gain access to learning resources and business development tools designed to strengthen their entrepreneurial capacity.

1. Opportunity to Receive EUR 2,000 in Direct Funding

Selected winners may receive EUR 2,000 in direct funding to support the development or growth of their business.

The funding can provide an important starting point for entrepreneurs seeking to test, launch, strengthen or scale a promising agribusiness concept.

For early-stage entrepreneurs, access to initial capital can be a major challenge. This opportunity provides selected participants with the possibility of receiving financial support to move their business idea closer to implementation.

2. Opportunity to Receive Business Equipment or Software

Winners may alternatively receive valuable tools to support their business operations, including:

A laptop

A tablet

Software

Digital tools are increasingly important for modern businesses. Equipment and software can help entrepreneurs manage operations, maintain records, communicate with customers, develop marketing strategies and improve overall business efficiency.

3. Free Access to Cashew Sector Learning

Applicants gain access to free e-learning courses designed to strengthen their understanding of agriculture and agribusiness.

The learning pathway helps participants build the knowledge necessary to develop stronger and more practical business ideas.

The courses are offered at no cost, meaning participants do not need to pay tuition or registration fees to access the required learning materials.

4. Development of an Investment-Ready Business Idea

One of the most important aspects of the programme is its focus on investment readiness.

Many entrepreneurs have innovative ideas but struggle to communicate them clearly to investors, partners or financial institutions.

The AgriCanvas process helps applicants structure their ideas by considering key elements of a viable business model.

Participants are encouraged to think about areas such as:

The problem their business intends to solve

Their target market

The products or services they will offer

Revenue generation

Required resources

Climate resilience

Business operations

Capital requirements

Growth potential

This approach can help transform a general business concept into a more structured and fundable proposal.

5. Focus on Climate-Smart and Resilient Agriculture

The initiative places significant emphasis on climate-smart and low-emission agricultural practices.

Applicants are expected to consider how their projects can contribute to environmental sustainability and resilience.

For example, an entrepreneur may consider:

Sustainable farming practices

Resource-efficient production

Climate adaptation strategies

Reduced emissions

Improved soil conservation

Reduced agricultural waste

Renewable energy solutions

Circular economy approaches

Resilient agricultural supply chains

By integrating climate-smart approaches into their business models, entrepreneurs can develop ventures that are better positioned to respond to environmental challenges.

6. Opportunity to Contribute to Sustainable Food Systems

The programme aims to support agricultural enterprises that can contribute to stronger and more sustainable food systems.

Innovative agribusinesses have the potential to:

Create employment opportunities

Support farmers

Increase agricultural productivity

Strengthen local economies

Improve value addition

Reduce post-harvest losses

Promote sustainable production

Support rural development

By supporting viable MSMEs, the initiative seeks to strengthen the role of young entrepreneurs in building resilient agricultural economies.

Who Can Apply for the e-MOVE Call for Proposals?

The Call for Proposals is designed for young and emerging entrepreneurs with innovative ideas related to the cashew sector.

To qualify, applicants must meet the following requirements.

Applicants Must Be 18 Years or Older

Participants must be at least 18 years old at the time of application.

Applicants Must Be Based in an OACPS Member State

The opportunity is open to individuals based in member states of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS).

The OACPS represents countries across Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific.

Applicants should confirm whether their country is an eligible OACPS member state before beginning their application.

Applicants Must Have an Innovative Cashew Value Chain Idea

The proposed business concept must focus on one or more aspects of the cashew value chain.

Applicants are encouraged to identify opportunities where innovation can improve existing systems, address challenges or create new economic opportunities.

Applicants Must Complete the Required e-MOVE Training

Completion of the mandatory e-learning pathway is an essential requirement.

Applicants cannot simply submit an idea without completing the required courses.

A valid certificate ID from the final required course must be included in the submission.

How to Apply for the e-MOVE Call for Proposals 2026

Applicants must follow a specific process to ensure that their submission is considered valid.

The application process involves registration, completion of mandatory courses, development of an AgriCanvas and submission of the final business idea.

Step 1: Register on atingi or Access the e-MOVE Landing Page

The first step is to access the e-MOVE learning platform through atingi.

Applicants can access the dedicated e-MOVE landing page, where the required learning resources are grouped together.

The platform provides free courses designed to help participants develop the knowledge necessary to create a stronger agribusiness proposal.

Applicants should ensure they create or use an account that allows them to complete the full learning pathway and access their course certificates.

Step 2: Complete the Mandatory e-MOVE Courses

Applicants must complete the required courses in the specified order.

The learning pathway includes two important stages.

Course 1: Introduction to Conservation Agriculture

The first requirement is to complete the course:

Introduction to Conservation Agriculture (CA)

This course introduces participants to concepts related to sustainable and conservation-focused agricultural practices.

Completing this first stage is necessary before progressing to the next required course.

Course 2: Creating an Investment-Ready Agribusiness

After successfully completing the first course, participants unlock the next required course:

Creating an Investment-Ready Agribusiness

This course is particularly important because it prepares applicants to structure their business ideas and develop proposals that demonstrate investment potential.

Applicants must complete this course successfully and obtain a valid certificate ID.

The certificate ID serves as proof that the applicant has completed the required training pathway.

Step 3: Develop Your AgriCanvas

After completing the required learning, participants must develop their business concept using the Business Model Canvas template provided in the submission module of the Creating an Investment-Ready Agribusiness course.

The AgriCanvas should clearly explain the proposed business idea.

Applicants should use this stage to carefully consider the major components of their proposed venture.

A strong AgriCanvas should demonstrate:

A clear business concept

A relevant problem or opportunity

The proposed solution

Target customers or beneficiaries

Revenue generation potential

Key business activities

Required resources

Partnerships

Operational considerations

Financial requirements

Climate-smart features

Potential for sustainability and growth

Applicants should avoid rushing this stage. A well-developed business model can significantly improve the clarity and strength of a proposal.

Step 4: Submit Your Business Idea Through the Official Form

Once the AgriCanvas is complete, applicants must submit their proposal through the official submission form.

To ensure that a submission is valid, applicants must:

Use the certificate ID from the Creating an Investment-Ready Agribusiness course

Complete the official submission form

Enter the complete AgriCanvas directly into the form

Provide all required information

Submit through the designated application platform

Applicants should note that file uploads for the AgriCanvas are not accepted.

The full AgriCanvas must be entered directly into the official form.

Only submissions completed through the designated form will be reviewed.

Additional Information Required in the Submission Form

In addition to the AgriCanvas, applicants will be asked to provide short written information about important aspects of their project.

These additional questions are designed to help evaluators understand the practicality and sustainability of the proposed business idea.

Describe the Climate-Smart or Resilience Component

Applicants must explain how their proposed business contributes to climate resilience or climate-smart agriculture.

This could involve demonstrating how the project responds to environmental challenges or promotes more sustainable agricultural practices.

Applicants should clearly explain the connection between their business model and climate resilience.

Explain the Revenue Model

Entrepreneurs must explain how their business intends to generate income.

A strong revenue model should clearly demonstrate how the venture can become financially sustainable.

Applicants may need to consider questions such as:

Who will pay for the product or service?

What will customers purchase?

How will the business generate revenue?

How frequently will revenue be generated?

What are the main sources of income?

What makes the business financially viable?

A clear revenue model is important because it demonstrates that the project is not simply an idea but has the potential to operate as a sustainable enterprise.

Estimate the Capital Required

Applicants must provide an estimate of the financial resources needed to start or scale the proposed project.

This should include a realistic assessment of the capital required for implementation.

Potential costs may include:

Equipment

Raw materials

Technology

Production

Marketing

Transportation

Staffing

Facilities

Licensing

Business development

Applicants should make reasonable and well-considered estimates based on the nature and scale of their proposed venture.

Can Applicants Save Their Submission and Return Later?

Yes.

The KoboToolbox submission form allows applicants to save a draft and return later.

This feature gives entrepreneurs the opportunity to take their time when developing their responses.

Applicants should use this flexibility to carefully review their AgriCanvas, climate-smart strategy, revenue model and capital requirements before submitting the final application.

However, saving a draft should not be confused with submitting the application.

Applicants must ensure that the final submission is completed before the deadline.

Can You Submit More Than One Business Idea?

No.

Each applicant may submit only one idea per submission window.

Applicants should therefore carefully select the strongest and most viable business concept before completing their application.

The organisers have also indicated that where multiple submissions are made using the same course certificate ID, only the last complete and valid submission will be considered.

Any additional submissions using the same certificate ID may be disregarded.

This makes it particularly important for applicants to review their proposal carefully before submitting it.

What Happens If You Are Not Selected?

Applicants who are not selected during the current submission window are encouraged not to give up.

Entrepreneurship often involves refining and improving ideas over time.

Unsuccessful applicants may have the opportunity to:

Improve their business concept

Strengthen their AgriCanvas

Continue learning through e-MOVE

Improve their financial projections

Develop a stronger climate-smart component

Refine their revenue model

Resubmit their idea in a future submission window

The organisers indicate that unsuccessful applicants will not necessarily receive individual notifications.

However, important announcements and future submission opportunities are expected to be shared through official channels.

When Will Successful Applicants Be Notified?

Successful applicants are expected to be contacted by mid-December 2026.

Applicants should ensure that they provide accurate contact information when completing their submission.

They should also monitor their email and official programme communication channels after submitting their proposal.

How Will Winners Be Selected?

The evaluation process and selection criteria are outlined in the official Terms and Conditions document.

Applicants are encouraged to review the Terms and Conditions carefully before submitting their proposals.

Understanding the evaluation criteria can help entrepreneurs prepare stronger applications and ensure that their submissions align with the expectations of the programme.

A competitive proposal should generally demonstrate:

Innovation

Practicality

Business viability

Investment potential

Clear revenue generation

Climate-smart practices

Resilience

Relevance to the value chain

Realistic capital requirements

Potential for growth and impact

Applicants should focus on clearly communicating why their idea matters and how it can realistically be implemented.

What Value Chains Are Eligible?

For the e-MOVE Call for Proposals, applicants should focus on the cashew value chain.

The broader programme information also references opportunities connected to other value chains under the Agribusiness e-Academy, including:

Maize

Livestock, including cattle, sheep and goats

Cocoa

However, applicants should carefully follow the requirements of the specific submission window and programme pathway they are applying under.

Ideas submitted outside the eligible value chains may not be considered.

For this particular e-MOVE opportunity, applicants should ensure that their proposal clearly demonstrates a connection to the cashew sector.

Who Is Organising the Competition?

The competition is organised by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH through initiatives including:

The Agri-Business Facility for Africa (ABF)

Market-Oriented Value Chains for Jobs and Growth in the ECOWAS Region (MOVE-ComCashew)

Both initiatives are part of German Development Cooperation.

The projects contribute to the Joint Action:

Business Support Facility for Resilient Agricultural Value Chains

The Joint Action brings together several development partners and institutions, including:

The European Union Directorate-General for International Partnerships (INTPA)

The Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS)

The German Government

The Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)

The initiative is jointly co-financed by the European Union under the Samoa Agreement with OACPS and by BMZ, with implementation support provided by GIZ.

Important Things to Remember Before Applying

Before submitting an application, candidates should carefully check that they have completed all requirements.

Here is a useful application checklist:

Eligibility Checklist

You are at least 18 years old

You are based in an eligible OACPS member state

You have an innovative idea connected to the cashew value chain

You are interested in developing a climate-smart agribusiness venture

Training Checklist

You have registered on the e-MOVE or atingi platform

You have completed Introduction to Conservation Agriculture

You have completed Creating an Investment-Ready Agribusiness

You have obtained a valid certificate ID from the required final course

Submission Checklist

You have developed a complete AgriCanvas

Your idea focuses on the eligible cashew value chain

You have explained the climate-smart or resilience component

You have developed a clear revenue model

You have estimated your capital requirements

You have entered your AgriCanvas directly into the official form

You have reviewed all responses before submitting

You have submitted before the deadline

Tips for Preparing a Strong AgriCanvas Submission

Applicants should approach the competition as an opportunity to develop a real business concept rather than simply filling out an application form.

Here are several tips that may help strengthen a proposal.

1. Identify a Real Problem

Strong business ideas often begin with a clearly identified problem.

Think about challenges within the cashew value chain that affect:

Farmers

Processors

Traders

Consumers

Exporters

Rural communities

Your proposed solution should demonstrate how it addresses a specific need.

2. Be Specific About Your Customers

Clearly identify who will benefit from or purchase your product or service.

Avoid describing your target market too broadly.

Instead, consider specific customer groups and their needs.

3. Develop a Realistic Revenue Model

Explain exactly how the business will generate income.

An innovative idea is important, but a sustainable business must also have a clear path toward financial viability.

4. Integrate Climate-Smart Solutions

Think carefully about how your project can contribute to environmental sustainability and resilience.

Do not treat the climate-smart component as an afterthought.

Instead, integrate it directly into your business model.

5. Make Realistic Financial Estimates

Your capital requirements should be reasonable and connected to the actual needs of your proposed venture.

Avoid unrealistic figures or estimates that cannot be explained.

6. Demonstrate Innovation

Innovation does not necessarily mean inventing an entirely new product.

Innovation can involve improving an existing process, introducing new technology, developing a better business model or adapting a successful solution to a new market.

7. Review Your Application Before Submission

Before submitting, carefully check:

Spelling and grammar

Certificate information

Business model details

Revenue projections

Climate-smart components

Capital estimates

Completeness of responses

A well-organised and clearly written submission can make it easier for evaluators to understand your idea.

APPLY HERE

Deadline

The deadline for submitting proposals under Submission Window 3 is: 30 October 2026

Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin the required courses and develop their AgriCanvas early.

Since completion of the mandatory training is required before submitting an idea, waiting until the final days of the submission window may create unnecessary pressure.

Starting early gives applicants sufficient time to:

Complete both mandatory courses.

Understand the learning materials.

Develop a strong business idea.

Build a detailed AgriCanvas.

Refine the revenue model.

Identify climate-smart components.

Estimate capital requirements.

Review the final application.

Submit before the deadline.

How to Apply

Interested and eligible applicants should begin by accessing the e-MOVE learning pathway, completing the mandatory courses and preparing their AgriCanvas.

Applicants can access the programme resources through the official platforms.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Call for Proposals 2026.

Conclusion

The e-MOVE Call for Proposals 2026: Build Your AgriCanvas. Build Your Future provides an important opportunity for young and emerging entrepreneurs to transform innovative cashew sector ideas into structured, investment-ready and climate-smart business ventures.

Beyond the possibility of receiving EUR 2,000 in direct funding or valuable business equipment, participants benefit from free agricultural and entrepreneurship training that can help them develop practical skills for building sustainable enterprises.

The programme is particularly valuable because it encourages applicants to think beyond an initial idea. Participants must consider how their businesses will generate revenue, respond to climate challenges, attract investment and contribute to resilient agricultural value chains.

For aspiring agripreneurs across eligible OACPS member states, this Call for Proposals presents an opportunity to combine learning, innovation and entrepreneurship while contributing to the future of the cashew industry.

Eligible applicants should begin the mandatory e-MOVE courses as early as possible, carefully develop their AgriCanvas and ensure their final submission is completed before the 30 October 2026 deadline.
